        if(!Number.isFinite(x)||!Number.isFinite(z))return false;
        const units=ids.map(id=>this.get(id)).filter(e=>e?.owner===owner&&e.kind==='unit'&&!e.embarked&&!['worker','fisher'].includes(UNITS[e.type].role));
        for(const e of units){const target=formationSlot(this,e,{x,z});this.command([e.id],{type:'patrol',...target,originX:e.x,originZ:e.z},append);}
        return units.length>0;
      };
      p.guard=function(ids,targetId,append=false,owner=0){
        const target=this.get(targetId);if(!target||!this.allied(target.owner,owner)||!['unit','building'].includes(target.kind))return false;
        const units=ids.map(id=>this.get(id)).filter(e=>e?.owner===owner&&e.kind==='unit'&&e!==target&&!e.embarked&&!['worker','fisher'].includes(UNITS[e.type].role));
        units.forEach((e,i)=>this.command([e.id],{type:'guard',target:target.id,offsetX:Math.cos(i*2.4)*(target.r+3),offsetZ:Math.sin(i*2.4)*(target.r+3)},append));
        return units.length>0;
      };
      p.setStance=function(ids,stance,owner=0){
        if(!['hold','aggressive'].includes(stance))return false;

        for(const e of units){e.stance=stance;if(stance==='hold'){e.order=null;e.orders=[];e.path=[];e.pathStatus='idle';e.stuckTime=0;}}
        return units.length>0;
      };

      p.initialize=function(){if(this.options.mode==='custom')initializeBattle(this);else initialize.call(this);};
      p.tickAI=function(){if(this.options.mode!=='custom')return tickAI.call(this);for(let owner=1;owner<this.players.length;owner++)if(!this.players[owner].defeated)tickAI.call(this,owner);};
      p.tickCustomAI=function(dt){for(let owner=0;owner<this.players.length;owner++){
        const player=this.players[owner];if(player.defeated||player.controller==='human')continue;player.aiClock+=dt;const interval=3*DIFFICULTIES[player.difficulty].ai;if(player.aiClock<interval)continue;player.aiClock-=interval;
        const tc=this.owned(owner,'building','towncenter')[0];
        if(!tc){const worker=this.owned(owner,'unit','villager').find(e=>e.order?.type!=='build');if(worker&&!this.owned(owner,'building','towncenter').length)for(let i=0;i<16;i++){const angle=i*2.4,r=12+Math.floor(i/4)*6,x=player.start.x+Math.cos(angle)*r,z=player.start.z+Math.sin(angle)*r;if(this.buildValid('towncenter',x,z,owner)){this.build('towncenter',x,z,[worker.id],owner);break;}}this.assignEconomy(owner);continue;}
        tickAI.call(this,owner);
      }};
      p.eliminateKingdom=function(owner,reason){
        const player=this.players[owner];if(!player||player.defeated)return;player.defeated=true;
        for(const e of this.owned(owner).filter(e=>e.kind==='unit'||e.kind==='building')){e.hp=0;if(e.queue)e.queue=[];player.battleStats.lost++;this.emit('death',{entity:e});}
        this.revision++;this.emit('kingdom-defeated',{owner,name:player.name,reason});this.updateFog();
      };
      p.resign=function(owner=0){if(this.options.mode!=='custom'||this.ended)return false;this.eliminateKingdom(owner,'Resigned');this.checkVictory();return true;};
      p.checkVictory=function(){
        if(this.options.mode!=='custom')return checkVictory.call(this);
        for(let owner=0;owner<this.players.length;owner++){
          const player=this.players[owner];if(player.defeated)continue;
          const buildings=this.owned(owner,'building'),units=this.owned(owner,'unit');
          if(this.options.victory==='capital'?!buildings.some(e=>e.type==='towncenter'):this.options.victory==='conquest'?!buildings.length&&!units.length:!buildings.length)this.eliminateKingdom(owner,'Victory condition reached');
          if(this.options.revealRemnants&&!player.defeated&&!buildings.some(e=>e.type==='towncenter')&&buildings.length<=5&&!this.revealedOwners.includes(owner)){
            this.revealedOwners.push(owner);this.emit('remnants-revealed',{owner,name:player.name});this.updateFog();
          }
        }
        const team=this.players[0].team,allies=this.players.filter(player=>player.team===team&&!player.defeated),enemies=this.players.filter(player=>player.team!==team&&!player.defeated);
        if(this.options.multiplayer){const teams=[...new Set(this.players.filter(player=>!player.defeated).map(player=>player.team))];if(teams.length<=1){this.end(teams[0]===team,teams.length?'The last surviving alliance controls the battlefield.':'Every kingdom has been eliminated.');this.ended.winningTeam=teams[0]??null;}return;}
        if(!allies.length)this.end(false,'Every kingdom in your alliance has been eliminated.');else if(!enemies.length)this.end(true,'Your alliance has eliminated every opposing kingdom.');
      };

    export function visibilityFor(sim,owner,explored,observer=false){
      const size=sim.gridSize,visible=new Uint8Array(size*size);
      if(observer){visible.fill(1);explored.fill(1);return visible;}
      const reveal=(e,r)=>{const c=sim.cell(e.x,e.z),rc=Math.ceil(r/2);for(let z=Math.max(0,c.z-rc);z<=Math.min(size-1,c.z+rc);z++)for(let x=Math.max(0,c.x-rc);x<=Math.min(size-1,c.x+rc);x++)if(Math.hypot(x-c.x,z-c.z)<=rc){visible[z*size+x]=1;explored[z*size+x]=1;}};
      for(const e of sim.entities)if(e.hp>0&&!e.embarked&&(e.owner===owner||sim.options.mode==='custom'&&sim.options.shareVision&&sim.allied(owner,e.owner))){if(e.kind==='unit')reveal(e,UNITS[e.type].vision);else if(e.kind==='building'&&e.progress>0)reveal(e,BUILDINGS[e.type].vision||18);else if(e.kind==='shrine')reveal(e,18);}
      for(const side of sim.revealedOwners||[])for(const e of sim.owned(side,'building'))reveal(e,e.r+4);
      return visible;
    }

      next(type){const i=this.items.findIndex(message=>message.type===type);if(i>=0)return Promise.resolve(this.items.splice(i,1)[0]);return new Promise((resolve,reject)=>{const waiter={type,resolve,timer:setTimeout(()=>reject(new Error('Missing '+type)),8000)};this.waiters.push(waiter);});}
    }

    import fs from 'node:fs';
    import http from 'node:http';
    import path from 'node:path';
    import {attachRooms} from '../server/rooms.js';
    
    // An isolated server keeps this destructive victory/reconnect check away from
    // rooms people may currently be playing on the normal Wi-Fi game server.
    const root=path.resolve('dist'),types={'.html':'text/html','.js':'text/javascript','.css':'text/css','.svg':'image/svg+xml','.png':'image/png','.webmanifest':'application/manifest+json'};
    const server=http.createServer((request,response)=>{
      const file=path.resolve(root,'.'+(new URL(request.url,'http://localhost').pathname==='/'?'/index.html':new URL(request.url,'http://localhost').pathname));
      if(!file.startsWith(root+path.sep)||!fs.existsSync(file)){response.writeHead(404);response.end();return;}
      response.writeHead(200,{'Content-Type':types[path.extname(file)]||'application/octet-stream','Cache-Control':'no-cache'});fs.createReadStream(file).pipe(response);
    });
    const service=attachRooms(server);await new Promise(resolve=>server.listen(0,'127.0.0.1',resolve));const base=`http://127.0.0.1:${server.address().port}/`;
    const browser=await chromium.launch({channel:'msedge',headless:true,args:['--enable-webgl','--ignore-gpu-blocklist']}),errors=[],reports=[];fs.mkdirSync('artifacts',{recursive:true});
    async function open(options){const page=await browser.newPage(options);page.setDefaultTimeout(60000);page.on('pageerror',error=>errors.push(error.message));await page.addInitScript(()=>localStorage.setItem('crowns-settings',JSON.stringify({quality:'low',volume:0,music:false,weather:'clear',autoQuality:false})));await page.goto(base,{waitUntil:'domcontentloaded'});await page.waitForFunction(()=>window.frontier?.view);return page;}
    async function join(page,code,name,slot=0){await page.evaluate(()=>frontier.action('lan'));await page.locator('#lan-name').fill(name);await page.locator('#lan-code').fill(code);await page.locator('#lan-slot').selectOption(String(slot));await page.locator('[data-action=lan-join]').click();await page.waitForSelector('#room-code');}
    try{
      const host=await open({viewport:{width:1440,height:900}});await host.locator('[data-action=custom-battle]').first().click();await host.locator('[data-battle-preset="2v2"]').click();await host.locator('#custom-age').selectOption('1');await host.locator('#custom-type-1').selectOption('human');await host.locator('#custom-type-2').selectOption('human');await host.locator('#custom-difficulty-3').selectOption('hard');await host.locator('[data-action=custom-host]').click();await host.waitForSelector('#room-code');const code=await host.locator('#room-code').textContent();assert.ok(await host.locator('[data-action=lan-start]').isDisabled());
      const enemy=await open({viewport:{width:1280,height:800}});await join(enemy,code,'Rival commander');assert.equal(await enemy.locator('#lobby-slot').inputValue(),'2');await enemy.locator('#lobby-slot').selectOption('3');await enemy.waitForFunction(()=>document.querySelector('#lobby-slot')?.value==='3');
      const ally=await open({viewport:{width:844,height:390},isMobile:true,hasTouch:true});await join(ally,code,'Phone ally',2);assert.ok(await ally.evaluate(()=>document.documentElement.scrollWidth<=innerWidth));
      await host.locator('[data-action=lan-ready]').click();await enemy.locator('[data-action=lan-ready]').click();assert.ok(await host.locator('[data-action=lan-start]').isDisabled());await ally.locator('[data-action=lan-ready]').tap();await host.waitForFunction(()=>!document.querySelector('[data-action=lan-start]').disabled);await host.screenshot({path:'artifacts/custom-multiplayer-lobby.png'});await host.locator('[data-action=lan-start]').click();
      for(const page of [host,enemy,ally])await page.waitForFunction(()=>frontier.playing&&frontier.sim.options.multiplayer);
      const room=service.rooms.get(code);assert.equal(room.sim.players.length,4);assert.equal(room.sim.players[3].difficulty,'hard');
      for(const [page,name,team]of [[host,room.sim.players[0].name,1],[enemy,'Rival commander',2],[ally,'Phone ally',1]]){
        const view=await page.evaluate(()=>({name:frontier.sim.players[0].name,team:frontier.sim.players[0].team,size:frontier.sim.worldSize,private:frontier.sim.players.slice(1).every(player=>Object.values(player.resources).every(value=>value===0)),controller:frontier.sim.players[0].controller,home:frontier.view.target.toArray(),start:frontier.sim.players[0].start}));assert.equal(view.name,name);assert.equal(view.team,team);assert.equal(view.size,400);assert.equal(view.controller,'human');assert.ok(view.private);assert.ok(Math.hypot(view.home[0]-view.start.x,view.home[2]-view.start.z)<1);reports.push(view);
      }
      const homeBarracks=room.sim.owned(0,'building','barracks')[0];await enemy.evaluate(id=>frontier.sim.train(id,'spearman'),homeBarracks.id);await enemy.waitForTimeout(350);assert.equal(homeBarracks.queue.length,0);
      await ally.evaluate(()=>frontier.select([frontier.sim.owned(0,'building','towncenter')[0].id]));await ally.locator('[data-train=villager]').tap();await ally.waitForFunction(()=>frontier.sim.owned(0,'building','towncenter')[0].queue.some(item=>item.type==='villager'));
      const before=room.sim.owned(1,'building','towncenter')[0].queue.length;await ally.reload({waitUntil:'domcontentloaded'});await ally.waitForFunction(()=>window.frontier?.view);await host.waitForFunction(()=>document.querySelector('#alert-line')?.textContent.includes('WAITING'));
      await ally.evaluate(()=>frontier.action('lan'));await ally.locator('[data-action=lan-resume]').tap();await ally.waitForFunction(()=>frontier.playing&&frontier.sim.players[0].name==='Phone ally');assert.ok(room.sim.owned(1,'building','towncenter')[0].queue.length>=before);await host.waitForFunction(()=>!document.querySelector('#alert-line').textContent.includes('WAITING'));
      const radar=await ally.locator('#minimap').boundingBox();assert.equal(radar.width,radar.height);await ally.screenshot({path:'artifacts/custom-multiplayer-phone.png'});
      await host.evaluate(()=>frontier.action('resign'));await host.waitForFunction(()=>frontier.sim.players[0].defeated);assert.equal(room.sim.ended,null);assert.ok(await host.locator('.battle-spectating').isVisible());
      await enemy.evaluate(()=>frontier.action('resign'));await enemy.waitForFunction(()=>frontier.sim.players[0].defeated);assert.equal(room.sim.ended,null);room.sim.resign(3);
      await host.waitForFunction(()=>frontier.sim.ended?.won===true);await ally.waitForFunction(()=>frontier.sim.ended?.won===true);await enemy.waitForFunction(()=>frontier.sim.ended?.won===false);assert.ok(await ally.locator('.battle-result-table').isVisible());
      reports.push({threeHumanBrowsers:true,oneIndependentAI:true,guestSlotSelection:true,readyGate:true,ownership:true,phoneProduction:true,phoneReconnect:true,hostDefeatContinues:true,correctTeamResults:true});assert.deepEqual(errors,[]);fs.writeFileSync('artifacts/custom-multiplayer-qa.json',JSON.stringify({reports,errors},null,2));console.log(JSON.stringify({reports,errors},null,2));
    }finally{await browser.close();service.close();await new Promise(resolve=>server.close(resolve));}

## Activity

    $ Get-Content -Raw README.md | Select-Object -First 1; Get-Content -Raw ROADMAP.md; Get-Content -Raw CHANGELOG.md | Select-Object -First 1; rg -n '\b(80|160|79|72)\b' src/world.js src/realm-3d.js src/landscape.js src/map-geometry.js src/minimap.js src/main.js src/navigation.js src/tactics.js
    # Crowns of the Frontier
    
    An original 3D browser RTS built with Three.js. Version 2.3, **Frontier chronicles**, adds staged campaign objectives, dialogue journals, optional medals, a supply-caravan escort, goal markers, and recoverable checkpoints alongside configurable controls, patrol and guard commands, deliberate AI planning, civilization-exclusive troops and technologies, and an interactive technology tree. Elevated terrain, solid models, articulated troops, animated water, model inspection, naval warfare, and two-player Wi-Fi matches remain part of the game.
    
    ## Play
    
    ```powershell
    npm install
    npm run build
    npm start
    ```
    
    Open **http://localhost:4173** on the laptop. On a phone connected to the same Wi-Fi, open **http://YOUR_LAPTOP_WIFI_IP:4173**. Landscape is recommended. The laptop must keep the game server running. If the phone cannot reach it, check that the local network permits connections to port 4173.
    
    For development, `npm run dev` serves on port 5173. Use `npm start` for Wi-Fi multiplayer; the static Vite preview server does not host rooms.
    
    ### Play with a friend
    
    Both players open the same laptop's game URL. Choose **Play with a friend over Wi-Fi**, enter a commander name, then create or join a room. Share the six-character room code with the second player. The host starts once both players join. Conquest, regicide, shrine control, wonder race, and naval conquest are supported.
    
    The server runs the simulation and checks command ownership. Each player sees their own economy and fog of war. Both receive mirrored starting towns and armies. If a connection drops, the match pauses for a reconnect grace period of two minutes. Refreshing the page preserves a room credential in session storage; choose **Rejoin your previous network session**. The menu does not pause an otherwise connected network match. Leaving a started match concedes it. Restarting the laptop server ends its in-memory rooms.
    
    Start with **First light**, the guided tutorial. Use **Clash of crowns** for a standard match. **Legendary** difficulty offers early attacks and relentless pressure. The game runs locally; it does not require an account.
    
    ## Included gameplay
    
    - **Eight modes:** tutorial, conquest skirmish, regicide, ten-wave survival, shrine control, monument race, peaceful sandbox, and naval conquest.
    - **Six campaign chapters:** settlement, river crossing, fortress defense, sacred valley, final siege, and a coastal invasion. All chapters can be played immediately. Each has three staged objectives, an original dialogue journal, an optional completion goal, and checkpoints. The river chapter requires a protected caravan escort; shrine control supports an alternative conquest route, and the coastal chapter supports landings or naval artillery.
    - **Seven seeded maps:** Emerald highlands, river crossing, sunlit steppe, Winterwood, iron frontier, twin rivers, and the divided coast. Seeds reproduce resource layouts. Bridges create movement chokepoints; winter has additional timber, the iron frontier has contested central ore, and the coast requires fleets or transports.
    - **Three original civilizations:** Alder Kingdom (durability), Sunward Sultanate (economy and construction), Raven Clans (cavalry).
    - **Four difficulties:** Explorer, Commander, Conqueror, Legendary. Difficulty changes enemy decision and attack timing; survival also changes wave strength.
    - **19 buildings:** town center, house, farm, mill, lumber camp, mining camp, barracks, archery range, stable, siege workshop, blacksmith, market, watchtower, castle, stone wall, gatehouse, monastery, grand monument, and harbor.
    - **16 trainable unit types across the catalog:** villager, scout, spearman, archer, man-at-arms, knight, battering ram, trebuchet, healer, fishing boat, galley, siege galleon, and transport, plus civilization-exclusive Alder sentinels, Sunward marksmen, and Raven outriders. Each civilization has access to its own exclusive troop. Regicide adds an irreplaceable sovereign for each side.
    - **Four ages** with population limits, paid training queues, rally points, age requirements, automatic age strength improvements, and queue cancellation refunds.
    - **Ten technology families across the catalog:** gathering tools, melee attack, armor, ranged attack, fortification, cavalry speed, and seamanship, plus civilization-exclusive Shield drill, Caravan ledger, and Raiding parties. Research levels have age requirements and increasing costs.
    - Harbors must be built near a shore. Fishing boats collect fish and return their catch to a harbor. Command land troops onto a friendly transport to embark up to eight passengers; select the transport, choose **Unload**, and select nearby open land. Sinking a transport defeats its passengers. Siege galleons can bombard shoreline defenses.
    - Villagers physically walk between resources and drop-off buildings, carry supplies, construct buildings, and repair damage. Farms provide renewable food. Mines and trees deplete. Markets buy and sell resources for gold.
    - Walls block paths; friendly units can pass through gates. Connected walls support queued construction. Construction can be canceled for a 70% resource refund; finished buildings can be demolished for a 20% refund. Your last town center is protected from accidental demolition.
    - Unit counters, splash siege damage, automatic healing, defensive towers, formations, aggressive/hold stances, queued orders, box selection, type selection, numbered control groups, and visible selected-unit attributes.
    - Enemy AI responds to visible threats, repairs damaged buildings, reinforces counters against observed unit types, escorts attacks with healers, and runs a fishing and transport economy on the coastal map.
    - Articulated walking, weapon motion, working villagers, rocking ships, ship wakes, drifting water textures, textured masonry and wood, gabled roofs, and biome-specific foliage. Hidden forests obey exploration. Battle audio includes impact layers, arrows, siege sounds, stereo placement, wind, birds, and ambient music, with bounded effects and audio voices.
    - Closer perspective cameras, selectable close/perspective/overview angles, mouse and touch rotation, surface relief, directional lighting, sharper camera-centered shadows, timber framing, window recesses, and shared instanced contact shadows that remain available in Performance quality.
    - All 19 building types and all 18 character/ship types (16 trainable across the catalog, the sovereign, and a campaign supply caravan) have solid mesh models. Buildings use arches, domes, gables, piers, fences, turrets, grain stalks, and distinct workshops. Human models have faces, shaped torsos, jointed limbs, held tools and weapons; cavalry adds modeled horses, and siege equipment has moving wheels and mechanisms. Trees, ore deposits, fruit, fish, and shrines also use mesh geometry.
    - All seven maps have seeded rolling terrain and surrounding ridges. Picking, walking, building foundations, effects, previews, and fog follow the surface. Bridges stay dry and naval channels have submerged beds. Water has moving vertices and updated normals. Nearby gate portcullises lift for friendly troops.
    - Selection portraits render the actual model as a live WebGL turntable. Tap/click the portrait, or press **I**, to inspect the selected object. The square camera button hides or restores battlefield panels for an unobstructed view.
    - Fog of war, exploration, a working minimap, mission objectives, victory/defeat screens, match statistics, synthesized audio, pause, game speed, local saves, and campaign completion tracking.
    - Landscape-first touch interface, pinch zoom, drag pan, responsive menus, graphics presets, and automatic rendering resolution adjustment.
    
    ## Controls
    
    These are the default keyboard bindings. Settings lets you remap controls with conflict checks; Escape, Tab, and numbered control groups stay reserved. Custom bindings, higher-contrast UI, reduced decorative motion, and order-route preferences are saved on this device.
    
    | Action | Laptop | Phone/tablet |
    |---|---|---|
    | Select | Left click; Shift adds; drag a selection box | Tap a unit or building |
    | Command | Right click; Shift queues | Select units, then tap ground, enemies, or resources |
    | Pan | Mouse at the game-window edges/corners, WASD/arrows, or middle-button drag | Drag the battlefield |
    | Zoom | Mouse wheel | Two-finger pinch |
    | Rotate | Q/E or camera arrow buttons | Two-finger twist or camera arrow buttons |
    | Camera angle | V or the camera view button | Camera view button |
    | Inspect selected model | I or selection portrait | Tap selection portrait |
    | Hide/show panels | Square camera button | Square camera button |
    | Center town | H or minimap home | Minimap home button |
    | Radar navigation | Click or drag the square minimap | Tap or drag the square minimap |
    | Production overview | P or top-bar P button | Top-bar P button |
    | Queue five troops | Shift-click a troop; +5 in building groups | +5 in building groups |
    | Select army | M | Army button |
    | Idle villagers | Period | Idle button |
    | Construct | B | Build button |
    | Attack move | F, then click | Attack button, then tap |
    | Stop / hold | X | Stop button |
    | Patrol | R, then click a destination | Select military units, tap Patrol, then a destination |
    | Guard | G, then click a friendly unit/building | Select military units, tap Guard, then an ally |
    | Groups | Ctrl + 1â€“9 assigns; 1â€“9 recalls | Army/type selection buttons |
    | Focus selection | Space | Tap minimap to navigate |
    | Pause | Esc | Pause button |
    
    Choose **Stone wall** and drag across visible, open land to place a connected line. Use **Shift** to keep other construction tools active. Select a completed military building to train troops, a blacksmith to research combat technologies, or the town center to advance ages. Use the in-game **Field guide** for costs and counters.
    
    Mouse edge scrolling is enabled by default. Bring the cursor into the outer 24 pixels of the game window to pan; corners pan diagonally and a directional arrow appears. Scrolling follows the rotated camera, stops outside the game or during menus/pauses, and avoids controls. **Settings** includes an on/off toggle and speed slider. Touch gestures continue to pan and zoom. Fullscreen lets you use the monitor edges.
    
    The square minimap acts as your battlefield radar. Its outlined rectangle encloses the ground within the camera view, and its center dot marks where the camera is aimed. The locator remains rectangular at map edges and follows rotation and zoom. Right-click the minimap to give selected units orders; commands outside the playable battlefield are ignored.
    
    Open **Production** with **P** or the top-bar button to see your completed production/research buildings, active queues, progress, and idle sites. Tap a building to select and locate it, or choose its type to select several. Troop orders across selected buildings go to the shortest available queue. Use **+5** or Shift-click to request a batch, limited by resources, population, ages, and queue capacity. Tap queued items to cancel and refund them. Research and age advancement also appear in the overview.
    
    Selected units show their current orders and queued waypoint counts. Movement commands display without route lines on desktop and phones. Unreachable orders report a blocked route and yield to the next queued order. Melee units do not automatically pursue ships beyond their reach.
    
    Open the Field guide and choose **Explore the technology tree** to compare civilizations, inspect age and building requirements, and train/research directly when eligible. The opponent uses paid queues and buildings, scouting memory, composition targets, age-resource reserves, repairs, retreats, and transport boarding reservations. These are implemented behaviors, not a claim of balanced difficulty.
    
    Campaign objectives include **Journal**, **Locate goal**, and (for the escort) **Select caravan** controls. A gold diamond marks the active destination on the minimap; an explored destination also has a 3D banner. Restore the starting or latest completed-objective checkpoint from the commander menu or defeat screen. Checkpoints capture a separate, frozen simulation snapshot and are included in local saves. Existing campaign saves retain their previous victory rules instead of acquiring a new escort requirement. Optional completions earn a chapter star.
    
    ## Build, offline play, and tests
    
    ```powershell
    npm run build
    npm run preview
    npm test
    node scripts/browser-qa.mjs
    node scripts/interaction-qa.mjs
    node scripts/visual-qa.mjs
    node scripts/realm-qa.mjs
    node scripts/edge-scroll-qa.mjs
    node scripts/map-qa.mjs
    node scripts/production-qa.mjs
    node scripts/offline-qa.mjs
    node scripts/release-qa.mjs
    node scripts/commander-qa.mjs
    node scripts/ai-soak.mjs
    node scripts/campaign-qa.mjs
    ```
    
    The production output is in `dist/`. Deploy it to a static web host. The generated service worker caches the game and its bundled assets for offline use after the first successful visit over HTTPS (or localhost). The web app manifest requests fullscreen landscape when installed. Browser support for fullscreen, installation, and orientation locking varies. Fonts and their licenses are bundled locally. No game assets depend on a third-party CDN.
    
    The browser QA scripts use a locally installed Microsoft Edge. `release-qa.mjs` tests a real room with desktop and emulated phone clients, both command perspectives, phone troop training, and reconnecting after a reload. It defaults to a test server on port 4180; set `QA_URL` to another server URL as needed. `npm test` also runs a real WebSocket test for fair starts, ownership rejection, fog masking, disconnect pauses, and session restoration. Emulation does not substitute for testing on physical phones.
    
    ## Implementation
    
    - `src/campaigns.js` and `src/campaign-view.js`: staged mission rules, story journals, escort actor, optional objectives, checkpoint snapshots, and 3D goal markers.
    
    - `src/controls.js` and `src/keyboard-settings.js`: saved keyboard bindings, conflict checks, active-key documentation, and the settings editor.
    - `src/tactics.js`: patrol/guard commands, legal formation destinations, and stances.
    - `src/commander-ai.js`: paid economy and army plans, scouting memory, counter composition, retreats, repairs, and naval staging.
    - `src/technology-tree.js`: civilization comparison, prerequisites, and direct training/research.
    
    - `src/data.js`: troops, buildings, research, civilizations, difficulties, maps, and missions.
    - `src/simulation.js`: deterministic map generation and independent fixed-step gameplay simulation. The opponent gathers, pays for buildings and units, advances ages, researches technologies, and attacks. Survival is explicitly a wave-spawn scenario.
    - `src/world.js`: procedural 3D models, camera, ray picking, shadows, fog, and combat effects. Forests and units use instanced rendering; buildings/resources merge geometry by material. Graphics adapt to sustained slow frames.
    - `src/landscape.js`: seeded elevated terrain, triangulated surface sampling and ray picking, river/coastal beds, bridges, terrain textures, solid grass tufts, and animated water meshes.
    - `src/models-3d.js`: solid world models for the complete building/unit/resource catalog and civilization architecture.
    - `src/realm-3d.js`: terrain/model integration, packed forest detail levels, foundations, construction clipping and scaffolds, previews, gate motion, and solid projectiles.
    - `src/portrait-3d.js`: throttled live 3D selection turntables.
    - `src/main.js`: menus, responsive HUD, touch/mouse/keyboard controls, objectives, saves, and modal flows.
    - `src/map-geometry.js` and `src/minimap.js`: square radar coordinates, bounded rectangular camera locator, waterways, icons, and camera location.
    - `src/production.js`: completed production sites and training batches balanced across eligible building queues, including virtual planning for multiplayer snapshots.
    - `src/audio.js`: synthesized cues and ambient music.
    - `src/frontiers.js`: naval mechanics and tactical AI additions.
    - `src/navigation.js`: heap-based pathfinding.
    - `src/world-polish.js`: articulated model animation, ship models, material textures, and exploration-aware foliage.
    - `src/soundscape.js`: battle sounds and atmospheric audio.
    - `src/network.js`: room connection, commands, and session reconnection.
    - `server/rooms.js`: authoritative Wi-Fi matches, player perspectives, command validation, disconnect handling, and room lifecycle.
    - `server/index.js`: local game hosting and WebSocket server.
    - `vite.config.js`: build splitting and offline cache generation.
    
    ## Research and scope
    
    The design draws on the genre's established exploration â†’ resource collection â†’ construction â†’ army â†’ age progression loop and varied victory conditions described in the [official Age of Empires IV quickstart](https://www.ageofempires.com/news/quickstart-guide-age-of-empires-iv/) and [official strategy introduction](https://www.ageofempires.com/news/age-of-empires-iv-tips-to-help-you-get-started/). Picking and repeated-model rendering follow the [Three.js Raycaster](https://threejs.org/docs/pages/Raycaster.html) and [InstancedMesh](https://threejs.org/docs/pages/InstancedMesh.html) documentation.
    
    Instanced animation follows the [Three.js update documentation](https://threejs.org/manual/pages/how-to-update-things.html). Room transport and heartbeat handling follow the [official ws documentation](https://github.com/websockets/ws). The naval design considers fishing economies, transport landings, and shoreline defense described in the [official Age of Empires naval update](https://www.ageofempires.com/news/age-of-empires-iv-update-11-0-782/).
    
    The graphics use shaped [CapsuleGeometry](https://threejs.org/docs/pages/CapsuleGeometry.html), solid architectural [ExtrudeGeometry](https://threejs.org/docs/pages/ExtrudeGeometry.html), and indexed terrain [BufferGeometry](https://threejs.org/docs/pages/BufferGeometry.html). Distant forests use simpler solid geometry and pack only visible instances; world objects do not switch to billboard images.
    
    This is an original playable RTS implementation with procedural art, fictional civilizations, and its own balance. It contains no Age of Empires assets or licensed branding. Two-player Wi-Fi gameplay is implemented; public internet matchmaking, accounts, historical documentary campaigns, professional voice acting, and a production-scale backend service are not. Commercial AAA parity is not claimed. Balance and performance need broader human playtesting and real-device testing; smooth performance on every device cannot be guaranteed.
    
    # Crowns of the Frontier: quality roadmap
    
    Reviewed 9 October 2026 against the version 2.3 source and current verification scripts.
    
    This is an ordered development proposal, not a claim that its milestones have been implemented. The current game is a playable beta. A world-class assessment needs independent player feedback, reliable performance, strong content, and sustained quality across complete matches.
    
    ## Current baseline
    
    - Three.js world with elevated terrain, solid building/unit/resource models, articulated parts, animated water, and 3D selection portraits.
    - Resource gathering, construction, queues, upgrades, ages, unit counters, siege, healing, walls, gates, fleets, transports, fog, saves, and several victory conditions.
    - Eight modes, seven seeded maps, six campaign chapters, three civilizations, 19 building types, and 16 trainable types across the catalog plus sovereigns.
    - Two-player Wi-Fi rooms with authoritative commands, player perspectives, and reconnection. Rooms are held in server memory; they are not a public matchmaking service.
    - Mouse edge scrolling, corner scrolling, cursor arrows, keyboard controls, camera inspection, and landscape touch input.
    - Square radar with a rectangular camera locator and mouse/touch dragging. Global production overview, selection across completed production buildings, balanced training batches, and cancel/refund controls.
    - Existing automated simulation/graphics/network checks and browser verification. Physical-device performance, balance, and extensive human playtesting remain unverified.
    
    ## Version 2.3 campaign progress
    
    - Six chapters now have three authored stages each, original dialogue journals, optional completion medals, and active goal markers in the minimap and explored 3D world.
    - The river chapter has a modeled supply caravan, guarded escort navigation, a bridgehead objective, a loss condition, and recovery through frozen checkpoints.
    - Fortress defense requires a completed castle and the wave objectives. Sacred valley supports shrine control or a recorded conquest alternative. Final siege requires paid siege production and a defensive breach. The coastal chapter counts actual deposited fishing catch and accepts a landing or an Imperial siege-galleon route.
    - Initial and stage checkpoints preserve actors, objectives, economy, armies, exploration, and AI state without recursive snapshots. Existing campaign saves retain legacy rules.
    - Automated scenarios use gathering, construction, training, escort movement, shrine control, fishing, and gate attacks to exercise the chapter flows. All four difficulties initialize every chapter. Browser verification covers journals, selecting and inspecting the caravan, locating goals, defeat recovery, local save/resume, and emulated-phone controls.
    
    Pass 4 has a playable scripted baseline. Human completion tests on all difficulties, more mission events and set pieces, professional narration/audio, broader map fairness checks, and mission pacing remain unfinished.
    
    ## Version 2.2 implementation progress
    
    - Saved remappable keyboard controls, reserved-key validation, conflict reporting, active key documentation, and updated shortcut labels.
    - Patrol and guard commands in the simulation, desktop/touch interface, saves, and authoritative network commands. Formation slots avoid blocked terrain. Partial paths no longer count as successful arrival; persistent blocked orders report feedback and yield to queued orders.
    - Selected-unit order summaries and bounded 3D route previews, including patrol return routes and ship routes above the water.
    - Paid AI economy and army planning, civilization-aware counter composition, scouting memory, age-resource reserves, worker reassignment, repairs, retreats, healer escorts, and transport boarding/departure reservations.
    - Three civilization-exclusive units with solid model variants, explicit costs, age/building requirements, and distinct roles. Three exclusive technologies affect armor, market exchange, and cavalry raids. Old saves initialize the new research fields.
    - Interactive technology tree with faction comparison, prerequisite/status explanations, training, and research. Higher-contrast UI, reduced decorative motion, and larger tactical touch buttons.
    - Regression coverage now includes these behaviors. Commander browser checks exercise remapping, persistence, tactics, route rendering, save/resume, and desktop/emulated-phone layouts. Passive-player soak checks exercise full land, river, and coastal matches and record simulation CPU timings.
    
    Passes 1 through 3 have concrete implementation progress; they are not fully complete. Group cohesion, advanced recovery, AI expansion, further economy/combat tuning, richer strategic interactions, authored missions, asset/audio production, measured device performance, public online services, and external playtesting remain on the roadmap. Naval regrouping now respects the current island, and movement reaches the actual final waypoint rather than stopping at a grid center. The latest coastal soak reports four blocked orders instead of 74 in the previous diagnostic run; remaining land/bridge cases still need review. CPU timings from automated simulations do not establish rendering FPS, phone performance, or enjoyable difficulty.
    
    ## Development order and release checks
    
    | Pass | Work to implement or improve | Evidence required before declaring the pass complete |
    |---|---|---|
    | 1. Controls and army movement | Remappable hotkeys, selection priority, production across selected buildings, global production queue, queued-command feedback, patrol/guard behaviors, formation cohesion, obstacle avoidance, and recovery from blocked routes. Preserve edge scrolling and touch input. | Repeatable mouse/keyboard/touch scenarios; armies navigate woods, walls, gates, bridges, and crowded towns; no duplicated queued orders or indefinitely stuck troops in the tested cases. Local command feedback and execution latency measured on reference hardware. |
    | 2. Economy, AI, and battle balance | Explicit AI build orders and resource budgets, scouting memory, different attack plans, counter-unit composition, regrouping, retreating, siege protection, expansion, transport decisions, and difficulty based on decisions. Audit starting advantages and any difficulty bonuses. | Seeded economy and combat scenarios; AI can recover after worker losses and exhausted nearby resources; attacks change based on observed enemies; difficulty rules are documented; human testers find each level understandable and challenging. |
    | 3. Civilizations and strategic depth | Unique units and technologies, clearer civilization identities, useful upgrade choices, meaningful land/naval counters, alternative economic strategies, and an interactive technology tree. Expand team/player support before adding team modes. | Comparable-cost counter scenarios plus human matches; all additions have costs, prerequisites, counters, descriptions, art, audio, AI support, saves, and multiplayer validation. Balance judged across maps and skill levels. |
    | 4. Missions and map design | A mission-event system with staged objectives, dialogue, reinforcements, escort/rescue tasks, branching optional goals, checkpoints, and authored set pieces. Curate resource placement, chokepoints, naval landings, and spawn fairness. | Each mission can be completed and failed correctly on each difficulty; checkpoints restore the correct event state; missions require different strategies; map objectives and travel routes remain reachable. |
    | 5. Art, animation, and sound | Establish a consistent medieval art direction; replace or refine the procedural assets with original or appropriately licensed authored models, textures, character rigs, transitions, worker tasks, cargo, attack impacts, damage, and death animations. Add distinctive music, unit responses, ambience, and readable combat sound. | Visual review in real gameplay at every quality setting and camera angle; recognizable units and silhouettes; animations match actions; assets fit performance budgets; retain real mesh geometry at every detail level. |
    | 6. Laptop and phone experience | Profile CPU/GPU work, pathfinding, draw calls, memory, network snapshots, and input delay. Improve detail levels, shared routes, batching, effects budgets, loading, safe areas, readable UI, touch selection, UI scaling, and accessibility options. | Publish device/browser/specification results. Proposed targets: 60 FPS on a defined reference laptop and 30 FPS on defined supported phones in benchmark matches. Verify sustained performance, frame-time spikes, thermal behavior, and memory over long sessions. Targets are not current achievements or guarantees for every device. |
    | 7. Multiplayer and community | Public hosting, persistent room/session state, matchmaking, reconnect recovery, cooperative/team games, profiles, replay/spectator tools, authoritative validation, and operational monitoring. Generalize the current two-player simulation and perspective assumptions first. | Test multiple clients, latency, packet loss, disconnects, server restarts, ownership, hidden-information handling, version compatibility, and replay results. Hosting choices and ongoing costs need an explicit deployment decision. |
    | 8. Release readiness | Improve onboarding, settings, saved-game migrations, campaign progression, post-match economy/combat graphs, installation/update behavior, diagnostics, recovery, and documentation. Conduct repeated external playtests and fix their highest-impact problems. | Long complete matches, all modes, save/resume/update cycles, physical phones/laptops, multiplayer failure scenarios, and accessibility reviews pass the agreed release checklist. Record remaining limitations instead of labeling unchecked areas complete. |
    
    Performance, regression testing, and human feedback run throughout these passes; they are not postponed until the end.
    
    ## Recommended next release
    
    Start with Pass 1 and the most visible parts of Pass 2:
    
    1. Global production overview and multi-building training are implemented. Configurable hotkeys and queued-order feedback are now implemented; continue with group cohesion, obstacle recovery, and full-match input testing.
    2. Continue control refinements with profile management, selection priority, and accessibility reviews.
    3. Improve group movement through gates, around buildings, and over bridges; show blocked-order feedback.
    4. Refine the implemented AI plans with expansion, resource exhaustion recovery, siege protection, and human difficulty tuning.
    5. Exercise complete economy-to-victory matches with several seeds and difficulties, followed by laptop and phone playtests.
    
    Deliver these as tested releases that can be played and reviewed. Additional units or prettier screenshots alone do not establish overall game quality.
    
    ## What can be developed here and what needs outside evidence
    
    The existing workspace supports implementation of gameplay, AI, UI, asset integration, shaders, animation, performance instrumentation, testing, and multiplayer services. Professional asset/audio production requires suitable original work or licensed sources. Physical-device results require access to the actual devices or measurements from testers. Public online operation requires a hosting decision and ongoing service resources. Fun and balance require repeated human playtesting.
    
    No honest development process can promise an objective â€œ100% world-classâ€ score. The useful commitment is to finish defined requirements, publish test evidence, address player feedback, and improve successive releases.
    
    ## Research references
    
    - [Official Age of Empires IV Season One development notes](https://www.ageofempires.com/news/age-of-empires-iv-season-one-update-release-notes/): controls, global production queues, patrol, player feedback, balance, maps, campaign tuning, and post-match navigation. Used as a genre quality reference, not a statement of this project's implemented features.
    - [Official Age of Empires IV Season Two development notes](https://www.ageofempires.com/news/age-of-empires-iv-update-17718/): continued iteration across controls, game modes, multiplayer, and stability.
    - The baseline above is supported by the local source, [README](README.md), [change log](CHANGELOG.md), and tests/scripts in this repository.
    
    # Movement display update
    
    - Removed selected-unit movement and queued-route lines on desktop and phones, including the route-display setting. Movement, patrol, guard, and queued commands remain available.
    
    # Frontier chronicles (version 2.3)
    
    - Three staged objectives per campaign chapter, original dialogue journals, optional medals, and active minimap/3D goal markers.
    - Supply-caravan mesh model and guarded river escort with an explicit loss condition. Select-caravan and locate-goal controls are available in the objective panel.
    - Frozen initial and stage checkpoints, commander-menu and defeat-screen recovery, local save/resume, and legacy rules for existing campaign saves.
    - Settlement, fortress, shrine-control/conquest, siege-breach, and coastal landing/artillery chapter flows. Fishing objectives count deposited boat catch.
    - Objective updates preserve scrolling/focus and expose interactive controls without triggering camera edge scrolling. Phone recovery controls and compact technology-tree layouts receive browser coverage.
    - Exact waypoint arrival and island-aware naval regrouping reduce the coastal diagnostic run from 74 blocked orders to four. Remaining bridge/crowding cases still need review.
    - Regression coverage includes normal economy/production, real escort navigation, shrine holding, paid naval artillery, actual gate attacks, actor loss, and checkpoint recovery.
    
    This continues the playable beta roadmap. External balance and mission-pacing tests, real-device rendering performance, richer authored assets/audio, public online operations, and overall world-class parity remain unfinished.
    
    # Commanders and kingdoms (version 2.2)
    
    - Saved remappable keys with conflict/reserved-key validation, updated shortcut labels, and active bindings in Help.
    - Patrol/guard orders, network ownership checks, queued-order summaries, and bounded 3D route previews. Routes follow terrain and stay visible above water for ships.
    - Legal formation destinations, correct partial-path arrival checks, blocked-order feedback/recovery, axis sliding near obstacles, and safer automatic naval target selection.
    - Paid strategic AI with planned economy/production, observed enemy memory, counters, age-resource reserves, repairs, retreats, healer escorts, scouting, and transport boarding reservations.
    - Alder sentinels, Sunward marksmen, and Raven outriders with solid 3D model variants, costs, prerequisites, and counters. Shield drill, Caravan ledger, and Raiding parties add civilization-specific research.
    - Interactive technology tree with faction comparison and eligible training/research. Older saves initialize added research fields.
    - Higher-contrast interface, reduced decorative motion, larger tactical touch controls, and saved route preferences.
    - Expanded simulation, graphics, control, strategy, save, and real-WebSocket regression coverage. New commander browser and passive-player AI soak scripts write reviewable artifacts.
    
    This is a tested development milestone. Public matchmaking, replay/spectator services, richer authored campaigns, production-quality assets/audio, measured physical-device targets, independent balance testing, and overall world-class parity remain unverified or unfinished. Naval blocked-order cases remain under review.
    
    # Realm in depth â€” version 2.1
    
    ## Radar and production controls
    
    - Square minimap at desktop, tablet, and phone sizes. A rectangular camera locator replaces the irregular perspective polygon; a center dot makes location readable when zoomed out. The rectangle encloses the visible ground and updates while scrolling, zooming, and rotating.
    - Mouse and touch dragging on the minimap, accurate curved waterways and bridges, visible ship/resource icons, and orders restricted to playable terrain with reachable edge coordinates.
    - Fog matches the terrain triangulation at every quality setting.
    - Production overview (P or the top-bar button) shows active/idle buildings, units, research, age advancement, progress, and cancel/refund controls. Select a production building to locate it or select a whole building type.
    - Queue refreshes preserve panel scrolling and keyboard focus, including short landscape phone layouts.
    - Train across several selected buildings, balancing requests by remaining queue time. Shift-click queues up to five; phones have +5 buttons. Resource, population, ownership, age, and queue limits remain enforced, including authoritative multiplayer requests.
    - Nine additional automated checks cover radar geometry, boundaries, batch distribution, budget limits, network request planning, and saved production queues. Browser scripts exercise laptop/phone radar and production controls.
    
    ## Mouse camera controls
    
    - Mouse edge scrolling enabled by default on all four viewport edges and diagonal corners, with directional cursor arrows and camera-relative movement.
    - Saved toggle and speed control in Settings; stops over controls, during menus and pauses, on blur/viewport exit, and for touch input or middle-button dragging.
    - Construction previews follow the cursor while edge scrolling moves the terrain beneath it.
    - Browser verification covers eight directions, rotated views, stopping conditions, settings persistence, and touch protection.
    
    - Rebuilt all 19 building models and all 14 troop/ship/sovereign models, with faction architecture, solid folded sails and banners, shaped humanoids and horses, and articulated limbs, wheels, oars, rams, and trebuchets.
    - Rebuilt trees, ore deposits, fruit, fish, and shrines as volumetric models.
    - Replaced flat ground and cone-shaped map borders with seeded terrain and ridges. Picking, actors, foundations, fog, construction previews, and effects follow the triangulated terrain surface.
    - Moving water vertices, submerged naval basins, dry bridges, lifting gate portcullises, construction scaffolds/clipping, and actual 3D building previews.
    - Live WebGL selection portraits, object inspection on mouse/touch, closer perspectives, and a button to hide battlefield panels.
    - Visible forests pack into near/far instanced batches with solid geometry at both detail levels. Camera obstruction handling, efficient crop geometry, bounded portrait refresh, and cleanup between maps.
    - Five additional graphics checks cover all model types/civilizations, terrain determinism, surface picking, bridge/sea elevations, model bounds, batching, and skeletal motion. Browser coverage exercises every biome, naval rendering, live portraits, inspection, and landscape phone controls.
    
    # Frontiers & fleets â€” version 2.0
    
    ## Visual depth update
    
    - A closer default perspective and three selectable camera angles, with visible rotate/zoom buttons, V shortcut, two-finger touch rotation, and saved camera preferences.
    - More directional light, procedural environment illumination, camera-centered shadow coverage, and shared contact shadows that remain available with dynamic shadows disabled.
    - Surface relief on masonry, timber, and roofs; separate roof and troop materials; aligned gables; raised timber framing, windows, eaves, and entry steps; smoother heads and shaped torsos.
    - Browser checks cover camera buttons, picking after rotation, persisted settings, actual two-finger touch events, and contact shadows in Performance quality.
    
    ## Gameplay
    
    - Two-player Wi-Fi rooms with five victory rules, mirrored starting forces, private player economies, per-player fog, command ownership checks, and session reconnection.
    - Naval conquest, a divided-coast map, and a sixth campaign chapter.
    - Shoreline harbors, fishing boats with actual catch deposits, galleys, siege galleons, and eight-passenger transports.
    - Embarking, disembarking, passenger loss when a transport sinks, naval navigation, ship production, and seamanship research.
    - Tactical AI responds to observed cavalry/archers, defends its base, repairs buildings, escorts attacks with healers, manages fishing, and ferries invasion forces.
    
    ## Presentation and performance
    
    - Articulated legs, arms, weapons, and working villagers through instanced model parts.
    - Rocking ships, ship wakes, animated water, harbor jetties, gabled roofs, textured materials, and rounded forest canopies.
    - Exploration controls forest visibility. Hidden units are not included in multiplayer opponent snapshots.
    - Layered impacts, arrows, siege sounds, stereo placement, birds, wind, and music. Effect counts and audio voices are bounded.
    - Heap-based pathfinding, indexed entity lookup, broader collision checks, cached animation transforms, and interpolated network movement.
    - Selected-unit combat attributes, clear transport unloading controls, room codes, and phone-compatible room menus.
    
    ## Validation
    
    - Automated simulation and real WebSocket tests cover economy, queues, ages, research, combat, walls, victory rules, save compatibility, naval mechanics, player ownership, fog masking, fair starts, and reconnect pauses.
    - Browser QA covers naval controls and a live desktop/landscape-phone match, phone troop training, and reconnection after a reload.
    - Hardware performance and game balance still need broader real-device and human playtesting. This release does not establish commercial AAA parity.

## Assistant

The machine has 4 GB of RAM, so concurrent 3D browser tests strained it. I’ve reduced rendering behind menus and in hidden tabs, and capped Low quality at 30 frames per second.

The simulation profile also found costly searches for unreachable routes. I’ve added cached movement regions and shared vision checks; the movement, transport, and alliance regressions pass.

    ROADMAP.md:1:# Crowns of the Frontier: quality roadmap
    ROADMAP.md:3:Reviewed 9 October 2026 against the version 2.3 source and current verification scripts.
    ROADMAP.md:5:This is an ordered development proposal, not a claim that its milestones have been implemented. The current game is a playable beta. A world-class assessment needs independent player feedback, reliable performance, strong content, and sustained quality across complete matches.
    ROADMAP.md:7:## Current baseline
    ROADMAP.md:12:- Two-player Wi-Fi rooms with authoritative commands, player perspectives, and reconnection. Rooms are held in server memory; they are not a public matchmaking service.
    ROADMAP.md:17:## Version 2.3 campaign progress
    ROADMAP.md:27:## Version 2.2 implementation progress
    ROADMAP.md:35:- Regression coverage now includes these behaviors. Commander browser checks exercise remapping, persistence, tactics, route rendering, save/resume, and desktop/emulated-phone layouts. Passive-player soak checks exercise full land, river, and coastal matches and record simulation CPU timings.
    ROADMAP.md:39:## Development order and release checks
    ROADMAP.md:45:| 3. Civilizations and strategic depth | Unique units and technologies, clearer civilization identities, useful upgrade choices, meaningful land/naval counters, alternative economic strategies, and an interactive technology tree. Expand team/player support before adding team modes. | Comparable-cost counter scenarios plus human matches; all additions have costs, prerequisites, counters, descriptions, art, audio, AI support, saves, and multiplayer validation. Balance judged across maps and skill levels. |
    ROADMAP.md:49:| 7. Multiplayer and community | Public hosting, persistent room/session state, matchmaking, reconnect recovery, cooperative/team games, profiles, replay/spectator tools, authoritative validation, and operational monitoring. Generalize the current two-player simulation and perspective assumptions first. | Test multiple clients, latency, packet loss, disconnects, server restarts, ownership, hidden-information handling, version compatibility, and replay results. Hosting choices and ongoing costs need an explicit deployment decision. |
    ROADMAP.md:50:| 8. Release readiness | Improve onboarding, settings, saved-game migrations, campaign progression, post-match economy/combat graphs, installation/update behavior, diagnostics, recovery, and documentation. Conduct repeated external playtests and fix their highest-impact problems. | Long complete matches, all modes, save/resume/update cycles, physical phones/laptops, multiplayer failure scenarios, and accessibility reviews pass the agreed release checklist. Record remaining limitations instead of labeling unchecked areas complete. |
    ROADMAP.md:54:## Recommended next release
    ROADMAP.md:66:## What can be developed here and what needs outside evidence
    ROADMAP.md:68:The existing workspace supports implementation of gameplay, AI, UI, asset integration, shaders, animation, performance instrumentation, testing, and multiplayer services. Professional asset/audio production requires suitable original work or licensed sources. Physical-device results require access to the actual devices or measurements from testers. Public online operation requires a hosting decision and ongoing service resources. Fun and balance require repeated human playtesting.
    ROADMAP.md:70:No honest development process can promise an objective “100% world-class” score. The useful commitment is to finish defined requirements, publish test evidence, address player feedback, and improve successive releases.
    ROADMAP.md:72:## Research references
    ROADMAP.md:74:- [Official Age of Empires IV Season One development notes](https://www.ageofempires.com/news/age-of-empires-iv-season-one-update-release-notes/): controls, global production queues, patrol, player feedback, balance, maps, campaign tuning, and post-match navigation. Used as a genre quality reference, not a statement of this project's implemented features.
    ROADMAP.md:75:- [Official Age of Empires IV Season Two development notes](https://www.ageofempires.com/news/age-of-empires-iv-update-17718/): continued iteration across controls, game modes, multiplayer, and stability.
    README.md:1:# Crowns of the Frontier
    README.md:3:An original 3D browser RTS built with Three.js. Version 2.3, **Frontier chronicles**, adds staged campaign objectives, dialogue journals, optional medals, a supply-caravan escort, goal markers, and recoverable checkpoints alongside configurable controls, patrol and guard commands, deliberate AI planning, civilization-exclusive troops and technologies, and an interactive technology tree. Elevated terrain, solid models, articulated troops, animated water, model inspection, naval warfare, and two-player Wi-Fi matches remain part of the game.
    README.md:5:## Play
    README.md:15:For development, `npm run dev` serves on port 5173. Use `npm start` for Wi-Fi multiplayer; the static Vite preview server does not host rooms.
    README.md:17:### Play with a friend
    README.md:19:Both players open the same laptop's game URL. Choose **Play with a friend over Wi-Fi**, enter a commander name, then create or join a room. Share the six-character room code with the second player. The host starts once both players join. Conquest, regicide, shrine control, wonder race, and naval conquest are supported.
    README.md:21:The server runs the simulation and checks command ownership. Each player sees their own economy and fog of war. Both receive mirrored starting towns and armies. If a connection drops, the match pauses for a reconnect grace period of two minutes. Refreshing the page preserves a room credential in session storage; choose **Rejoin your previous network session**. The menu does not pause an otherwise connected network match. Leaving a started match concedes it. Restarting the laptop server ends its in-memory rooms.
    README.md:25:## Included gameplay
    README.md:49:## Controls
    README.md:92:## Build, offline play, and tests
    README.md:116:## Implementation
    README.md:134:- `src/production.js`: completed production sites and training batches balanced across eligible building queues, including virtual planning for multiplayer snapshots.
    README.md:141:- `server/rooms.js`: authoritative Wi-Fi matches, player perspectives, command validation, disconnect handling, and room lifecycle.
    README.md:145:## Research and scope
    README.md:153:This is an original playable RTS implementation with procedural art, fictional civilizations, and its own balance. It contains no Age of Empires assets or licensed branding. Two-player Wi-Fi gameplay is implemented; public internet matchmaking, accounts, historical documentary campaigns, professional voice acting, and a production-scale backend service are not. Commercial AAA parity is not claimed. Balance and performance need broader human playtesting and real-device testing; smooth performance on every device cannot be guaranteed.

    ## Recommended next release
    
    Start with Pass 1 and the most visible parts of Pass 2:
    
    1. Global production overview and multi-building training are implemented. Configurable hotkeys and queued-order feedback are now implemented; continue with group cohesion, obstacle recovery, and full-match input testing.
    2. Continue control refinements with profile management, selection priority, and accessibility reviews.
    3. Improve group movement through gates, around buildings, and over bridges; show blocked-order feedback.
    4. Refine the implemented AI plans with expansion, resource exhaustion recovery, siege protection, and human difficulty tuning.
    5. Exercise complete economy-to-victory matches with several seeds and difficulties, followed by laptop and phone playtests.
    
    Deliver these as tested releases that can be played and reviewed. Additional units or prettier screenshots alone do not establish overall game quality.
    
    # Movement display update
    
    - Removed selected-unit movement and queued-route lines on desktop and phones, including the route-display setting. Movement, patrol, guard, and queued commands remain available.
    
    # Frontier chronicles (version 2.3)
    
    - Three staged objectives per campaign chapter, original dialogue journals, optional medals, and active minimap/3D goal markers.
    - Supply-caravan mesh model and guarded river escort with an explicit loss condition. Select-caravan and locate-goal controls are available in the objective panel.
    - Frozen initial and stage checkpoints, commander-menu and defeat-screen recovery, local save/resume, and legacy rules for existing campaign saves.
    - Settlement, fortress, shrine-control/conquest, siege-breach, and coastal landing/artillery chapter flows. Fishing objectives count deposited boat catch.
    - Objective updates preserve scrolling/focus and expose interactive controls without triggering camera edge scrolling. Phone recovery controls and compact technology-tree layouts receive browser coverage.
    - Exact waypoint arrival and island-aware naval regrouping reduce the coastal diagnostic run from 74 blocked orders to four. Remaining bridge/crowding cases still need review.
    - Regression coverage includes normal economy/production, real escort navigation, shrine holding, paid naval artillery, actual gate attacks, actor loss, and checkpoint recovery.
    
    This continues the playable beta roadmap. External balance and mission-pacing tests, real-device rendering performance, richer authored assets/audio, public online operations, and overall world-class parity remain unfinished.

    The production output is in `dist/`. Deploy it to a static web host. The generated service worker caches the game and its bundled assets for offline use after the first successful visit over HTTPS (or localhost). The web app manifest requests fullscreen landscape when installed. Browser support for fullscreen, installation, and orientation locking varies. Fonts and their licenses are bundled locally. No game assets depend on a third-party CDN.
    
    The browser QA scripts use a locally installed Microsoft Edge. `release-qa.mjs` tests a real room with desktop and emulated phone clients, both command perspectives, phone troop training, and reconnecting after a reload. It defaults to a test server on port 4180; set `QA_URL` to another server URL as needed. `npm test` also runs a real WebSocket test for fair starts, ownership rejection, fog masking, disconnect pauses, and session restoration. Emulation does not substitute for testing on physical phones.
    
    ## Implementation
    
    - `src/campaigns.js` and `src/campaign-view.js`: staged mission rules, story journals, escort actor, optional objectives, checkpoint snapshots, and 3D goal markers.
    
    - `src/controls.js` and `src/keyboard-settings.js`: saved keyboard bindings, conflict checks, active-key documentation, and the settings editor.
    - `src/tactics.js`: patrol/guard commands, legal formation destinations, and stances.
    - `src/commander-ai.js`: paid economy and army plans, scouting memory, counter composition, retreats, repairs, and naval staging.
    - `src/technology-tree.js`: civilization comparison, prerequisites, and direct training/research.
    
    - `src/data.js`: troops, buildings, research, civilizations, difficulties, maps, and missions.
    - `src/simulation.js`: deterministic map generation and independent fixed-step gameplay simulation. The opponent gathers, pays for buildings and units, advances ages, researches technologies, and attacks. Survival is explicitly a wave-spawn scenario.
    - `src/world.js`: procedural 3D models, camera, ray picking, shadows, fog, and combat effects. Forests and units use instanced rendering; buildings/resources merge geometry by material. Graphics adapt to sustained slow frames.
    - `src/landscape.js`: seeded elevated terrain, triangulated surface sampling and ray picking, river/coastal beds, bridges, terrain textures, solid grass tufts, and animated water meshes.
    - `src/models-3d.js`: solid world models for the complete building/unit/resource catalog and civilization architecture.
    - `src/realm-3d.js`: terrain/model integration, packed forest detail levels, foundations, construction clipping and scaffolds, previews, gate motion, and solid projectiles.
    - `src/portrait-3d.js`: throttled live 3D selection turntables.
    - `src/main.js`: menus, responsive HUD, touch/mouse/keyboard controls, objectives, saves, and modal flows.
    - `src/map-geometry.js` and `src/minimap.js`: square radar coordinates, bounded rectangular camera locator, waterways, icons, and camera location.
    - `src/production.js`: completed production sites and training batches balanced across eligible building queues, including virtual planning for multiplayer snapshots.
    - `src/audio.js`: synthesized cues and ambient music.
    - `src/frontiers.js`: naval mechanics and tactical AI additions.
    - `src/navigation.js`: heap-based pathfinding.
    - `src/world-polish.js`: articulated model animation, ship models, material textures, and exploration-aware foliage.
    - `src/soundscape.js`: battle sounds and atmospheric audio.
    - `src/network.js`: room connection, commands, and session reconnection.
    - `server/rooms.js`: authoritative Wi-Fi matches, player perspectives, command validation, disconnect handling, and room lifecycle.
    - `server/index.js`: local game hosting and WebSocket server.
    - `vite.config.js`: build splitting and offline cache generation.
    
    ## Research and scope
    
    The design draws on the genre's established exploration â†’ resource collection â†’ construction â†’ army â†’ age progression loop and varied victory conditions described in the [official Age of Empires IV quickstart](https://www.ageofempires.com/news/quickstart-guide-age-of-empires-iv/) and [official strategy introduction](https://www.ageofempires.com/news/age-of-empires-iv-tips-to-help-you-get-started/). Picking and repeated-model rendering follow the [Three.js Raycaster](https://threejs.org/docs/pages/Raycaster.html) and [InstancedMesh](https://threejs.org/docs/pages/InstancedMesh.html) documentation.
    
    Instanced animation follows the [Three.js update documentation](https://threejs.org/manual/pages/how-to-update-things.html). Room transport and heartbeat handling follow the [official ws documentation](https://github.com/websockets/ws). The naval design considers fishing economies, transport landings, and shoreline defense described in the [official Age of Empires naval update](https://www.ageofempires.com/news/age-of-empires-iv-update-11-0-782/).
    
    # Crowns of the Frontier: quality roadmap
    
    Reviewed 9 October 2026 against the version 2.3 source and current verification scripts.
    
    This is an ordered development proposal, not a claim that its milestones have been implemented. The current game is a playable beta. A world-class assessment needs independent player feedback, reliable performance, strong content, and sustained quality across complete matches.
    
    ## Current baseline
    
    - Three.js world with elevated terrain, solid building/unit/resource models, articulated parts, animated water, and 3D selection portraits.
    - Resource gathering, construction, queues, upgrades, ages, unit counters, siege, healing, walls, gates, fleets, transports, fog, saves, and several victory conditions.
    - Eight modes, seven seeded maps, six campaign chapters, three civilizations, 19 building types, and 16 trainable types across the catalog plus sovereigns.
    - Two-player Wi-Fi rooms with authoritative commands, player perspectives, and reconnection. Rooms are held in server memory; they are not a public matchmaking service.
    - Mouse edge scrolling, corner scrolling, cursor arrows, keyboard controls, camera inspection, and landscape touch input.
    - Square radar with a rectangular camera locator and mouse/touch dragging. Global production overview, selection across completed production buildings, balanced training batches, and cancel/refund controls.
    - Existing automated simulation/graphics/network checks and browser verification. Physical-device performance, balance, and extensive human playtesting remain unverified.

    Instanced animation follows the [Three.js update documentation](https://threejs.org/manual/pages/how-to-update-things.html). Room transport and heartbeat handling follow the [official ws documentation](https://github.com/websockets/ws). The naval design considers fishing economies, transport landings, and shoreline defense described in the [official Age of Empires naval update](https://www.ageofempires.com/news/age-of-empires-iv-update-11-0-782/).
    
    The graphics use shaped [CapsuleGeometry](https://threejs.org/docs/pages/CapsuleGeometry.html), solid architectural [ExtrudeGeometry](https://threejs.org/docs/pages/ExtrudeGeometry.html), and indexed terrain [BufferGeometry](https://threejs.org/docs/pages/BufferGeometry.html). Distant forests use simpler solid geometry and pack only visible instances; world objects do not switch to billboard images.
    
    This is an original playable RTS implementation with procedural art, fictional civilizations, and its own balance. It contains no Age of Empires assets or licensed branding. Two-player Wi-Fi gameplay is implemented; public internet matchmaking, accounts, historical documentary campaigns, professional voice acting, and a production-scale backend service are not. Commercial AAA parity is not claimed. Balance and performance need broader human playtesting and real-device testing; smooth performance on every device cannot be guaranteed.

    ## Development order and release checks
    
    | Pass | Work to implement or improve | Evidence required before declaring the pass complete |
    |---|---|---|
    | 1. Controls and army movement | Remappable hotkeys, selection priority, production across selected buildings, global production queue, queued-command feedback, patrol/guard behaviors, formation cohesion, obstacle avoidance, and recovery from blocked routes. Preserve edge scrolling and touch input. | Repeatable mouse/keyboard/touch scenarios; armies navigate woods, walls, gates, bridges, and crowded towns; no duplicated queued orders or indefinitely stuck troops in the tested cases. Local command feedback and execution latency measured on reference hardware. |
    | 2. Economy, AI, and battle balance | Explicit AI build orders and resource budgets, scouting memory, different attack plans, counter-unit composition, regrouping, retreating, siege protection, expansion, transport decisions, and difficulty based on decisions. Audit starting advantages and any difficulty bonuses. | Seeded economy and combat scenarios; AI can recover after worker losses and exhausted nearby resources; attacks change based on observed enemies; difficulty rules are documented; human testers find each level understandable and challenging. |
    | 3. Civilizations and strategic depth | Unique units and technologies, clearer civilization identities, useful upgrade choices, meaningful land/naval counters, alternative economic strategies, and an interactive technology tree. Expand team/player support before adding team modes. | Comparable-cost counter scenarios plus human matches; all additions have costs, prerequisites, counters, descriptions, art, audio, AI support, saves, and multiplayer validation. Balance judged across maps and skill levels. |
    | 4. Missions and map design | A mission-event system with staged objectives, dialogue, reinforcements, escort/rescue tasks, branching optional goals, checkpoints, and authored set pieces. Curate resource placement, chokepoints, naval landings, and spawn fairness. | Each mission can be completed and failed correctly on each difficulty; checkpoints restore the correct event state; missions require different strategies; map objectives and travel routes remain reachable. |
    | 5. Art, animation, and sound | Establish a consistent medieval art direction; replace or refine the procedural assets with original or appropriately licensed authored models, textures, character rigs, transitions, worker tasks, cargo, attack impacts, damage, and death animations. Add distinctive music, unit responses, ambience, and readable combat sound. | Visual review in real gameplay at every quality setting and camera angle; recognizable units and silhouettes; animations match actions; assets fit performance budgets; retain real mesh geometry at every detail level. |
    | 6. Laptop and phone experience | Profile CPU/GPU work, pathfinding, draw calls, memory, network snapshots, and input delay. Improve detail levels, shared routes, batching, effects budgets, loading, safe areas, readable UI, touch selection, UI scaling, and accessibility options. | Publish device/browser/specification results. Proposed targets: 60 FPS on a defined reference laptop and 30 FPS on defined supported phones in benchmark matches. Verify sustained performance, frame-time spikes, thermal behavior, and memory over long sessions. Targets are not current achievements or guarantees for every device. |
    | 7. Multiplayer and community | Public hosting, persistent room/session state, matchmaking, reconnect recovery, cooperative/team games, profiles, replay/spectator tools, authoritative validation, and operational monitoring. Generalize the current two-player simulation and perspective assumptions first. | Test multiple clients, latency, packet loss, disconnects, server restarts, ownership, hidden-information handling, version compatibility, and replay results. Hosting choices and ongoing costs need an explicit deployment decision. |
    | 8. Release readiness | Improve onboarding, settings, saved-game migrations, campaign progression, post-match economy/combat graphs, installation/update behavior, diagnostics, recovery, and documentation. Conduct repeated external playtests and fix their highest-impact problems. | Long complete matches, all modes, save/resume/update cycles, physical phones/laptops, multiplayer failure scenarios, and accessibility reviews pass the agreed release checklist. Record remaining limitations instead of labeling unchecked areas complete. |

    +# Kingdoms and skies (version 2.4)
    +
    +- Configurable custom battles with two to eight kingdoms, human or AI slots, civilizations, teams, individual AI difficulties and six team/free-for-all presets.
    +- Huge 400 × 400 maps by default, plus 320 × 320 and 240 × 240 options. Navigation, fog, terrain picking, camera limits, minimap and rendering support the larger battlefield and eight army colors.

    +

## Assistant

The eight-kingdom battle diagnostic reached a real result after about 29 simulated minutes. All kingdoms advanced to Imperial Age, and the losing alliance was eliminated through normal economy, production, and combat.

That is useful evidence for a longer battle, though human playtesting is still needed to judge pacing. I’ve also added paid market trades so AI kingdoms can recover from resource shortages without receiving free supplies.
