    # Crowns of the Frontier: quality roadmap
    
    Reviewed 10 October 2026 against the version 2.4 source and current verification scripts.
    
    This is an ordered development proposal, not a claim that its milestones have been implemented. The current game is a playable beta. A world-class assessment needs independent player feedback, reliable performance, strong content, and sustained quality across complete matches.
    
    ## Current baseline
    
    - Three.js world with elevated terrain, solid building/unit/resource models, articulated parts, animated water, and 3D selection portraits.
    - Resource gathering, construction, queues, upgrades, ages, unit counters, siege, healing, walls, gates, fleets, transports, fog, saves, and several victory conditions.
    - Nine modes, seven seeded maps, six campaign chapters, three civilizations, 19 building types, and 16 trainable types across the catalog plus sovereigns.
    - Two-to-eight-kingdom custom battles, AI allies/enemies with individual difficulties, human slots, huge maps and three elimination rules.
    - Classic two-player and custom mixed human/AI Wi-Fi rooms with authoritative commands, team perspectives, readiness and reconnection. Rooms are held in server memory; they are not a public matchmaking service.
    - Seeded volumetric weather, pooled effects, optional audio/lightning and quality budgets.
    - Mouse edge scrolling, corner scrolling, cursor arrows, keyboard controls, camera inspection, and landscape touch input.
    - Square radar with a rectangular camera locator and mouse/touch dragging. Global production overview, selection across completed production buildings, balanced training batches, and cancel/refund controls.
    - Existing automated simulation/graphics/network checks and browser verification. Physical-device performance, balance, and extensive human playtesting remain unverified.
    
    ## Version 2.4 custom-battle progress
    
    - The requested AI and real-human battle configurations are implemented separately in one custom setup. Solo configurations convert the other enabled slots to AI; multiplayer preserves Human slots and allows AI kingdoms alongside them.
    - Huge maps, eight kingdoms, allied gates/healing/shared vision, independent AI economies and planning clocks, capital rebuilding, all-building elimination, optional conquest/capital rules and team victory are implemented.
    - Multiplayer checks include eight real WebSocket participants, private economies and fog, ownership, mixed AI/humans, guest slot choice, readiness, concessions, host defeat, reconnect and winning/losing alliance perspectives.
    - Resource exhaustion, unreachable routes, outer-map picking and private completion notices were corrected during the audit. Cached movement regions, route retention, vision indexing, pooled weather and reduced render cadence address measured CPU/GPU pressure.
    - Keep physical-device performance, multiplayer latency/failure testing and human balance/pacing reviews in the release checklist. The original 3D art remains procedural; commercial world-class parity has not been established.
    
    ## Version 2.3 campaign progress
    
    - Six chapters now have three authored stages each, original dialogue journals, optional completion medals, and active goal markers in the minimap and explored 3D world.
    - The river chapter has a modeled supply caravan, guarded escort navigation, a bridgehead objective, a loss condition, and recovery through frozen checkpoints.
    - Fortress defense requires a completed castle and the wave objectives. Sacred valley supports shrine control or a recorded conquest alternative. Final siege requires paid siege production and a defensive breach. The coastal chapter counts actual deposited fishing catch and accepts a landing or an Imperial siege-galleon route.
    - Initial and stage checkpoints preserve actors, objectives, economy, armies, exploration, and AI state without recursive snapshots. Existing campaign saves retain legacy rules.
    - Automated scenarios use gathering, construction, training, escort movement, shrine control, fishing, and gate attacks to exercise the chapter flows. All four difficulties initialize every chapter. Browser verification covers journals, selecting and inspecting the caravan, locating goals, defeat recovery, local save/resume, and emulated-phone controls.
    
    Pass 4 has a playable scripted baseline. Human completion tests on all difficulties, more mission events and set pieces, professional narration/audio, broader map fairness checks, and mission pacing remain unfinished.
    
    ## Version 2.2 implementation progress
    
    - Saved remappable keyboard controls, reserved-key validation, conflict reporting, active key documentation, and updated shortcut labels.
    - Patrol and guard commands in the simulation, desktop/touch interface, saves, and authoritative network commands. Formation slots avoid blocked terrain. Partial paths no longer count as successful arrival; persistent blocked orders report feedback and yield to queued orders.
    - Selected-unit order summaries and bounded 3D route previews, including patrol return routes and ship routes above the water.
    - Paid AI economy and army planning, civilization-aware counter composition, scouting memory, age-resource reserves, worker reassignment, repairs, retreats, healer escorts, and transport boarding/departure reservations.
    - Three civilization-exclusive units with solid model variants, explicit costs, age/building requirements, and distinct roles. Three exclusive technologies affect armor, market exchange, and cavalry raids. Old saves initialize the new research fields.
    - Interactive technology tree with faction comparison, prerequisite/status explanations, training, and research. Higher-contrast UI, reduced decorative motion, and larger tactical touch buttons.
    - Regression coverage now includes these behaviors. Commander browser checks exercise remapping, persistence, tactics, queued-order feedback without movement lines, save/resume, and desktop/emulated-phone layouts. Passive-player soak checks exercise full land, river, and coastal matches and record simulation CPU timings.
    
    Passes 1 through 3 have concrete implementation progress; they are not fully complete. Group cohesion, advanced recovery, AI expansion, further economy/combat tuning, richer strategic interactions, authored missions, asset/audio production, measured device performance, public online services, and external playtesting remain on the roadmap. Naval regrouping now respects the current island, and movement reaches the actual final waypoint rather than stopping at a grid center. The latest coastal soak reports four blocked orders instead of 74 in the previous diagnostic run; remaining land/bridge cases still need review. CPU timings from automated simulations do not establish rendering FPS, phone performance, or enjoyable difficulty.
    
    ## Development order and release checks
    
    | Pass | Work to implement or improve | Evidence required before declaring the pass complete |
    |---|---|---|
    | 1. Controls and army movement | Remappable hotkeys, selection priority, production across selected buildings, global production queue, queued-command feedback, patrol/guard behaviors, formation cohesion, obstacle avoidance, and recovery from blocked routes. Preserve edge scrolling and touch input. | Repeatable mouse/keyboard/touch scenarios; armies navigate woods, walls, gates, bridges, and crowded towns; no duplicated queued orders or indefinitely stuck troops in the tested cases. Local command feedback and execution latency measured on reference hardware. |
    | 2. Economy, AI, and battle balance | Explicit AI build orders and resource budgets, scouting memory, different attack plans, counter-unit composition, regrouping, retreating, siege protection, expansion, transport decisions, and difficulty based on decisions. Audit starting advantages and any difficulty bonuses. | Seeded economy and combat scenarios; AI can recover after worker losses and exhausted nearby resources; attacks change based on observed enemies; difficulty rules are documented; human testers find each level understandable and challenging. |
    | 3. Civilizations and strategic depth | Build on the implemented exclusive units/technologies, technology tree and eight-kingdom team support with clearer identities, more useful upgrade choices, land/naval counters and alternative economic strategies. | Comparable-cost counter scenarios plus human matches; all additions have costs, prerequisites, counters, descriptions, art, audio, AI support, saves, and multiplayer validation. Balance judged across maps and skill levels. |
    | 4. Missions and map design | A mission-event system with staged objectives, dialogue, reinforcements, escort/rescue tasks, branching optional goals, checkpoints, and authored set pieces. Curate resource placement, chokepoints, naval landings, and spawn fairness. | Each mission can be completed and failed correctly on each difficulty; checkpoints restore the correct event state; missions require different strategies; map objectives and travel routes remain reachable. |
    | 5. Art, animation, and sound | Establish a consistent medieval art direction; replace or refine the procedural assets with original or appropriately licensed authored models, textures, character rigs, transitions, worker tasks, cargo, attack impacts, damage, and death animations. Add distinctive music, unit responses, ambience, and readable combat sound. | Visual review in real gameplay at every quality setting and camera angle; recognizable units and silhouettes; animations match actions; assets fit performance budgets; retain real mesh geometry at every detail level. |
    | 6. Laptop and phone experience | Profile CPU/GPU work, pathfinding, draw calls, memory, network snapshots, and input delay. Improve detail levels, shared routes, batching, effects budgets, loading, safe areas, readable UI, touch selection, UI scaling, and accessibility options. | Publish device/browser/specification results. Proposed targets: 60 FPS on a defined reference laptop and 30 FPS on defined supported phones in benchmark matches. Verify sustained performance, frame-time spikes, thermal behavior, and memory over long sessions. Targets are not current achievements or guarantees for every device. |
    | 7. Multiplayer and community | Extend the implemented team rooms, readiness, authoritative validation, defeat spectating and reconnect recovery with public hosting, persistent rooms, matchmaking, profiles, replays and operational monitoring. | Test multiple clients, latency, packet loss, disconnects, server restarts, ownership, hidden-information handling, version compatibility, and replay results. Hosting choices and ongoing costs need an explicit deployment decision. |
    | 8. Release readiness | Improve onboarding, settings, saved-game migrations, campaign progression, post-match economy/combat graphs, installation/update behavior, diagnostics, recovery, and documentation. Conduct repeated external playtests and fix their highest-impact problems. | Long complete matches, all modes, save/resume/update cycles, physical phones/laptops, multiplayer failure scenarios, and accessibility reviews pass the agreed release checklist. Record remaining limitations instead of labeling unchecked areas complete. |
    
    Performance, regression testing, and human feedback run throughout these passes; they are not postponed until the end.
    
    ## Recommended next release
    
    Start with Pass 1 and the most visible parts of Pass 2:
    
    1. Global production overview and multi-building training are implemented. Configurable hotkeys and queued-order feedback are now implemented; continue with group cohesion, obstacle recovery, and full-match input testing.
    2. Continue control refinements with profile management, selection priority, and accessibility reviews.
    3. Improve group movement through gates, around buildings, and over bridges; show blocked-order feedback.
    4. Refine the implemented AI plans with expansion, resource exhaustion recovery, siege protection, and human difficulty tuning.
    5. Exercise complete economy-to-victory matches with several seeds and difficulties, followed by laptop and phone playtests.
    
    Deliver these as tested releases that can be played and reviewed. Additional units or prettier screenshots alone do not establish overall game quality.
    
    ## What can be developed here and what needs outside evidence
    
    The existing workspace supports implementation of gameplay, AI, UI, asset integration, shaders, animation, performance instrumentation, testing, and multiplayer services. Professional asset/audio production requires suitable original work or licensed sources. Physical-device results require access to the actual devices or measurements from testers. Public online operation requires a hosting decision and ongoing service resources. Fun and balance require repeated human playtesting.
    
    No honest development process can promise an objective â€œ100% world-classâ€ score. The useful commitment is to finish defined requirements, publish test evidence, address player feedback, and improve successive releases.
    
    ## Research references
    
    - [Official Age of Empires IV Season One development notes](https://www.ageofempires.com/news/age-of-empires-iv-season-one-update-release-notes/): controls, global production queues, patrol, player feedback, balance, maps, campaign tuning, and post-match navigation. Used as a genre quality reference, not a statement of this project's implemented features.
    - [Official Age of Empires IV Season Two development notes](https://www.ageofempires.com/news/age-of-empires-iv-update-17718/): continued iteration across controls, game modes, multiplayer, and stability.
    - The baseline above is supported by the local source, [README](README.md), [change log](CHANGELOG.md), and tests/scripts in this repository.

    README.md:31:The default victory rule is **destroy all opposing buildings**, including walls and unfinished foundations. Losing a capital alone does not eliminate a kingdom; surviving villagers can rebuild. Other rules require the last town center to fall, or require every opposing unit and building to be defeated. The final few buildings can be revealed after a capital falls to help finish the war. Battles develop through real paid gathering, construction, upgrades and armies; their length depends on the battle rather than a forced minimum timer.

    src/main.js:56:function toast(message,tone=''){const el=document.createElement('div');el.className=`toast ${tone}`;el.textContent=message;$('#toasts').append(el);while($('#toasts').children.length>3)$('#toasts').firstElementChild.remove();setTimeout(()=>el.remove(),4800);}
    src/main.js:75:function startGame(options,save=null){if(!view)return;edgeScroll.reset();audio.lastThunder=undefined;tacticalMode=null;unloadMode=false;productionOpen=false;productionKey='';$('#production-panel').classList.add('hidden');$('#production-toggle').setAttribute('aria-expanded','false');$('#hud').classList.remove('panels-hidden');$('[data-action=camera-panels]').setAttribute('aria-pressed','false');closeModal();setupOptions={...setupOptions,...options};sim=save?Simulation.restore(save):new Simulation(options);view.attach(sim);sim.on(onEvent);playing=true;paused=false;speed=1;groups={};$('#toasts').innerHTML='';selection=[];view.selection=new Set();buildType=null;attackMove=false;accumulator=0;lastAutosave=sim.time;$('#landing').classList.add('hidden');$('#hud').classList.remove('hidden');$('#build-panel').classList.add('hidden');view.angle=Math.PI/4;view.setCameraPreset(settings.cameraPreset,true);updateCameraLabel();audio.unlock();renderHUD();renderSelection();updateRotate();toast('Your kingdom awaits.     src/main.js:178:  if(name==='custom-battle')return showCustomBattle();if(name==='custom-start')return launchCustom(false);if(name==='custom-host')return launchCustom(true);if(name==='lan-ready'){net.ready=!net.ready;net.send({type:'ready',ready:net.ready});return;}if(name==='resign'){closeModal();sim.resign(0);return;}if(name==='lan')return showLan();if(name==='lan-host')return connectLan(true);if(name==='lan-join')return connectLan(false);if(name==='lan-start'){net.send({type:'start'});return;}if(name==='lan-leave'){net.leave();closeModal();return;}if(name==='lan-resume'){net.connect({type:'resume',...net.session});showModal('<h2>Rejoining your kingdom…</h2>','lan');return;}if(name==='unload'){unloadMode=true;$('#order-hint').textContent='Choose open shore within 11 meters of the transport.';return;}if(name==='close')return closeModal();if(name==='campaign')return showCampaign();if(name==='settings')return showSettings();if(name==='codex')return showCodex();if(name==='tech-tree')return showTechnologyTree();if(name==='help')return showHelp();if(name==='dismiss-rotate'){portraitDismissed=true;return updateRotate();}
    src/main.js:281:function showLan(){if(net.active)return showPause();showModal(`<div class="eyebrow">TWO COMMANDERS. ONE FRONTIER.</div><h2>Meet on the battlefield.</h2><p class="modal-intro">Open this laptop's Wi-Fi game link on every device. Join a room by code, or create a custom battle with up to eight kingdoms and a mix of friends and AI.</p><button class="secondary full" data-action="custom-battle">Create custom multiplayer battle</button><div class="setup-grid"><div><label class="field-label" for="lan-name">COMMANDER NAME</label><input id="lan-name" maxlength="24" value="Commander"></div><div><label class="field-label" for="lan-faction">CIVILIZATION</label><select id="lan-faction">${Object.entries(FACTIONS).map(([id,f])=>`<option value="${id}">${f.name}</option>`).join('')}</select></div><div><label class="field-label" for="lan-mode">VICTORY CONDITION</label><select id="lan-mode">${MODES.filter(m=>['skirmish','regicide','dominion','wonder','tides'].includes(m.id)).map(m=>`<option value="${m.id}">${m.name}</option>`).join('')}</select></div><div><label class="field-label" for="lan-map">BATTLEFIELD</label><select id="lan-map">${Object.entries(MAPS).map(([id,m])=>`<option value="${id}">${m.name}</option>`).join('')}</select></div></div><button class="primary full lan-create" data-action="lan-host">Create a room <span>➜</span></button><label class="field-label" for="lan-slot">CUSTOM ROOM SLOT</label><select id="lan-slot"><option value="0">Automatic assignment</option><option value="2">Slot 2</option><option value="3">Slot 3</option><option value="4">Slot 4</option><option value="5">Slot 5</option><option value="6">Slot 6</option><option value="7">Slot 7</option><option value="8">Slot 8</option></select><div class="lan-join"><input id="lan-code" maxlength="6" placeholder="ROOM CODE" aria-label="Room code"><button class="secondary" data-action="lan-join">Join a room ↗</button></div>${net.session?'<button class="text-button" data-action="lan-resume">Rejoin your previous network session</button>':''}<p class="settings-note">Wi-Fi multiplayer requires the game server started with <b>npm start</b>. Matches pause during a connection interruption and allow up to two minutes to reconnect.</p>`,'lan',true);}

        let active=0;draft.slots.forEach((slot,index)=>{if(!slot.enabled)return;const point=spawns[active++],x=(point.x/battle.worldSize+.5)*size,z=(point.z/battle.worldSize+.5)*size;

    }
    export function battleResultMarkup(sim){

      return `<div class="battle-result-table"><table><caption>Kingdom results</caption><thead><tr><th>Kingdom</th><th>Team</th><th>Defeated</th><th>Gathered</th></tr></thead><tbody>${sim.players.map(player=>`<tr><th>${esc(player.name)}</th><td>${player.team}</td><td>${player.battleStats.kills}</td><td>${Math.floor(player.battleStats.gathered)}</td></tr>`).join('')}</tbody></table></div>`;
    }

        const slots=customDraft.slots.map(slot=>({...slot}));if(!slots.slice(1).some(slot=>slot.enabled&&slot.controller==='human')){const next=slots.findIndex((slot,i)=>i>0&&slot.enabled);slots[next].controller='human';}
        const options=normalizeBattle({...customDraft,slots,multiplayer:true});if(net.socket)net.leave();net.connect({type:'create',name:options.slots[0].name,faction:options.slots[0].faction,options});showModal('<h2>Creating your war roomâ€¦</h2><button class="secondary" data-action="lan-leave">Cancel</button>','lan');
      }catch(error){toast(error.message,'warning');}
    }

## Assistant

    # Crowns of the Frontier: quality roadmap
    
    Reviewed 10 October 2026 against the version 2.4 source and current verification scripts.
    
    This is an ordered development proposal, not a claim that its milestones have been implemented. The current game is a playable beta. A world-class assessment needs independent player feedback, reliable performance, strong content, and sustained quality across complete matches.
    
    ## Current baseline
    
    - Three.js world with elevated terrain, solid building/unit/resource models, articulated parts, animated water, and 3D selection portraits.
    - Resource gathering, construction, queues, upgrades, ages, unit counters, siege, healing, walls, gates, fleets, transports, fog, saves, and several victory conditions.
    - Nine modes, seven seeded maps, six campaign chapters, three civilizations, 19 building types, and 16 trainable types across the catalog plus sovereigns.
    - Two-to-eight-kingdom custom battles, AI allies/enemies with individual difficulties, human slots, huge maps and three elimination rules.
    - Classic two-player and custom mixed human/AI Wi-Fi rooms with authoritative commands, team perspectives, readiness and reconnection. Rooms are held in server memory; they are not a public matchmaking service.
    - Seeded volumetric weather, pooled effects, optional audio/lightning and quality budgets.
    - Rooted and wind-animated trees, winter snowcaps, harvested tree falls/stumps, batched carried supplies, ore depletion, and age-specific town-center architecture. Huge-map fog and grass cover the full playable area.
    - Free Render deployment configuration for one game/multiplayer service, plus optional Netlify static hosting and a separate secure multiplayer endpoint. Hosting variants have local browser coverage; no public deployment is active.
    - Mouse edge scrolling, corner scrolling, cursor arrows, keyboard controls, camera inspection, and landscape touch input.
    - Square radar with a rectangular camera locator and mouse/touch dragging. Global production overview, selection across completed production buildings, balanced training batches, and cancel/refund controls.
    - Existing automated simulation/graphics/network checks and browser verification. Physical-device performance, balance, and extensive human playtesting remain unverified.
    
    ## Version 2.4 custom-battle progress
    
    - The requested AI and real-human battle configurations are implemented separately in one custom setup. Solo configurations convert the other enabled slots to AI; multiplayer preserves Human slots and allows AI kingdoms alongside them.
    - Huge maps, eight kingdoms, allied gates/healing/shared vision, independent AI economies and planning clocks, capital rebuilding, all-building elimination, optional conquest/capital rules and team victory are implemented.
    - Multiplayer checks include eight real WebSocket participants, private economies and fog, ownership, mixed AI/humans, guest slot choice, readiness, concessions, host defeat, reconnect and winning/losing alliance perspectives.
    - Resource exhaustion, unreachable routes, outer-map picking and private completion notices were corrected during the audit. Cached movement regions, route retention, vision indexing, pooled weather and reduced render cadence address measured CPU/GPU pressure.
    - Coastal armies use their current shore, scout capitals, search remaining settlements, reserve fleet capacity, rebuild harbors, prioritize transports and fill balanced crews. A full eight-kingdom paid coastal war now reaches all-building victory; the final diagnostic lasted about 19 simulated minutes.
    - Keep physical-device performance, multiplayer latency/failure testing and human balance/pacing reviews in the release checklist. The original 3D art remains procedural; commercial world-class parity has not been established.
    
    ## Version 2.3 campaign progress
    
    - Six chapters now have three authored stages each, original dialogue journals, optional completion medals, and active goal markers in the minimap and explored 3D world.
    - The river chapter has a modeled supply caravan, guarded escort navigation, a bridgehead objective, a loss condition, and recovery through frozen checkpoints.
    - Fortress defense requires a completed castle and the wave objectives. Sacred valley supports shrine control or a recorded conquest alternative. Final siege requires paid siege production and a defensive breach. The coastal chapter counts actual deposited fishing catch and accepts a landing or an Imperial siege-galleon route.
    - Initial and stage checkpoints preserve actors, objectives, economy, armies, exploration, and AI state without recursive snapshots. Existing campaign saves retain legacy rules.
    - Automated scenarios use gathering, construction, training, escort movement, shrine control, fishing, and gate attacks to exercise the chapter flows. All four difficulties initialize every chapter. Browser verification covers journals, selecting and inspecting the caravan, locating goals, defeat recovery, local save/resume, and emulated-phone controls.
    
    Pass 4 has a playable scripted baseline. Human completion tests on all difficulties, more mission events and set pieces, professional narration/audio, broader map fairness checks, and mission pacing remain unfinished.
    
    ## Version 2.2 implementation progress
    
    - Saved remappable keyboard controls, reserved-key validation, conflict reporting, active key documentation, and updated shortcut labels.
    - Patrol and guard commands in the simulation, desktop/touch interface, saves, and authoritative network commands. Formation slots avoid blocked terrain. Partial paths no longer count as successful arrival; persistent blocked orders report feedback and yield to queued orders.
    - Selected-unit order summaries and bounded 3D route previews, including patrol return routes and ship routes above the water.
    - Paid AI economy and army planning, civilization-aware counter composition, scouting memory, age-resource reserves, worker reassignment, repairs, retreats, healer escorts, and transport boarding/departure reservations.
    - Three civilization-exclusive units with solid model variants, explicit costs, age/building requirements, and distinct roles. Three exclusive technologies affect armor, market exchange, and cavalry raids. Old saves initialize the new research fields.
    - Interactive technology tree with faction comparison, prerequisite/status explanations, training, and research. Higher-contrast UI, reduced decorative motion, and larger tactical touch buttons.
    - Regression coverage now includes these behaviors. Commander browser checks exercise remapping, persistence, tactics, queued-order feedback without movement lines, save/resume, and desktop/emulated-phone layouts. Passive-player soak checks exercise full land, river, and coastal matches and record simulation CPU timings.
    
    Passes 1 through 3 have concrete implementation progress; they are not fully complete. Group cohesion, advanced recovery, AI expansion, further economy/combat tuning, richer strategic interactions, authored missions, asset/audio production, measured device performance, public online services, and external playtesting remain on the roadmap. Naval regrouping now respects the current island, and movement reaches the actual final waypoint rather than stopping at a grid center. The latest coastal soak reports four blocked orders instead of 74 in the previous diagnostic run; remaining land/bridge cases still need review. CPU timings from automated simulations do not establish rendering FPS, phone performance, or enjoyable difficulty.
    
    ## Development order and release checks
    
    | Pass | Work to implement or improve | Evidence required before declaring the pass complete |
    |---|---|---|
    | 1. Controls and army movement | Remappable hotkeys, selection priority, production across selected buildings, global production queue, queued-command feedback, patrol/guard behaviors, formation cohesion, obstacle avoidance, and recovery from blocked routes. Preserve edge scrolling and touch input. | Repeatable mouse/keyboard/touch scenarios; armies navigate woods, walls, gates, bridges, and crowded towns; no duplicated queued orders or indefinitely stuck troops in the tested cases. Local command feedback and execution latency measured on reference hardware. |
    | 2. Economy, AI, and battle balance | Explicit AI build orders and resource budgets, scouting memory, different attack plans, counter-unit composition, regrouping, retreating, siege protection, expansion, transport decisions, and difficulty based on decisions. Audit starting advantages and any difficulty bonuses. | Seeded economy and combat scenarios; AI can recover after worker losses and exhausted nearby resources; attacks change based on observed enemies; difficulty rules are documented; human testers find each level understandable and challenging. |
    | 3. Civilizations and strategic depth | Build on the implemented exclusive units/technologies, technology tree and eight-kingdom team support with clearer identities, more useful upgrade choices, land/naval counters and alternative economic strategies. | Comparable-cost counter scenarios plus human matches; all additions have costs, prerequisites, counters, descriptions, art, audio, AI support, saves, and multiplayer validation. Balance judged across maps and skill levels. |
    | 4. Missions and map design | A mission-event system with staged objectives, dialogue, reinforcements, escort/rescue tasks, branching optional goals, checkpoints, and authored set pieces. Curate resource placement, chokepoints, naval landings, and spawn fairness. | Each mission can be completed and failed correctly on each difficulty; checkpoints restore the correct event state; missions require different strategies; map objectives and travel routes remain reachable. |
    | 5. Art, animation, and sound | Establish a consistent medieval art direction; replace or refine the procedural assets with original or appropriately licensed authored models, textures, character rigs, transitions, worker tasks, cargo, attack impacts, damage, and death animations. Add distinctive music, unit responses, ambience, and readable combat sound. | Visual review in real gameplay at every quality setting and camera angle; recognizable units and silhouettes; animations match actions; assets fit performance budgets; retain real mesh geometry at every detail level. |
    | 6. Laptop and phone experience | Profile CPU/GPU work, pathfinding, draw calls, memory, network snapshots, and input delay. Improve detail levels, shared routes, batching, effects budgets, loading, safe areas, readable UI, touch selection, UI scaling, and accessibility options. | Publish device/browser/specification results. Proposed targets: 60 FPS on a defined reference laptop and 30 FPS on defined supported phones in benchmark matches. Verify sustained performance, frame-time spikes, thermal behavior, and memory over long sessions. Targets are not current achievements or guarantees for every device. |
    | 7. Multiplayer and community | Extend the implemented team rooms, readiness, authoritative validation, defeat spectating and reconnect recovery with public hosting, persistent rooms, matchmaking, profiles, replays and operational monitoring. | Test multiple clients, latency, packet loss, disconnects, server restarts, ownership, hidden-information handling, version compatibility, and replay results. Hosting choices and ongoing costs need an explicit deployment decision. |
    | 8. Release readiness | Improve onboarding, settings, saved-game migrations, campaign progression, post-match economy/combat graphs, installation/update behavior, diagnostics, recovery, and documentation. Conduct repeated external playtests and fix their highest-impact problems. | Long complete matches, all modes, save/resume/update cycles, physical phones/laptops, multiplayer failure scenarios, and accessibility reviews pass the agreed release checklist. Record remaining limitations instead of labeling unchecked areas complete. |
    
    Performance, regression testing, and human feedback run throughout these passes; they are not postponed until the end.
    
    ## Recommended next release
    
    Start with Pass 1 and the most visible parts of Pass 2:
    
    1. Global production overview and multi-building training are implemented. Configurable hotkeys and queued-order feedback are now implemented; continue with group cohesion, obstacle recovery, and full-match input testing.
    2. Continue control refinements with profile management, selection priority, and accessibility reviews.
    3. Improve group movement through gates, around buildings, and over bridges; show blocked-order feedback.
    4. Refine the implemented AI plans with expansion, resource exhaustion recovery, siege protection, and human difficulty tuning.
    5. Exercise complete economy-to-victory matches with several seeds and difficulties, followed by laptop and phone playtests.
    
    Deliver these as tested releases that can be played and reviewed. Additional units or prettier screenshots alone do not establish overall game quality.
    
    ## What can be developed here and what needs outside evidence
    
    The existing workspace supports implementation of gameplay, AI, UI, asset integration, shaders, animation, performance instrumentation, testing, and multiplayer services. Professional asset/audio production requires suitable original work or licensed sources. Physical-device results require access to the actual devices or measurements from testers. Public online operation requires a hosting decision and ongoing service resources. Fun and balance require repeated human playtesting.
    
    No honest development process can promise an objective “100% world-class” score. The useful commitment is to finish defined requirements, publish test evidence, address player feedback, and improve successive releases.

Used as a genre quality reference, not a statement of this project's implemented features.
    - [Official Age of Empires IV Season Two development notes](https://www.ageofempires.com/news/age-of-empires-iv-update-17718/): continued iteration across controls, game modes, multiplayer, and stability.
    - The baseline above is supported by the local source, [README](README.md), [change log](CHANGELOG.md), and tests/scripts in this repository.
    # Version 2.4 verification
    
    Checked 10 October 2026. This records observed checks, rather than a claim that all possible bugs or all device configurations have been ruled out.
    
    ## Automated game checks
    
    `npm test`: **118 passed, zero failed**. Coverage includes paid gathering/construction/training/research; ages and civilization restrictions; counters, healing and siege; walls, gates and bridges; fleets and transports; all modes and staged campaigns; checkpoints and save compatibility; production batches; custom alliances, large-map fog/navigation/picking, each victory rule, independent AI clocks, seeded weather, real WebSocket rooms, shore-aware invasion targets, fleet population reserves, visible work animations, solid cargo/tree transforms, secure hosted endpoints and canceled reconnect timers.
    
    Eight simultaneous real WebSocket clients exercised readiness, private economies and fog, command ownership, reconnect recovery, host elimination and alliance results. Mixed human/AI rooms also passed. These tests use isolated services and do not modify live player rooms.
    
    ## Custom battle and 3D checks
    
    `scripts/custom-battle-qa.mjs` passed in a real Edge renderer with desktop and emulated landscape-phone layouts:
    
    - Huge 400 × 400 battlefield, eight kingdoms, independent AI difficulty and eight army materials.
    - Actual terrain clicks beyond the former ±160 picking limit and full-map radar navigation.
    - Deferred unseen-mesh allocation, persistent objective scrolling/rules, and custom save/resume with a paid training queue.
    - Volumetric rain with three effect draw calls; quality-limited snow, weather settings and optional lightning.
    - Square minimap, touch interaction and no horizontal page overflow at 844 × 390.
    
    `scripts/custom-multiplayer-qa.mjs` passed with desktop and phone-sized browsers, a third real WebSocket commander and an AI kingdom: guest slot choice, host/guest readiness, private local perspectives, rejected foreign commands, phone production, reload/rejoin, host defeat without ending the match, and correct alliance victory/defeat.
    
    The machine reports approximately 4 GB RAM. Three simultaneous 3D browser contexts timed out without a JavaScript error; a later two-renderer run also timed out during startup. The current mixed-room check keeps two browser connections, suspends rendering in the background desktop host, actively renders the landscape-phone client, and connects a third real WebSocket commander. This is not a simultaneous multi-device FPS measurement. Failed attempts remain recorded in the browser report. A reconnect assertion was corrected to count both queued and completed paid units in the received resume state, because production can finish while a cold browser redraws.
    
    `scripts/interactions-qa.mjs` passed actual harvesting, carried logs/sacks/ingots/rocks, tree falls and persistent stumps, ore depletion, one-time town-center model replacement per age change, huge-map fog/grass coverage and landscape-phone camera interaction. The scene contains no sprites. Four repeated Huge winter matches held GPU counts at **245 geometries and 11 textures** in this fixture. Cargo/stumps used at most five extra draw calls. This follows Three.js's [explicit resource disposal guidance](https://threejs.org/manual/pages/how-to-dispose-of-objects.html) and [mesh batching guidance](https://threejs.org/manual/pages/optimize-lots-of-objects.html).
    
    ## Full-match diagnostic
    
    `scripts/battle-benchmark.mjs`, seed 512, Huge highlands, eight Hard AI kingdoms, standard resources and an 80-person cap:
    
    - Started with the normal economy. The diagnostic alone assigned AI control to the normal human slot.
    - All kingdoms reached Imperial Age. The winning alliance eliminated every opposing building through normal production and combat, finishing at **977.4 simulated seconds** (about 16 minutes).
    - CPU-only simulation tick times: median **10.44 ms**, p95 **21.24 ms**, p99 **30.10 ms**, maximum **65.68 ms** on this run. These are simulation timings, not rendered FPS or phone timings.
    - An earlier pre-optimization match also reached a normal result after about 29 simulated minutes. Battle length is situational, without a forced minimum timer.
    
    Recorded artifacts include `artifacts/battle-benchmark-highlands.json`, the earlier baseline/pre-route-cache reports, custom browser JSON reports and screenshots.
    
    The expanded coastal audit initially exposed stalled cross-shore orders, repeated harbor losses and fleet recruitment starvation. After the fixes, the eight-Hard-AI Huge coast diagnostic reached normal all-building victory at **1138.8 simulated seconds** (about 19 minutes), with all kingdoms reaching Imperial Age. It used standard starting resources, paid production and actual combat. The earlier fleet-fix run also reached victory at 778.5 seconds; flanking strategy changed the final battle's course. The final report is `artifacts/battle-benchmark-coast.json`, with failed/stalled earlier runs retained separately. It ran alongside browser checks on this low-memory machine: median tick 12.86 ms, p95 73.86 ms and a 2.51-second maximum under contention. These timings are not a standalone performance baseline or evidence of smooth phone FPS.
    
    ## Corrections made during the audit
    
    Corrected outer-map picking, resource/harbor overlap, coastal resource access, final-load delivery after deposits/shoals are exhausted, sustained AI attack orders, final-building visibility for AI, naval boarding reservations, individual AI ownership/budgets, private research/error notices and objective scroll resets. I chose **Render because it can host the game and its running multiplayer server in one deployment**, including WebSocket connections. Here are the direct answers:

- **Fully free?** It has a Free plan, with **750 server hours per workspace each month**, plus bandwidth and build limits. Without a payment method, exceeding chargeable allowances causes suspension rather than overage billing.
- **No expiry?** The free **web service has recurring monthly allowances**, rather than a fixed trial expiry. Its separate free database expires after 30 days; our deployment does not use that database. Pricing and terms can still change.
- **Always available immediately?** It sleeps after **15 minutes without traffic** and takes about **one minute to wake**. Free services can also restart. [Official free-plan limits](https://render.com/docs/free)

**Deployment is straightforward:** upload the project to GitHub, connect it through **Render → New → Blueprint**, confirm **Free**, and deploy. I prepared `render.yaml` to fill in the settings. [Blueprint documentation](https://render.com/docs/blueprint-spec)

It suits a free testing release. Unlimited, uninterrupted multiplayer hosting is not guaranteed.

    # Free deployment
    
    Use **Render Free Web Service** for the simplest complete deployment: one URL serves the game and its real-person multiplayer rooms. The included [render.yaml](render.yaml) fills in the build, start, free plan, and health-check settings.
    
    1. Put this project in its own GitHub repository, with `package.json` and `render.yaml` at the root. Do not upload `node_modules`, test artifacts, or local `.env` files.
    2. Sign in to Render, select **New > Blueprint**, and connect that repository.
    3. Confirm that the service plan is **Free**, then deploy. Share the resulting HTTPS `onrender.com` address with players. No separate multiplayer URL or database is needed.
    
    If using **New > Web Service** instead, choose Node, the Free plan, build command `npm ci --include=dev && npm run build`, start command `npm start`, and health-check path `/health`. The server reads Render's `PORT` automatically. Use one instance because rooms are currently kept in memory.
    
    The web-service free tier uses recurring monthly allowances, rather than a fixed trial expiry. It provides 750 instance hours per workspace each month, sleeps after 15 idle minutes, and takes about a minute to wake. Active incoming WebSocket messages count as traffic. Free services can restart, ending live rooms; local single-player saves stay in the player's browser. Bandwidth and build limits also apply. Keep the Free plan and avoid adding a payment method if you want services suspended at chargeable usage limits instead of overage billing. No database is provisioned, so the separate 30-day free database expiry does not apply. Provider terms may change.
    
    This is a free hobby/testing deployment, with limited server CPU. Eight large kingdoms or many simultaneous rooms require hosted performance validation. Free hosting does not establish unlimited capacity or uninterrupted public-game service.
    
    The free deployment defaults to Singapore for Philippine players and one simultaneous multiplayer room to fit the small server. A room still supports up to eight kingdoms. Solo games run on each player's device and do not consume multiplayer rooms. `MAX_ROOMS` can be changed later after measuring server capacity. No account secrets or payment information are stored in the deployment file.
    
    Sources checked 10 October 2026: [free-tier limits](https://render.com/docs/free), [WebSocket support](https://render.com/docs/websocket), [Blueprint configuration](https://render.com/docs/blueprint-spec).
    
    ## Optional Netlify frontend
    
    Netlify can host solo/AI gameplay with the included [netlify.toml](netlify.toml): build `npm run build`, publish `dist`. A static-only build reports that online multiplayer is unavailable while solo modes continue working.
    
    To enable multiplayer from Netlify, set `VITE_MULTIPLAYER_URL=wss://YOUR_RENDER_SERVICE.onrender.com/socket` in the Netlify build environment. On the separate Node service, set `ALLOWED_ORIGINS=https://YOUR_SITE.netlify.app`. Add any custom frontend domain as another comma-separated exact origin, then rebuild/redeploy the frontend. These are public endpoint settings, not credentials. HTTPS sites require secure `wss://` connections.
    
    Netlify's build command and output directory follow its [official Vite guide](https://docs.netlify.com/build/frameworks/framework-setup-guides/vite/). The existing authoritative Node simulation remains a running web service; it is not executed by uploading `dist` to a static host.

## Assistant

To deploy the **current beta** on Render:

1. **Download and extract** [the game source ZIP](C:/New/Age_Of_Emprire/artifacts/crowns-of-the-frontier-2.4-source.zip).

2. Go to [GitHub](https://github.com/new) and create a repository named **age_of_empire**.

3. Choose **Add file → Upload files**. Upload the extracted files and folders, then click **Commit changes**. Upload the contents, **not the ZIP**. `package.json` and `render.yaml` must appear directly inside the repository.

4. Sign in to [Render](https://dashboard.render.com/), connect your GitHub account, and choose **New → Blueprint**.

5. Select your repository. The prepared `render.yaml` fills in the settings. Confirm the plan says **Free**, then click **Deploy Blueprint**. [Official instructions](https://render.com/docs/infrastructure-as-code)

6. Wait until the service says **Live**, then open its **HTTPS `onrender.com` address**.

Use that address on your laptop and phone. Once deployed, your laptop does **not** need to keep the local server running. Friends open the same address and join multiplayer using your room code.

    Provide current, cited OpenAI product, API, model, and Codex guidance. Read zero or one primary reference.

Otherwise, immediately use official-domain web search, then actually open or fetch the relevant official page. Complete this source order before reading a reference, inspecting local or repository files, running a Codex manual or model resolver, drafting a plan, or answering from memory. Use the actual fetched page, not a search snippet or an unopened link. If one official search or page does not establish the answer, search another appropriate official domain and actually open or fetch the result. Preserve the exact requested model; never substitute a newer model.
    
    **Only exception:** An explicitly requested, genuinely broad, cross-topic Codex setup, orientation, or system-map synthesis may use the manual first when shell execution and an allowed temporary cache are available. A specific Codex feature, setting, command, error, model, or requested citation remains docs-first. Mixed Chat/Work/Codex comparisons are official documentation questions, not manual-first Codex requests.

Prioritize `learn.chatgpt.com` for ChatGPT Work.

    - **Model selection and comparisons:** Read [model-selection.md](references/model-selection.md) only when nuanced current, latest, default, cost, latency, quality, or modality tradeoffs need more guidance. Do not run a migration resolver for selection alone.

    - **Explicitly broad Codex setup, orientation, or cross-topic synthesis:** Read [codex-self-knowledge.md](references/codex-self-knowledge.md) when the eligible Codex manual or deeper Codex procedures are needed.

    ### `codex mcp`
    
    Manage Model Context Protocol server entries stored in `~/.codex/config.toml`.
    
    <ConfigTable client:load options={mcpCommands} />
    
    The `add` subcommand supports both stdio and streamable HTTP transports:
    
    <ConfigTable client:load options={mcpAddOptions} />
    
    OAuth actions (`login`, `logout`) only work with streamable HTTP servers (and only when the server supports OAuth).

## Assistant

**You handle the initial installation and connection; I handle creating and integrating the game’s 3D assets.** You don’t need to learn modeling first.

1. **Install Blender** using the Windows installer from the [official Blender download page](https://www.blender.org/download/). Blender is free.

2. **Open PowerShell** and run this command. Your laptop already has `uvx` installed:

   ```powershell
   uvx mcp-for-blender setup
   ```

3. **Choose Codex** when the setup asks which AI application to connect. Follow its prompts to install and enable the Blender add-on. This uses the [community MCP for Blender connector](https://github.com/ahujasid/mcp-for-blender).

4. **Fully close and reopen Codex**, then open Blender. Inside Blender’s 3D viewport, press **N**, find **MCP for Blender**, and click **Start MCP Server** if it isn’t running.

5. **Return to this conversation once setup finishes.** I’ll verify that the Blender tools are available before using them.

After connection, I can create detailed buildings, trees, characters, materials, and animations; export optimized **GLB** models; and integrate them into the game. We’ll start with a town center, an animated villager, and trees so we can verify appearance and performance before expanding.

**Blender creates the assets; Three.js continues running the interactive game.** Players on phones and laptops won’t need Blender installed. Better models still require integration and testing to produce smooth gameplay.

    name: plugin-management

Use when the user asks about plugins or when a task would materially benefit from an external app, account, service, or data source that available tools cannot access.
    ---
    
    # Plugin Management
    
    Use the Plugin Management app to discover useful integrations and manage
    existing plugins. Choose the most direct capability for the user's task before
    searching for anything new.
    
    ## Choose the right capability
    
    1. Use an available built-in tool when it already provides the needed
       capability. General web search, image generation, memory, and sites do not
       require a plugin unless the user requests a specific external provider or a
       capability unavailable natively.
    2. Use an already connected plugin when it can complete the task.
    3. Search for a plugin when an external app, account, service, or data source
       would materially improve the result and no available tool can access it.
    
    Infer plugin intent from the user's actual task. Requests involving email,
    calendars, messaging, documents, project management, customer systems, finance,
    or analytics may need an external integration even when the user never says
    "plugin," "install," or "connect."
    
    Before saying an external service is unavailable, requesting pasted data, or
    proposing a manual workaround, determine whether a relevant plugin exists.
    
    ## Find and suggest plugins
    
    Call `search_plugins` with concise provider names, product names, or capability
    keywords. For example, use `Gmail`, `calendar`, or `project management`, not
    the entire user request. The currently available tools and any recommended
    plugin list are not a complete directory.
    
    When a relevant unconnected plugin would help, call `suggest_plugins` with its
    exact returned plugin ID. Suggest the smallest useful set, preferably three or
    fewer. Do not suggest plugins that are already installed or already pending.
    
    Suggestions do not block the task. Continue any work that does not require the
    connection and briefly explain what still needs the user's action. Never claim
    a plugin is installed or connected without verification. Use its tools only
    after its individual connection is confirmed.
    
    ## Manage existing plugins
    
    - Use `get_app_permissions` to inspect a plugin's permissions.
    - Use `update_app_permissions` only for a permission change the user requested.
      Ask before ambiguous, broad, or risky changes.
    - Use `get_plugin_dependencies` to inspect required apps or dependencies.
    - Use `uninstall_app` only when the user explicitly requests removal. Correct
      an obvious spelling mistake when the intended plugin is unambiguous, and pass
      its actual name without inventing an identifier.
    
    Keep user-facing explanations focused on the task, connection state, and
    requested change. Do not expose internal tool names or claim actions happened
    without checking their results.

    """
    Bundle, install, and version-check the MCP for Blender addon.
    
    Existing users often update only the MCP server (`uvx mcp-for-blender`). This module:
    1. Ships a bundled copy of addon.py inside the package
    2. Can copy it into Blender's user addons directory (`install-addon`)
    3. Handshake with a running addon to detect outdated installs
    """
    
    from __future__ import annotations
    
    import logging
    import os
    import re
    import shutil
    import sys
    from dataclasses import dataclass, field
    from pathlib import Path
    
    logger = logging.getLogger("BlenderMCPServer")
    
    # Must match ADDON_PROTOCOL_VERSION in addon.py / bundled/addon.py
    EXPECTED_ADDON_PROTOCOL_VERSION = 13
    
    _ADDON_MARKER = 'bl_info = {\n    "name": "MCP for Blender"'
    _INSTALLED_FILENAME = "blender_mcp.py"
    _PROTOCOL_RE = re.compile(r"ADDON_PROTOCOL_VERSION\s*=\s*(\d+)")
    _BL_INFO_VERSION_RE = re.compile(r'"version":\s*\((\d+)\s*,\s*(\d+)(?:\s*,\s*(\d+))?\s*\)')
    # Matches the current name and the pre-rename "Blender MCP" so install-addon
    # still replaces installs from older releases.
    _BL_INFO_NAME_RE = re.compile(
        r"""["']name["']\s*:\s*["'](?:MCP for Blender|Blender MCP)["']"""
    )
    
    
    def read_addon_protocol_version(path: Path) -> int | None:
        """Parse ADDON_PROTOCOL_VERSION from an installed addon file."""
        try:
            text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore")
        except OSError:
            return None
        match = _PROTOCOL_RE.search(text)
        if not match:
            return None
        try:
            return int(match.group(1))
        except ValueError:
            return None
    
    
    def addon_file_needs_update(path: Path) -> bool:
        """True if path is missing protocol metadata or behind the bundled addon."""
        if not path.is_file():
            return True
        installed = read_addon_protocol_version(path)
        if installed is None:
            return True
        return installed < EXPECTED_ADDON_PROTOCOL_VERSION
    
    
    @dataclass
    class AddonStatusReport:
        """Read-only view of the addon files on disk versus the bundled copy."""
    
        checked: bool
        outdated_paths: list[str]
        missing: bool
        message: str
        reason: str | None = None
    
        @property
        def needs_action(self) -> bool:
            return bool(self.outdated_paths) or self.missing
    
    
    _UPDATE_HINT = (
        "Run `uvx mcp-for-blender install-addon` to update it, then in Blender: "
        "Preferences → Add-ons → disable and re-enable 'Interface: MCP for Blender' "
        "(or restart Blender) and click Start MCP Server."
    )
    
    
    def check_addon_status_on_startup() -> AddonStatusReport:
        """
        Report whether the on-disk Blender addon is behind the bundled copy.
    
        Deliberately read-only. Starting an MCP server is not a request to modify
        files in the user's Blender configuration, and a silent overwrite at an
        unrelated moment can discard local edits with no prompt and no undo. We
        detect and tell; `install-addon` does the writing, when the user asks.
        Never raises; safe to call from server lifespan.
        """
        try:
            dirs = discover_blender_addon_dirs()
            if not dirs:
                return AddonStatusReport(
                    checked=False,
                    outdated_paths=[],
                    missing=False,
                    reason="no_addons_dir",
                    message=(
                        "Could not find a Blender addons folder. If Blender is "
                        "installed, set BLENDERMCP_ADDONS_DIR, or install addon.py "
                        "manually from the repo."
                    ),
                )
    
            existing = find_existing_addon_installs(dirs)
            if not existing:
                return AddonStatusReport(
                    checked=True,
                    outdated_paths=[],
                    missing=True,
                    reason="not_installed",
                    message=(
                        "MCP for Blender addon not found in any Blender addons folder. "
                        "Run `uvx mcp-for-blender install-addon` to install it."
                    ),
                )
    
            outdated = [str(p) for p in existing if addon_file_needs_update(p)]
            if not outdated:
                return AddonStatusReport(
                    checked=True,
                    outdated_paths=[],
                    missing=False,
                    reason="already_current",
                    message=(
                        f"Blender addon on disk is current "
                        f"(protocol {EXPECTED_ADDON_PROTOCOL_VERSION})."
                    ),
                )
    
            return AddonStatusReport(
                checked=True,
                outdated_paths=outdated,
                missing=False,
                reason="outdated",
                message=(
                    f"MCP for Blender addon on disk is outdated (expected protocol "
                    f"{EXPECTED_ADDON_PROTOCOL_VERSION}): {', '.join(outdated)}. "
                    + _UPDATE_HINT
                ),
            )
        except Exception as e:
            logger.debug(f"Addon status check failed: {e}")
            return AddonStatusReport(
                checked=False,
                outdated_paths=[],
                missing=False,
                reason="error",
                message=f"Could not check Blender addon status: {e}",
            )
    
    
    @dataclass
    class AddonInstallResult:
        success: bool
        message: str
        target_path: str | None = None
        addons_dir: str | None = None
    
    
    @dataclass
    class AddonHandshake:
        up_to_date: bool
        protocol_version: int | None
        addon_version: list[int] | None
        capabilities: list[str]
        blender_version: str | None
        source: str  # native | missing | error
        warning: str | None = None
        premium_generators: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    
    
    def get_bundled_addon_path() -> Path:
        """Resolve the addon.py shipped with this package (or repo root in editable installs)."""
        here = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
        candidates = [
            here / "bundled" / "addon.py",
            here.parents[1] / "addon.py",  # repo root when running from src layout
        ]
        for path in candidates:
            if path.is_file():
                return path
        raise FileNotFoundError(
            "Bundled MCP for Blender addon.py not found. Reinstall mcp-for-blender or "
            "copy addon.py from the GitHub repo into Blender manually."
        )
    
    
    def blender_config_base() -> Path | None:
        """Blender's per-user folder, which holds one subfolder per version (4.2, 4.3, ...)."""
        home = Path.home()
        if sys.platform == "darwin":
            return home / "Library" / "Application Support" / "Blender"
        if sys.platform == "win32":
            appdata = os.environ.get("APPDATA")
            return Path(appdata) / "Blender Foundation" / "Blender" if appdata else None
        return home / ".config" / "blender"
    
    
    def discover_blender_addon_dirs() -> list[Path]:
        """Find Blender user scripts/addons directories across versions."""
        dirs: list[Path] = []
        base = blender_config_base()
    
        if base and base.is_dir():
            for child in sorted(base.iterdir(), reverse=True):
                if not child.is_dir():
                    continue
                # Blender versions look like 3.6, 4.0, 4.2
                if not re.match(r"^\d+\.\d+", child.name):
                    continue
                dirs.append(child / "scripts" / "addons")
                # Blender 4.2+ installs through the extensions system.
                extensions = child / "extensions" / "user_default"
                if extensions.is_dir():
                    dirs.append(extensions)
    
        env = os.environ.get("BLENDER_USER_ADDONS") or os.environ.get("BLENDERMCP_ADDONS_DIR")
        if env:
            env_path = Path(env).expanduser()
            dirs.insert(0, env_path)
    
        seen: set[str] = set()
        unique: list[Path] = []
        for d in dirs:
            key = str(d)
            if key not in seen:
                seen.add(key)
                unique.append(d)
        return unique
    
    
    def _is_blendermcp_addon_file(path: Path) -> bool:
        """True only for a file whose bl_info declares it as the MCP for Blender addon.
    
        Deliberately narrower than a substring search for "BlenderMCPServer": that
        also matches a user's own fork or a script that merely references the class,
        and install_addon overwrites everything this returns True for.
        """
        try:
            text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore")
        except OSError:
            return False
        return _BL_INFO_NAME_RE.search(text) is not None
    
    
    def find_existing_addon_installs(addons_dirs: list[Path] | None = None) -> list[Path]:
        """Locate already-installed MCP for Blender addon files."""
        found: list[Path] = []
        for addons_dir in addons_dirs or discover_blender_addon_dirs():
            if not addons_dir.is_dir():
                continue
            for path in addons_dir.iterdir():
                if path.is_file() and path.suffix == ".py" and _is_blendermcp_addon_file(path):
                    found.append(path)
                elif path.is_dir() and (path / "__init__.py").is_file():
                    init = path / "__init__.py"
                    if _is_blendermcp_addon_file(init):
                        found.append(init)
        return found
    
    
    def _backup_addon_file(path: Path, source: Path | None = None) -> Path | None:
        """Keep one .bak copy before overwriting, so local edits are recoverable.
    
        Skipped when the file already matches what we are about to write: a repeat
        install would otherwise overwrite a .bak holding the user's real previous
        version with an identical copy of the bundled addon, destroying the very
        edits the backup exists to preserve.
        """
        if not path.is_file():
            return None
        if source is not None:
            try:
                if path.read_bytes() == source.read_bytes():
                    return None
            except OSError as e:
                logger.debug(f"Could not compare {path} with {source}: {e}")
        backup = path.with_suffix(path.suffix + ".bak")
        try:
            shutil.copy2(path, backup)
            return backup
        except OSError as e:
            logger.debug(f"Could not back up {path}: {e}")
            return None
    
    
    def install_addon(
        addons_dir: Path | None = None,
        *,
        create_dir: bool = True,
    ) -> AddonInstallResult:
        """
        Copy the bundled addon into Blender's user addons folder.
    
        Replaces known existing MCP for Blender addon files in that directory.
        User must disable/enable the addon or restart Blender to load the new code.
        """
        try:
            source = get_bundled_addon_path()
        except FileNotFoundError as e:
            return AddonInstallResult(False, str(e))
    
        if addons_dir is None:
            dirs = discover_blender_addon_dirs()
            if not dirs:
                return AddonInstallResult(
                    False,
                    "Could not find a Blender user addons directory. "
                    "Set BLENDERMCP_ADDONS_DIR to your Blender scripts/addons path, "
                    "or install addon.py manually from the repo.",
                )
            # Update where the addon already lives rather than the newest
            # scripts/addons dir.
            existing = find_existing_addon_installs(dirs)
            addons_dir = existing[0].parent if existing else dirs[0]
    
        addons_dir = Path(addons_dir).expanduser()
        if not addons_dir.exists():
            if not create_dir:
                return AddonInstallResult(
                    False,
                    f"Addons directory does not exist: {addons_dir}",
                    addons_dir=str(addons_dir),
                )
            try:
                addons_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            except OSError as e:
                return AddonInstallResult(
                    False,
                    f"Failed to create addons directory {addons_dir}: {e}",
                    addons_dir=str(addons_dir),
                )
    
        replaced: list[str] = []
        if addons_dir.is_dir():
            for path in list(addons_dir.iterdir()):
                if path.is_file() and path.suffix == ".py" and _is_blendermcp_addon_file(path):
                    _backup_addon_file(path, source)
                    shutil.copy2(source, path)
                    replaced.append(str(path))
    
        target = addons_dir / _INSTALLED_FILENAME
        if str(target) not in replaced:
            _backup_addon_file(target, source)
            shutil.copy2(source, target)
            replaced.append(str(target))
    
        msg = (
            f"Installed MCP for Blender addon to {target}. "
            "In Blender: Preferences → Add-ons → disable then enable "
            "'Interface: MCP for Blender', or restart Blender, then click Start MCP Server."
        )
        if len(replaced) > 1:
            msg += f" Also updated: {', '.join(replaced[:-1])}."
    
        return AddonInstallResult(
            True,
            msg,
            target_path=str(target),
            addons_dir=str(addons_dir),
        )
    
    
    def addon_release_key(text: str) -> tuple[int, int, int, int] | None:
        """(major, minor, patch, protocol) of an addon file's text; mirrors addon.py's own."""
        bl_info_at = text.find("bl_info = {")
        if bl_info_at < 0:
            return None
        version = _BL_INFO_VERSION_RE.search(text, bl_info_at)
        protocol = _PROTOCOL_RE.search(text)
        if not version or not protocol:
            return None
        return (
            int(version.group(1)),
            int(version.group(2)),
            int(version.group(3) or 0),
            int(protocol.group(1)),
        )
    
    
    def addon_version_label(key: tuple[int, int, int, int] | None) -> str:
        if key is None:
            return "an older release"
        major, minor, patch, _protocol = key
        return f"{major}.{minor}.{patch}" if patch else f"{major}.{minor}"
    
    
    @dataclass
    class AddonUpdate:
        path: Path
        # updated | current | newer | failed (dry runs report updated without writing)
        action: str
        installed: tuple[int, int, int, int] | None
        detail: str = ""
    
    
    def update_installed_addons(
        addons_dirs: list[Path] | None = None,
        *,
        dry_run: bool = False,
    ) -> list[AddonUpdate]:
        """Bring every installed copy of the addon up to the bundled release, in place.
    
        Unlike install_addon, this writes only over files that already exist, and
        never downgrades: the addon's own updater pulls from the main branch, so an
        installed copy can be ahead of the release this package bundles. A copy at
        the same release but with different bytes is left alone too, since the
        difference is someone's local edit.
        """
        source = get_bundled_addon_path()
        source_bytes = source.read_bytes()
        bundled = addon_release_key(source_bytes.decode("utf-8", errors="ignore"))
    
        results: list[AddonUpdate] = []
        for path in find_existing_addon_installs(addons_dirs):
            try:
                data = path.read_bytes()
            except OSError as e:
                results.append(AddonUpdate(path, "failed", None, str(e)))
                continue
            installed = addon_release_key(data.decode("utf-8", errors="ignore"))
            if data == source_bytes:
                results.append(AddonUpdate(path, "current", installed))
                continue
            # A file without a readable key passed the bl_info name check, so it is
            # the addon from before versions were stamped (or the old "Blender MCP").
            if installed is not None and bundled is not None and installed >= bundled:
                action = "newer" if installed > bundled else "current"
                results.append(AddonUpdate(path, action, installed))
                continue
            if not dry_run:
                try:
                    _backup_addon_file(path, source)
                    shutil.copy2(source, path)
                except OSError as e:
                    results.append(AddonUpdate(path, "failed", installed, str(e)))
                    continue
            results.append(AddonUpdate(path, "updated", installed))
        return results
    
    
    def handshake_addon(blender_connection) -> AddonHandshake:
        """
        Query a connected Blender addon for protocol version.
    
        Old addons without get_addon_info are treated as outdated (but still usable
        via execute_code fallbacks elsewhere).
        """
        try:
            info = blender_connection.send_command("get_addon_info")
            if not isinstance(info, dict):
                return AddonHandshake(
                    up_to_date=False,
                    protocol_version=None,
                    addon_version=None,
                    capabilities=[],
                    blender_version=None,
                    source="error",
                    warning="Addon returned invalid get_addon_info payload.",
                )
            protocol = info.get("protocol_version")
            try:
                protocol_i = int(protocol) if protocol is not None else None
            except (TypeError, ValueError):
                protocol_i = None
    
            up_to_date = (
                protocol_i is not None and protocol_i >= EXPECTED_ADDON_PROTOCOL_VERSION
            )
            warning = None
            if not up_to_date:
                warning = (
                    f"Blender addon protocol {protocol_i!r} is behind "
                    f"expected {EXPECTED_ADDON_PROTOCOL_VERSION}. "
                    "Run `uvx mcp-for-blender install-addon` to update it, then "
                    "restart Blender or disable/enable 'Interface: MCP for Blender', "
                    "then Start MCP Server. Trajectory still works via fallbacks."
                )
            return AddonHandshake(
                up_to_date=up_to_date,
                protocol_version=protocol_i,
                addon_version=info.get("addon_version"),
                capabilities=list(info.get("capabilities") or []),
                blender_version=info.get("blender_version"),
                source="native",
                warning=warning,
                premium_generators=list(info.get("premium_generators") or []),
            )
        except Exception as e:
            msg = str(e).lower()
            if "unknown command" in msg or "get_addon_info" in msg:
                warning = (
                    "Blender addon is outdated (no get_addon_info). "
                    "Run `uvx mcp-for-blender install-addon` to update it, then "
                    "restart Blender or disable/enable 'Interface: MCP for Blender', "
                    "then Start MCP Server. Fallbacks keep working in the meantime."
                )
                return AddonHandshake(
                    up_to_date=False,
                    protocol_version=None,
                    addon_version=None,
                    capabilities=[],
                    blender_version=None,
                    source="missing",
                    warning=warning,
                )
            return AddonHandshake(
                up_to_date=False,
                protocol_version=None,
                addon_version=None,
                capabilities=[],
                blender_version=None,
                source="error",
                warning=f"Addon handshake failed: {e}",
            )
    
    
    def format_handshake_log(result: AddonHandshake) -> str:
        if result.up_to_date:
            return (
                f"Blender addon up to date "
                f"(protocol {result.protocol_version}, "
                f"addon {result.addon_version}, "
                f"Blender {result.blender_version})"
            )
        return result.warning or "Blender addon may be outdated."
    
    
    def run_cli(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
        """CLI entry for install-addon / addon-paths / setup / update. Returns process exit code."""
        import argparse
    
        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
            prog="mcp-for-blender",
            description="MCP for Blender server and addon installer",
        )
        # Declared here only so they show up in `mcp-for-blender --help`; the server
        # entry point parses them itself (see server.parse_connection_args), since
        # this CLI returns -1 and exits before the no-subcommand case reaches them.
        parser.add_argument(
            "--host",
            type=str,
            default=None,
            help="Host of the Blender socket server (overrides BLENDER_HOST)",
        )
        parser.add_argument(
            "--port",
            type=int,
            default=None,
            help="Port of the Blender socket server (overrides BLENDER_PORT)",
        )
        sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command")
    
        install_p = sub.add_parser(
            "install-addon",
            help="Copy the bundled addon.py into Blender's user addons folder",
        )
        install_p.add_argument(
            "--addons-dir",
            type=str,
            default=None,
            help="Override Blender scripts/addons directory "
            "(or set BLENDERMCP_ADDONS_DIR)",
        )
    
        sub.add_parser(
            "addon-paths",
            help="List discovered Blender user addons directories",
        )
    
        setup_p = sub.add_parser(
            "setup",
            help="Configure your MCP clients and install and enable the Blender addon",
        )
        setup_p.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true", help="Show what would change without changing anything")
        setup_p.add_argument("--yes", "-y", action="store_true", help="Configure every client found without asking")
        setup_p.add_argument("--skip-addon", action="store_true", help="Configure clients only; leave Blender alone")
    
        update_p = sub.add_parser(
            "update",
            help="Update the MCP server and the installed Blender addon to the latest release",
        )
        update_p.add_argument("--dry-run", action="store_true", help="Show what would change without changing anything")
    
        args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    
        if args.command == "update":
            from .update_cli import run_update
    
            return run_update(dry_run=args.dry_run)
    
        if args.command == "setup":
            from .setup_cli import run_setup
    
            return run_setup(dry_run=args.dry_run, assume_yes=args.yes, skip_addon=args.skip_addon)
    
        if args.command == "install-addon":
            result = install_addon(
                Path(args.addons_dir) if args.addons_dir else None,
            )
            print(result.message)
            return 0 if result.success else 1
    
        if args.command == "addon-paths":
            dirs = discover_blender_addon_dirs()
            if not dirs:
                print("No Blender addons directories found.")
                return 1
            for d in dirs:
                marker = " (exists)" if d.is_dir() else " (missing)"
                print(f"{d}{marker}")
            existing = find_existing_addon_installs(dirs)
            if existing:
                print("\nExisting MCP for Blender installs:")
                for p in existing:
                    print(f"  {p}")
            return 0
    
        # No subcommand → caller should start MCP server
        return -1
