    # Crowns of the Frontier: quality roadmap
    
    Reviewed 10 October 2026 against the version 2.4 source and current verification scripts.
    
    This is an ordered development proposal, not a claim that its milestones have been implemented. The current game is a playable beta. A world-class assessment needs independent player feedback, reliable performance, strong content, and sustained quality across complete matches.
    
    ## Current baseline
    
    - Three.js world with elevated terrain, solid building/unit/resource models, articulated parts, animated water, and 3D selection portraits.
    - Resource gathering, construction, queues, upgrades, ages, unit counters, siege, healing, walls, gates, fleets, transports, fog, saves, and several victory conditions.
    - Nine modes, seven seeded maps, six campaign chapters, three civilizations, 19 building types, and 16 trainable types across the catalog plus sovereigns.
    - Two-to-eight-kingdom custom battles, AI allies/enemies with individual difficulties, human slots, huge maps and three elimination rules.
    - Classic two-player and custom mixed human/AI Wi-Fi rooms with authoritative commands, team perspectives, readiness and reconnection. Rooms are held in server memory; they are not a public matchmaking service.
    - Seeded volumetric weather, pooled effects, optional audio/lightning and quality budgets.
    - Rooted and wind-animated trees, winter snowcaps, harvested tree falls/stumps, batched carried supplies, ore depletion, and age-specific town-center architecture. Huge-map fog and grass cover the full playable area.
    - Free Render deployment configuration for one game/multiplayer service, plus optional Netlify static hosting and a separate secure multiplayer endpoint. Hosting variants have local browser coverage; no public deployment is active.
    - Mouse edge scrolling, corner scrolling, cursor arrows, keyboard controls, camera inspection, and landscape touch input.
    - Square radar with a rectangular camera locator and mouse/touch dragging. Global production overview, selection across completed production buildings, balanced training batches, and cancel/refund controls.
    - Existing automated simulation/graphics/network checks and browser verification. Physical-device performance, balance, and extensive human playtesting remain unverified.
    
    ## Version 2.4 custom-battle progress
    
    - The requested AI and real-human battle configurations are implemented separately in one custom setup. Solo configurations convert the other enabled slots to AI; multiplayer preserves Human slots and allows AI kingdoms alongside them.
    - Huge maps, eight kingdoms, allied gates/healing/shared vision, independent AI economies and planning clocks, capital rebuilding, all-building elimination, optional conquest/capital rules and team victory are implemented.
    - Multiplayer checks include eight real WebSocket participants, private economies and fog, ownership, mixed AI/humans, guest slot choice, readiness, concessions, host defeat, reconnect and winning/losing alliance perspectives.
    - Resource exhaustion, unreachable routes, outer-map picking and private completion notices were corrected during the audit. Cached movement regions, route retention, vision indexing, pooled weather and reduced render cadence address measured CPU/GPU pressure.
    - Coastal armies use their current shore, scout capitals, search remaining settlements, reserve fleet capacity, rebuild harbors, prioritize transports and fill balanced crews. A full eight-kingdom paid coastal war now reaches all-building victory; the final diagnostic lasted about 19 simulated minutes.
    - Keep physical-device performance, multiplayer latency/failure testing and human balance/pacing reviews in the release checklist. The original 3D art remains procedural; commercial world-class parity has not been established.
    
    ## Version 2.3 campaign progress
    
    - Six chapters now have three authored stages each, original dialogue journals, optional completion medals, and active goal markers in the minimap and explored 3D world.
    - The river chapter has a modeled supply caravan, guarded escort navigation, a bridgehead objective, a loss condition, and recovery through frozen checkpoints.
    - Fortress defense requires a completed castle and the wave objectives. Sacred valley supports shrine control or a recorded conquest alternative. Final siege requires paid siege production and a defensive breach. The coastal chapter counts actual deposited fishing catch and accepts a landing or an Imperial siege-galleon route.
    - Initial and stage checkpoints preserve actors, objectives, economy, armies, exploration, and AI state without recursive snapshots. Existing campaign saves retain legacy rules.
    - Automated scenarios use gathering, construction, training, escort movement, shrine control, fishing, and gate attacks to exercise the chapter flows. All four difficulties initialize every chapter. Browser verification covers journals, selecting and inspecting the caravan, locating goals, defeat recovery, local save/resume, and emulated-phone controls.
    
    Pass 4 has a playable scripted baseline. Human completion tests on all difficulties, more mission events and set pieces, professional narration/audio, broader map fairness checks, and mission pacing remain unfinished.
    
    ## Version 2.2 implementation progress
    
    - Saved remappable keyboard controls, reserved-key validation, conflict reporting, active key documentation, and updated shortcut labels.
    - Patrol and guard commands in the simulation, desktop/touch interface, saves, and authoritative network commands. Formation slots avoid blocked terrain. Partial paths no longer count as successful arrival; persistent blocked orders report feedback and yield to queued orders.
    - Selected-unit order summaries and bounded 3D route previews, including patrol return routes and ship routes above the water.
    - Paid AI economy and army planning, civilization-aware counter composition, scouting memory, age-resource reserves, worker reassignment, repairs, retreats, healer escorts, and transport boarding/departure reservations.
    - Three civilization-exclusive units with solid model variants, explicit costs, age/building requirements, and distinct roles. Three exclusive technologies affect armor, market exchange, and cavalry raids. Old saves initialize the new research fields.
    - Interactive technology tree with faction comparison, prerequisite/status explanations, training, and research. Higher-contrast UI, reduced decorative motion, and larger tactical touch buttons.
    - Regression coverage now includes these behaviors. Commander browser checks exercise remapping, persistence, tactics, queued-order feedback without movement lines, save/resume, and desktop/emulated-phone layouts. Passive-player soak checks exercise full land, river, and coastal matches and record simulation CPU timings.
    
    Passes 1 through 3 have concrete implementation progress; they are not fully complete. Group cohesion, advanced recovery, AI expansion, further economy/combat tuning, richer strategic interactions, authored missions, asset/audio production, measured device performance, public online services, and external playtesting remain on the roadmap. Naval regrouping now respects the current island, and movement reaches the actual final waypoint rather than stopping at a grid center. The latest coastal soak reports four blocked orders instead of 74 in the previous diagnostic run; remaining land/bridge cases still need review. CPU timings from automated simulations do not establish rendering FPS, phone performance, or enjoyable difficulty.
    
    ## Development order and release checks
    
    | Pass | Work to implement or improve | Evidence required before declaring the pass complete |
    |---|---|---|
    | 1. Controls and army movement | Remappable hotkeys, selection priority, production across selected buildings, global production queue, queued-command feedback, patrol/guard behaviors, formation cohesion, obstacle avoidance, and recovery from blocked routes. Preserve edge scrolling and touch input. | Repeatable mouse/keyboard/touch scenarios; armies navigate woods, walls, gates, bridges, and crowded towns; no duplicated queued orders or indefinitely stuck troops in the tested cases. Local command feedback and execution latency measured on reference hardware. |
    | 2. Economy, AI, and battle balance | Explicit AI build orders and resource budgets, scouting memory, different attack plans, counter-unit composition, regrouping, retreating, siege protection, expansion, transport decisions, and difficulty based on decisions. Audit starting advantages and any difficulty bonuses. | Seeded economy and combat scenarios; AI can recover after worker losses and exhausted nearby resources; attacks change based on observed enemies; difficulty rules are documented; human testers find each level understandable and challenging. |
    | 3. Civilizations and strategic depth | Build on the implemented exclusive units/technologies, technology tree and eight-kingdom team support with clearer identities, more useful upgrade choices, land/naval counters and alternative economic strategies. | Comparable-cost counter scenarios plus human matches; all additions have costs, prerequisites, counters, descriptions, art, audio, AI support, saves, and multiplayer validation. Balance judged across maps and skill levels. |
    | 4. Missions and map design | A mission-event system with staged objectives, dialogue, reinforcements, escort/rescue tasks, branching optional goals, checkpoints, and authored set pieces. Curate resource placement, chokepoints, naval landings, and spawn fairness. | Each mission can be completed and failed correctly on each difficulty; checkpoints restore the correct event state; missions require different strategies; map objectives and travel routes remain reachable. |
    | 5. Art, animation, and sound | Establish a consistent medieval art direction; replace or refine the procedural assets with original or appropriately licensed authored models, textures, character rigs, transitions, worker tasks, cargo, attack impacts, damage, and death animations. Add distinctive music, unit responses, ambience, and readable combat sound. | Visual review in real gameplay at every quality setting and camera angle; recognizable units and silhouettes; animations match actions; assets fit performance budgets; retain real mesh geometry at every detail level. |
    | 6. Laptop and phone experience | Profile CPU/GPU work, pathfinding, draw calls, memory, network snapshots, and input delay. Improve detail levels, shared routes, batching, effects budgets, loading, safe areas, readable UI, touch selection, UI scaling, and accessibility options. | Publish device/browser/specification results. Proposed targets: 60 FPS on a defined reference laptop and 30 FPS on defined supported phones in benchmark matches. Verify sustained performance, frame-time spikes, thermal behavior, and memory over long sessions. Targets are not current achievements or guarantees for every device. |
    | 7. Multiplayer and community | Extend the implemented team rooms, readiness, authoritative validation, defeat spectating and reconnect recovery with public hosting, persistent rooms, matchmaking, profiles, replays and operational monitoring. | Test multiple clients, latency, packet loss, disconnects, server restarts, ownership, hidden-information handling, version compatibility, and replay results. Hosting choices and ongoing costs need an explicit deployment decision. |
    | 8. Release readiness | Improve onboarding, settings, saved-game migrations, campaign progression, post-match economy/combat graphs, installation/update behavior, diagnostics, recovery, and documentation. Conduct repeated external playtests and fix their highest-impact problems. | Long complete matches, all modes, save/resume/update cycles, physical phones/laptops, multiplayer failure scenarios, and accessibility reviews pass the agreed release checklist. Record remaining limitations instead of labeling unchecked areas complete. |
    
    Performance, regression testing, and human feedback run throughout these passes; they are not postponed until the end.
    
    ## Recommended next release
    
    Start with Pass 1 and the most visible parts of Pass 2:
    
    1. Global production overview and multi-building training are implemented. Configurable hotkeys and queued-order feedback are now implemented; continue with group cohesion, obstacle recovery, and full-match input testing.
    2. Continue control refinements with profile management, selection priority, and accessibility reviews.
    3. Improve group movement through gates, around buildings, and over bridges; show blocked-order feedback.
    4. Refine the implemented AI plans with expansion, resource exhaustion recovery, siege protection, and human difficulty tuning.
    5. Exercise complete economy-to-victory matches with several seeds and difficulties, followed by laptop and phone playtests.
    
    Deliver these as tested releases that can be played and reviewed. Additional units or prettier screenshots alone do not establish overall game quality.
    
    ## What can be developed here and what needs outside evidence

        const group=fighters.filter(e=>Math.sign(e.x)===sign);if(!group.length)continue;const center={x:group.reduce((n,e)=>n+e.x,0)/group.length,z:group.reduce((n,e)=>n+e.z,0)/group.length};

        const target=threat||((phase==='attack'||Math.sign(tc.x)!==sign)&&(capital||unscouted||buildings[0]||search));
        if(target)sim.command(group.map(e=>e.id),{type:'attackmove',x:target.x,z:target.z});
        else{const base=bases.filter(e=>Math.sign(e.x)===sign).sort(nearby)[0],rally=base?{x:base.x+8,z:base.z-6}:{x:Math.sin(center.z*.03)*2+sign*22,z:center.z};for(const unit of group)if(distance(unit,rally)>12)sim.command([unit.id],{type:'move',x:rally.x+(unit.id%4)*1.5,z:rally.z});}

    import {UNITS} from './data.js';
    const clamp=(sim,n)=>Math.max(-sim.halfWorld+3,Math.min(sim.halfWorld-3,n));
    
    // Resolve formation slots on the unit's own movement surface. This keeps edge
    // slots out of foundations and water without sending land troops across a sea.
    export function formationSlot(sim,unit,point){
      const size=sim.gridSize,half=sim.halfWorld,grid=sim.grid(unit.owner,!!UNITS[unit.type].naval),cell=sim.cell(point.x,point.z);
      if(!grid[cell.z*size+cell.x])return {x:clamp(sim,point.x),z:clamp(sim,point.z)};
      let best=null,score=Infinity;
      for(let r=1;r<=4;r++)for(let z=Math.max(0,cell.z-r);z<=Math.min(size-1,cell.z+r);z++)for(let x=Math.max(0,cell.x-r);x<=Math.min(size-1,cell.x+r);x++){
        if(grid[z*size+x])continue;const wx=x*2-half+1,wz=z*2-half+1,s=Math.hypot(wx-point.x,wz-point.z)+Math.hypot(wx-unit.x,wz-unit.z)*.03;
        if(s<score){score=s;best={x:wx,z:wz};}
      }return best||{x:clamp(sim,point.x),z:clamp(sim,point.z)};
    }
    
    export function installTactics(Simulation){
      const p=Simulation.prototype;
      p.patrol=function(ids,x,z,append=false,owner=0){
        if(!Number.isFinite(x)||!Number.isFinite(z))return false;
        const units=ids.map(id=>this.get(id)).filter(e=>e?.owner===owner&&e.kind==='unit'&&!e.embarked&&!['worker','fisher'].includes(UNITS[e.type].role));
        for(const e of units){const target=formationSlot(this,e,{x,z});this.command([e.id],{type:'patrol',...target,originX:e.x,originZ:e.z},append);}
        return units.length>0;
      };
      p.guard=function(ids,targetId,append=false,owner=0){
        const target=this.get(targetId);if(!target||!this.allied(target.owner,owner)||!['unit','building'].includes(target.kind))return false;
        const units=ids.map(id=>this.get(id)).filter(e=>e?.owner===owner&&e.kind==='unit'&&e!==target&&!e.embarked&&!['worker','fisher'].includes(UNITS[e.type].role));
        units.forEach((e,i)=>this.command([e.id],{type:'guard',target:target.id,offsetX:Math.cos(i*2.4)*(target.r+3),offsetZ:Math.sin(i*2.4)*(target.r+3)},append));
        return units.length>0;
      };
      p.setStance=function(ids,stance,owner=0){
        if(!['hold','aggressive'].includes(stance))return false;
        const units=ids.map(id=>this.get(id)).filter(e=>e?.owner===owner&&e.kind==='unit');
        for(const e of units){e.stance=stance;if(stance==='hold'){e.order=null;e.orders=[];e.path=[];e.pathStatus='idle';e.stuckTime=0;}}
        return units.length>0;
      };
    }

    import {formationSlot} from './tactics.js';
    const distance=(a,b)=>Math.hypot(a.x-b.x,a.z-b.z);
    
    export function installFrontiers(Simulation){
      const p=Simulation.prototype,original={};
      for(const method of ['initialize','grid','buildValid','tickUnit','tickBuilding','hurt','smartCommand','assignWorker','tickAI','serialize','addUnit','addBuilding','addResource','addShrine'])original[method]=p[method];
      for(const method of ['addUnit','addBuilding','addResource','addShrine'])p[method]=function(...args){const entity=original[method].apply(this,args);this.index?.set(entity.id,entity);if(['unit','building'].includes(entity.kind))this.sightCache=null;if(entity.kind==='unit'&&UNITS[entity.type].naval)entity.r=entity.type==='warship'?2:1.6;return entity;};
      p.get=function(id){if(!this.index)this.index=new Map(this.entities.map(e=>[e.id,e]));const e=this.index.get(id);return e?.hp>0?e:null;};
      const restore=Simulation.restore;
      Simulation.restore=function(data){const sim=restore.call(this,data);sim.index=new Map(sim.entities.map(e=>[e.id,e]));sim.sightCache=null;for(const player of sim.players)for(const key of Object.keys(TECHS))player.tech[key]??=0;sim.intel=data.intel||{};return sim;};
      p.initialize=function(){this.intel={};if(this.options.mode==='tides')this.options.map='coast';original.initialize.call(this);
        this.players.forEach(player=>{player.tech.seamanship??=0;});
        if(this.options.map==='coast'){
          this.players.forEach(player=>{player.age=Math.max(1,player.age);player.resources.wood+=350;player.resources.gold+=180;});
          for(const owner of [0,1]){
            if(owner===1&&(['sandbox','tutorial','survival'].includes(this.options.mode)||this.mission?.survival))continue;
            const sign=owner===0?-1:1;this.addBuilding('dock',owner,sign*19,owner===0?25:-25,true);
            const boat=this.addUnit('fishingboat',owner,sign*10,owner===0?24:-24);
            this.addUnit('galley',owner,sign*9,owner===0?14:-14);this.addUnit('transport',owner,sign*10,owner===0?34:-34);
            boat.order={type:'gather',target:null};

          for(let i=0;i<12;i++){const fish=this.addResource('food',(this.rng()-.5)*17,-66+i*12,2200);fish.water=true;fish.r=2.1;}
          for(const e of this.entities.filter(e=>e.kind==='unit'||e.kind==='building')){e.maxHp=this.maxHP(e);e.hp=e.maxHp;}
          for(const boat of this.entities.filter(e=>e.type==='fishingboat'))this.assignWorker(boat);
          this.updateFog();

      p.grid=function(owner,naval=false){if(!naval)return original.grid.call(this,owner);const key='sea'+owner;if(this.grids[key]?.revision===this.revision)return this.grids[key].data;
        const size=this.gridSize,half=this.halfWorld,data=new Uint8Array(size*size);for(let z=0;z<size;z++)for(let x=0;x<size;x++)data[z*size+x]=this.isWater(x*2-half+1,z*2-half+1)?0:1;this.grids[key]={revision:this.revision,data};return data;
      }
      isVisible(x,z){const c=this.cell(x,z);return !!this.visible[c.z*this.gridSize+c.x];}
      isExplored(x,z){const c=this.cell(x,z);return !!this.explored[c.z*this.gridSize+c.x];}
      updateFog(){this.visible.fill(0);for(const owner of this.revealedOwners||[])for(const e of this.owned(owner,'building')){const c=this.cell(e.x,e.z),r=Math.ceil(e.r/2)+2;for(let z=Math.max(0,c.z-r);z<=Math.min(this.gridSize-1,c.z+r);z++)for(let x=Math.max(0,c.x-r);x<=Math.min(this.gridSize-1,c.x+r);x++){this.visible[z*this.gridSize+x]=1;this.explored[z*this.gridSize+x]=1;}}for(const e of this.entities.filter(e=>e.hp>0&&(e.owner===0||this.options.mode==='custom'&&this.options.shareVision&&this.allied(0,e.owner))&&!e.embarked&&(e.kind==='unit'||e.kind==='building'&&e.progress>0))){const r=e.kind==='unit'?UNITS[e.type].vision:BUILDINGS[e.type].vision||18,c=this.cell(e.x,e.z),rc=Math.ceil(r/2);for(let z=Math.max(0,c.z-rc);z<=Math.min(this.gridSize-1,c.z+rc);z++)for(let x=Math.max(0,c.x-rc);x<=Math.min(this.gridSize-1,c.x+rc);x++)if(Math.hypot(x-c.x,z-c.z)<=rc){this.visible[z*this.gridSize+x]=1;this.explored[z*this.gridSize+x]=1;}}

    # Version 2.4 verification
    
    Checked 10 October 2026. This records observed checks, rather than a claim that all possible bugs or all device configurations have been ruled out.

    Eight simultaneous real WebSocket clients exercised readiness, private economies and fog, command ownership, reconnect recovery, host elimination and alliance results. Mixed human/AI rooms also passed. These tests use isolated services and do not modify live player rooms.

    # Crowns of the Frontier
    
    An original 3D browser RTS built with Three.js. Version 2.4, **Kingdoms and skies**, adds custom battles with up to eight kingdoms, configurable human/AI slots, allies and enemies, independent AI difficulties, spacious maps, team multiplayer, and changing 3D weather. Staged campaigns, checkpoints, naval warfare, civilization-exclusive troops and upgrades, a technology tree, solid world models, elevated terrain, and landscape phone controls remain available.
    
    ## Play
    
    For a free online address with one service hosting the game and multiplayer, use the included Render deployment file. See [the short deployment guide](DEPLOYMENT.md). Netlify static hosting is also configured; it needs a separate running server for real-person multiplayer.
    
    ```powershell
    npm install
    npm run build
    npm start
    ```
    
    Open **http://localhost:4173** on the laptop. On a phone connected to the same Wi-Fi, open **http://YOUR_LAPTOP_WIFI_IP:4173**. Landscape is recommended. The laptop must keep the game server running. If the phone cannot reach it, check that the local network permits connections to port 4173.
    
    For development, `npm run dev` serves on port 5173. Use `npm start` for Wi-Fi multiplayer; the static Vite preview server does not host rooms.
    
    ### Play with a friend
    
    Both players open the same laptop's game URL. Choose **Play with friends**, enter a commander name, then create or join a room. Share the six-character room code with the second player. The host starts once both players join. Conquest, regicide, shrine control, wonder race, and naval conquest are supported.
    
    The server runs the simulation and checks command ownership. Each player sees their own economy and fog of war. Classic two-player rooms receive mirrored starting towns and armies. If a connection drops, the match pauses for a reconnect grace period of two minutes. Refreshing the page preserves a room credential in session storage; choose **Rejoin your previous network session**. The menu does not pause an otherwise connected network match. Leaving a started match concedes that kingdom. Restarting the laptop server ends its in-memory rooms.
    
    ### Custom battles with AI or real people
    
    Choose **Custom battle**. Enable two to eight kingdoms, set their civilizations and team numbers, and choose a difficulty for each AI. Matching team numbers are allies. Presets include 2v2, 3v3, 4v4, 1v3, and four/eight-way free-for-all. Without other people, all remaining enabled kingdoms are AI, including your allies.
    
    **Huge** is the default: a 400 Ã— 400 battlefield, 6.25 times the area of a classic map. Large is 320 Ã— 320 and Spacious is 240 Ã— 240. Choose any of the seven biomes, a seed, starting age, starting resources, population cap, shared allied vision, and victory rule. Coast battles begin in at least the Feudal Age and include harbors, fishing boats and transports.
    
    The default victory rule is **destroy all opposing buildings**, including walls and unfinished foundations. Losing a capital alone does not eliminate a kingdom; surviving villagers can rebuild. Other rules require the last town center to fall, or require every opposing unit and building to be defeated. The final few buildings can be revealed after a capital falls to help finish the war. Battles develop through real paid gathering, construction, upgrades and armies; their length depends on the battle rather than a forced minimum timer.
    
    For real people, choose **Human slot** for each friend and **Host multiplayer battle**. Friends join using the room code and can choose an available Human slot. Every human must be connected and ready before the host starts; AI slots are ready automatically. Human and AI kingdoms can fight together or against each other. A defeated host can watch surviving allies, and the match continues until one alliance remains. Each client receives its own command perspective and private economy.
    
    ### Weather and graphics
    
    Automatic weather changes from clear skies to clouds, rain or storms; Winterwood can receive snow, and the desert is drier. Rain, snow, clouds and splash rings use 3D meshes with pooled instances. Weather changes atmosphere without altering resource or combat rules. Settings provide automatic or forced weather, independent weather audio, and optional lightning flashes; reduced motion disables flashes.
    
    The world also has rooted trees with wind movement and winter snowcaps, falling harvested trees and persistent stumps, carried logs/sacks/ingots/rocks, shrinking ore deposits, stronger terrain relief, and town-center architecture that changes through the four ages. Cargo and stumps use at most five additional draw calls. The HUD, text, and square radar remain readable interface elements over the 3D battlefield.
    
    Low quality limits active rendering to 30 FPS and reduces particles, shadows and detail. When the browser reports at most 4 GB of memory or four processor threads, a fresh installation starts on Low; saved quality choices take precedence. Menus and hidden tabs render less often, and hidden world objects defer mesh allocation until revealed. These are performance budgets, not guarantees for every device. Start with Low quality and 80 population per kingdom on phones.
    
    Start with **First light**, the guided tutorial. Use **Clash of crowns** for a standard match. **Legendary** difficulty offers early attacks and relentless pressure. The game runs locally; it does not require an account.
    
    ## Included gameplay
    
    - **Nine modes:** tutorial, conquest skirmish, regicide, ten-wave survival, shrine control, monument race, peaceful sandbox, naval conquest, and configurable custom battles.
    - **Six campaign chapters:** settlement, river crossing, fortress defense, sacred valley, final siege, and a coastal invasion. All chapters can be played immediately. Each has three staged objectives, an original dialogue journal, an optional completion goal, and checkpoints. The river chapter requires a protected caravan escort; shrine control supports an alternative conquest route, and the coastal chapter supports landings or naval artillery.
    - **Seven seeded maps:** Emerald highlands, river crossing, sunlit steppe, Winterwood, iron frontier, twin rivers, and the divided coast. Seeds reproduce resource layouts. Bridges create movement chokepoints; winter has additional timber, the iron frontier has contested central ore, and the coast requires fleets or transports.
    - **Three original civilizations:** Alder Kingdom (durability), Sunward Sultanate (economy and construction), Raven Clans (cavalry).
    - **Four difficulties:** Explorer, Commander, Conqueror, Legendary. Difficulty changes enemy decision and attack timing; survival also changes wave strength.
    - **19 buildings:** town center, house, farm, mill, lumber camp, mining camp, barracks, archery range, stable, siege workshop, blacksmith, market, watchtower, castle, stone wall, gatehouse, monastery, grand monument, and harbor.
    - **16 trainable unit types across the catalog:** villager, scout, spearman, archer, man-at-arms, knight, battering ram, trebuchet, healer, fishing boat, galley, siege galleon, and transport, plus civilization-exclusive Alder sentinels, Sunward marksmen, and Raven outriders. Each civilization has access to its own exclusive troop. Regicide adds an irreplaceable sovereign for each side.
    - **Four ages** with population limits, paid training queues, rally points, age requirements, automatic age strength improvements, and queue cancellation refunds.
    - **Ten technology families across the catalog:** gathering tools, melee attack, armor, ranged attack, fortification, cavalry speed, and seamanship, plus civilization-exclusive Shield drill, Caravan ledger, and Raiding parties. Research levels have age requirements and increasing costs.
    - Harbors must be built near a shore. Fishing boats collect fish and return their catch to a harbor. Command land troops onto a friendly transport to embark up to eight passengers; select the transport, choose **Unload**, and select nearby open land. Sinking a transport defeats its passengers. Siege galleons can bombard shoreline defenses.
    - Villagers physically walk between resources and drop-off buildings, carry supplies, construct buildings, and repair damage. Farms provide renewable food. Mines and trees deplete. Markets buy and sell resources for gold.
    - Walls block paths; friendly units can pass through gates. Connected walls support queued construction. Construction can be canceled for a 70% resource refund; finished buildings can be demolished for a 20% refund. Your last town center is protected from accidental demolition.
    - Unit counters, splash siege damage, automatic healing, defensive towers, formations, aggressive/hold stances, queued orders, box selection, type selection, numbered control groups, and visible selected-unit attributes.
    - Enemy AI responds to visible threats, repairs damaged buildings, reinforces counters against observed unit types, escorts attacks with healers, and runs a fishing and transport economy on the coastal map.
    - Articulated walking, weapon motion, working villagers, rocking ships, ship wakes, drifting water textures, textured masonry and wood, gabled roofs, and biome-specific foliage. Hidden forests obey exploration. Battle audio includes impact layers, arrows, siege sounds, stereo placement, wind, birds, and ambient music, with bounded effects and audio voices.
    - Closer perspective cameras, selectable close/perspective/overview angles, mouse and touch rotation, surface relief, directional lighting, sharper camera-centered shadows, timber framing, window recesses, and shared instanced contact shadows that remain available in Performance quality.
    - All 19 building types and all 18 character/ship types (16 trainable across the catalog, the sovereign, and a campaign supply caravan) have solid mesh models. Buildings use arches, domes, gables, piers, fences, turrets, grain stalks, and distinct workshops. Human models have faces, shaped torsos, jointed limbs, held tools and weapons; cavalry adds modeled horses, and siege equipment has moving wheels and mechanisms. Trees, ore deposits, fruit, fish, and shrines also use mesh geometry.
    - All seven maps have seeded rolling terrain and surrounding ridges. Picking, walking, building foundations, effects, previews, and fog follow the surface. Bridges stay dry and naval channels have submerged beds. Water has moving vertices and updated normals. Nearby gate portcullises lift for friendly troops.
    - Selection portraits render the actual model as a live WebGL turntable. Tap/click the portrait, or press **I**, to inspect the selected object. The square camera button hides or restores battlefield panels for an unobstructed view.
    - Fog of war, exploration, a working minimap, mission objectives, victory/defeat screens, match statistics, synthesized audio, pause, game speed, local saves, and campaign completion tracking.
    - Landscape-first touch interface, pinch zoom, drag pan, responsive menus, graphics presets, and automatic rendering resolution adjustment.
    
    ## Controls
    
    These are the default keyboard bindings. Settings lets you remap controls with conflict checks; Escape, Tab, and numbered control groups stay reserved. Custom bindings, higher-contrast UI, and reduced decorative motion are saved on this device.
    
    | Action | Laptop | Phone/tablet |
    |---|---|---|
    | Select | Left click; Shift adds; drag a selection box | Tap a unit or building |
    | Command | Right click; Shift queues | Select units, then tap ground, enemies, or resources |
    | Pan | Mouse at the game-window edges/corners, WASD/arrows, or middle-button drag | Drag the battlefield |
    | Zoom | Mouse wheel | Two-finger pinch |
    | Rotate | Q/E or camera arrow buttons | Two-finger twist or camera arrow buttons |
    | Camera angle | V or the camera view button | Camera view button |
    | Inspect selected model | I or selection portrait | Tap selection portrait |
    | Hide/show panels | Square camera button | Square camera button |
    | Center town | H or minimap home | Minimap home button |
    | Radar navigation | Click or drag the square minimap | Tap or drag the square minimap |
    | Production overview | P or top-bar P button | Top-bar P button |
    | Queue five troops | Shift-click a troop; +5 in building groups | +5 in building groups |
    | Select army | M | Army button |
    | Idle villagers | Period | Idle button |
    | Construct | B | Build button |
    | Attack move | F, then click | Attack button, then tap |
    | Stop / hold | X | Stop button |
    | Patrol | R, then click a destination | Select military units, tap Patrol, then a destination |
    | Guard | G, then click a friendly unit/building | Select military units, tap Guard, then an ally |
    | Groups | Ctrl + 1â€“9 assigns; 1â€“9 recalls | Army/type selection buttons |
    | Focus selection | Space | Tap minimap to navigate |
    | Pause | Esc | Pause button |
    
    Choose **Stone wall** and drag across visible, open land to place a connected line. Use **Shift** to keep other construction tools active. Select a completed military building to train troops, a blacksmith to research combat technologies, or the town center to advance ages. Use the in-game **Field guide** for costs and counters.
    
    Mouse edge scrolling is enabled by default. Bring the cursor into the outer 24 pixels of the game window to pan; corners pan diagonally and a directional arrow appears. Scrolling follows the rotated camera, stops outside the game or during menus/pauses, and avoids controls. **Settings** includes an on/off toggle and speed slider. Touch gestures continue to pan and zoom. Fullscreen lets you use the monitor edges.
    
    The square minimap acts as your battlefield radar. Its outlined rectangle encloses the ground within the camera view, and its center dot marks where the camera is aimed. The locator remains rectangular at map edges and follows rotation and zoom. Right-click the minimap to give selected units orders; commands outside the playable battlefield are ignored.
    
    Open **Production** with **P** or the top-bar button to see your completed production/research buildings, active queues, progress, and idle sites. Tap a building to select and locate it, or choose its type to select several. Troop orders across selected buildings go to the shortest available queue. Use **+5** or Shift-click to request a batch, limited by resources, population, ages, and queue capacity. Tap queued items to cancel and refund them. Research and age advancement also appear in the overview.
    
    Selected units show their current orders and queued waypoint counts. Movement commands display without route lines on desktop and phones. Unreachable orders report a blocked route and yield to the next queued order. Melee units do not automatically pursue ships beyond their reach.
    
    Open the Field guide and choose **Explore the technology tree** to compare civilizations, inspect age and building requirements, and train/research directly when eligible. The opponent uses paid queues and buildings, scouting memory, composition targets, age-resource reserves, repairs, retreats, and transport boarding reservations. These are implemented behaviors, not a claim of balanced difficulty.
    
    Campaign objectives include **Journal**, **Locate goal**, and (for the escort) **Select caravan** controls. A gold diamond marks the active destination on the minimap; an explored destination also has a 3D banner. Restore the starting or latest completed-objective checkpoint from the commander menu or defeat screen. Checkpoints capture a separate, frozen simulation snapshot and are included in local saves. Existing campaign saves retain their previous victory rules instead of acquiring a new escort requirement. Optional completions earn a chapter star.

    - Rooted near-detail trees, solid winter snowcaps, wind movement, harvested tree falls and persistent stumps. Batched 3D cargo follows villagers, ore visibly shrinks with depletion, and town-center architecture gains physical features at each age. Stronger playable terrain relief, huge-map grass/fog coverage, allied animated gates, and observed multiplayer work animations.
    - Coastal armies stay on their current shore, scout capitals before repeated harbor foundations, search cleared settlements, rebuild harbors with paid workers, reserve fleet population, prioritize transport replacement, fill balanced invasion crews, retry voyages, and choose flanking landing sites around observed defenses.
    - Free single-service Render deployment configuration, health checks and a short deployment guide; optional Netlify static builds with a separate secure multiplayer endpoint and exact frontend origin permissions. Leaving now cancels pending reconnect attempts.
    - Health, carried-resource and production timer updates preserve existing buttons and portrait canvases, preventing live updates from interrupting touch training or cancellation. Hosted connection errors stay visible in the multiplayer dialog.
    
    - Configurable custom battles with two to eight kingdoms, human or AI slots, civilizations, teams, individual AI difficulties and six team/free-for-all presets.
    - Huge 400 Ã— 400 maps by default, plus 320 Ã— 320 and 240 Ã— 240 options. Navigation, fog, terrain picking, camera limits, minimap and rendering support the larger battlefield and eight army colors.
    - Default victory requires all opposing buildings, including walls and foundations. Optional capital and total-conquest rules, capital rebuilding, public final-building markers, alliance results and defeat spectating.
    - Authoritative mixed human/AI multiplayer, slot choice, readiness gating, per-team visibility, private economies, ownership, compressed compact snapshots, disconnect pauses, reconnect recovery and concessions that preserve surviving teams.
    - Seeded weather transitions, volumetric rain/snow/clouds and splash rings, wet terrain/light changes, optional lightning, independent weather audio, reduced-motion support and quality budgets.
    - Sustained AI attacks across large maps, independent planning, remembered-target cleanup and paid market trade for shortages. AI gathers and pays for armies, buildings and upgrades.
    - Physical tree/ore navigation and construction obstacles, final-load delivery after resources run out, cached vision/movement regions, valid-route retention and bounded blocked-path retries.
    - Low quality renders at up to 30 FPS; menu and hidden-tab rendering is throttled. Fresh settings choose Low on modest reported hardware, and unseen objects defer mesh allocation. Real-device FPS and balance remain separate release validation requirements.
    - Expanded automated, browser and long-match diagnostics cover custom setup, eight real WebSocket clients, phone layouts, weather, ownership, reconnects, alliances, late-game progression and full-building elimination.

    import test from 'node:test';
    import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
    import {Simulation} from '../src/simulation.js';
    
    test('workers select eligible drop-offs and immediately recover after destruction, completion and restoration',()=>{
      const sim=new Simulation({mode:'sandbox',map:'highlands',seed:512}),worker=sim.owned(0,'unit','villager')[0];
      const enemy=sim.addBuilding('mine',1,worker.x+1,worker.z,true),foundation=sim.addBuilding('mine',0,worker.x+2,worker.z,false);
      assert.notEqual(sim.nearestDrop(worker,'gold'),enemy);assert.notEqual(sim.nearestDrop(worker,'gold'),foundation);
      sim.command([worker.id],{type:'build',target:foundation.id});foundation.progress=.999;sim.tickUnit(worker,1);
      assert.equal(foundation.progress,1);assert.equal(sim.nearestDrop(worker,'gold'),foundation);
      sim.hurt(foundation,foundation.hp+1,null);assert.notEqual(sim.nearestDrop(worker,'gold'),foundation);
      const camp=sim.addBuilding('camp',0,worker.x+1,worker.z,true);assert.equal(sim.nearestDrop(worker,'wood'),camp);assert.notEqual(sim.nearestDrop(worker,'stone'),camp);
      const restored=Simulation.restore(JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(sim.serialize())));assert.equal(restored.nearestDrop(restored.get(worker.id),'wood').id,camp.id);
      const coast=new Simulation({mode:'sandbox',map:'coast'}),boat=coast.owned(0,'unit','fishingboat')[0];
      assert.equal(coast.nearestDrop(boat,'food',true).type,'dock');assert.equal(coast.nearestDrop(boat,'gold',true),null);
    });

    Add: C:\New\Age_Of_Emprire\ART_PIPELINE.md
    # Blender art and runtime rendering
    
    The deployed game includes both GLB catalogues and texture files. Playing or deploying it requires no Blender installation and no external asset service.
    
    The catalogue contains 126 models: 66 civilization/age building variants, 18 troop/ship/caravan types plus four worker task variants, 24 forest variants and 14 resource models. The models were made for this original game. They are not Age of Empires or Warcraft assets.
    
    ## Edit and regenerate
    
    The development installation uses Blender 4.5.14 LTS at `.tools/blender-4.5.14-windows-x64/blender.exe`. The editable generated project is `.tools/art-refined/frontier-assets.blend`. Open the current catalogue showcase with:
    
    ```powershell
    powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/blender/start.ps1 -Visible -Showcase
    ```
    
    `scripts/blender/showcase.py` arranges the catalogue for inspection with material colors. The live browser applies the photographed surfaces, lighting, fog and weather. The lightweight Blender preview disables expensive viewport modifiers for this laptop.
    
    ```powershell
    npm run art:build
    npm run art:materials
    npm run build
    ```
    
    `art:build` exports the original model source, refines it in background Blender, creates adult-proportioned figures and solid worker tools, then compresses near/low GLBs with gltfpack. Bevels, baked vertex shading, normals, UVs and semantic material/joint metadata survive export. The builder runs jobs sequentially to limit memory pressure. Blender and gltfpack are development tools in `.tools`; they are excluded from deployment archives. Blender's [published minimum is 8 GB RAM](https://www.blender.org/download/requirements/), above this laptop's approximately 4 GB, so large art tasks need care.
    
    `art:materials` downloads three CC0 surface sets using the published Poly Haven API and verifies file sizes and hashes. Runtime uses local bundled JPEGs, with no asset API requests. Creator credits and source links are in [the texture license](src/assets3d/textures/LICENSE.md).
    
    ## In-game behavior and budgets
    
    - The near GLB is approximately 11.9 MiB; the lower detail GLB is approximately 2.4 MiB. Both contain the full 126-model catalogue. Nine photographed surface maps total approximately 7.4 MiB.
    - High uses near geometry and color/normal/roughness maps. Medium uses low geometry with color/normal maps. Low uses low geometry and color maps.
    - Nested joint metadata drives runtime poses. The catalogue does not contain baked skeletal animation clips. Worker tools follow their actual gathering/building/repair task.
    - Troops share instanced batches across team colors. Visible instance IDs are packed together so picking and selection still identify the correct unit. Fog and offscreen culling reduce submitted instances.
    - Buildings merge static surfaces into one opaque draw, with shared geometry for repeat structures. Flags, windmills, gates and harbor piers retain their independent transforms. Construction clipping preserves the textured material shader.
    - Solid grass uses one instanced draw and clears building foundations. Fallen units and flying/settling rubble are cosmetic, bounded and excluded from collision, orders and saves.
    - The square radar, HUD and text remain interface overlays. The playable world and selectable objects use solid 3D meshes.
    
    `tests/authored-assets.test.js`, `tests/render-batches.test.js`, `tests/ground-cover.test.js` and `tests/battle-remains.test.js` check catalogue coverage, bounds, joints, tools, ownership, packing, foundations and effect limits. `scripts/authored-art-qa.mjs` reviews the live renderer, camera/selection preservation, biomes, naval models and emulated landscape-phone controls. Rendering targets and actual measured limitations are recorded separately in [RELEASE_CHECKS.md](RELEASE_CHECKS.md).

    +# Crafted battlefields (version 2.5)
    +
    +- 126 original Blender models with near/low catalogues, adult-proportioned figures, nested joints, task-specific worker tools, refined buildings and solid foliage. Photographed CC0 grass, wood and masonry surfaces have local creator/source credits.
    +- Solid grass blades, bounded fallen troops and physical building rubble. Landscape-phone controls use a compact selection panel with larger touch targets.
    +- Shared troop batches across team colors, viewport/fog instance packing with correct picking IDs, building surface batching and repeat geometry sharing. Moving gates, flags, mills, harbor piers and construction clipping keep their behavior.
    +- Balanced, Grand war and Aggressive custom AI pacing. Major balanced offensives require an economy, Feudal Age and a fuller army; early defense remains active. AI allies lend real troops or ships, retain defenders, and recall help when threatened at home. Support assignments and pace survive saves.
    +- Allied support notices are private and remapped for each multiplayer perspective. Server AI alarm data is excluded from client snapshots.
    +- Indexed spatial queries, cached eligible resource drop-offs, cheaper fog circles and a single custom-victory scan reduce simulation CPU work. Automatic graphics reacts to actual elapsed frame time and respects manual quality.
    +- Added art, support/recall, privacy, graphics adaptation and economy regression checks, plus crowded-battle rendering diagnostics. High-load performance and physical-device/human release testing remain open.
    +

    +Choose **Balanced** for economy and army buildup before major AI offensives, **Grand war** for a longer opening, or **Aggressive** for early pressure. Balanced also requires Feudal Age, enough workers and a fuller army. Defense stays active from the beginning. AI allies can send a limited reinforcement group to a threatened allied settlement or harbor, keep troops at home, and recall support if their own base is attacked. They use existing units and regular movement, with no free reinforcements. The selected pace is preserved in saves and multiplayer setup; older saves retain their previous aggressive pacing.
    +
     For real people, choose **Human slot** for each friend and **Host multiplayer battle**. Friends join using the room code and can choose an available Human slot. Every human must be connected and ready before the host starts; AI slots are ready automatically. Human and AI kingdoms can fight together or against each other. A defeated host can watch surviving allies, and the match continues until one alliance remains. Each client receives its own command perspective and private economy.

When the browser reports at most 4 GB of memory or four processor threads, a fresh installation starts on Low; saved quality choices take precedence.         if (cached) return cached;
        return fetch(event.request).catch(() => {
          if (event.request.mode === 'navigate') return caches.match('/index.html');

    import * as THREE from 'three';
    import {animatePart} from './world-polish.js';
    
    // Keep allocation slots stable while packing only the current visible poses.
    // Picking uses the packed IDs, never the allocator's potentially empty slots.
    export function beginUnitFrame(view){
      view.camera.updateMatrixWorld();
      const projection=view.frameProjection??=new THREE.Matrix4();
      (view.frameFrustum??=new THREE.Frustum()).setFromProjectionMatrix(projection.multiplyMatrices(view.camera.projectionMatrix,view.camera.matrixWorldInverse));
      for(const batch of view.unitBatches.values())batch.renderIds.length=0;
    }
    
    export function nearViewport(view,x,y,z,radius=12){
      if(!view.frameFrustum)return true;
      const sphere=view.frameSphere??=new THREE.Sphere();sphere.center.set(x,y,z);sphere.radius=radius;
      return view.frameFrustum.intersectsSphere(sphere);
    }
    
    export function writeUnitPose(view,batch,e,matrix,shown){
      if(!shown)return false;
      const position=view.framePosition??=new THREE.Vector3();position.setFromMatrixPosition(matrix);
      if(!nearViewport(view,position.x,position.y,position.z))return false;
      const index=batch.renderIds.length;
      batch.renderIds.push(e.id);
      for(const part of batch.parts){part.setMatrixAt(index,animatePart(view,part,e,matrix));part.geometry.getAttribute('instanceOwner')?.setX(index,e.owner||0);}
      return true;
    }
    
    export function endUnitFrame(view){
      let drawn=0,allocated=0,activeBatches=0;
      for(const batch of view.unitBatches.values()){
        const count=batch.renderIds.length;drawn+=count;allocated+=batch.ids.length-batch.free.length;
        if(count)activeBatches++;
        for(const part of batch.parts){part.count=count;part.visible=count>0;part.instanceMatrix.needsUpdate=true;part.boundingSphere=null;const owner=part.geometry.getAttribute('instanceOwner');if(owner)owner.needsUpdate=true;}
      }
      view.unitRenderDiagnostics={drawn,allocated,activeBatches};
    }
      }
      return 0;
    }
    export function animatePart(view,part,e,matrix){
      const m=part.userData.motion;if(!m)return matrix;
      const result=view.poseMatrix??=new THREE.Matrix4(),rotation=view.poseRotation??=new THREE.Matrix4();result.copy(matrix);
      if(m.type==='ram'){const translation=part.userData.ramTranslation??=new THREE.Matrix4();translation.makeTranslation(0,0,e.cooldown>0?Math.sin(e.cooldown*8)*.25:0);return result.multiply(translation);}
      if(!part.userData.poseChain){const chain=[];for(let joint=m;joint;joint=joint.parent)chain.unshift({joint,forward:new THREE.Matrix4().makeTranslation(...joint.pivot),back:new THREE.Matrix4().makeTranslation(-joint.pivot[0],-joint.pivot[1],-joint.pivot[2])});part.userData.poseChain=chain;}
      for(const pose of part.userData.poseChain){rotation.makeRotationX(jointAngle(view,pose.joint,e));result.multiply(pose.forward).multiply(rotation).multiply(pose.back);}
      return result;
    }

    export function drawMinimap(canvas,sim,view,settings){
      const ctx=canvas.getContext('2d'),size=canvas.width,worldSize=sim.worldSize||WORLD,half=worldSize/2,scale=size/worldSize,coord=value=>(value+half)*scale;
      ctx.clearRect(0,0,size,size);ctx.fillStyle={desert:'#8e8968',winter:'#b8c5b8',canyon:'#9a8875'}[sim.options.map]||'#6e7c59';ctx.fillRect(0,0,size,size);
      // Water must be drawn before ships and resources, using the same channels as the 3D map.
      for(const channel of view.landscape.channels()){
        ctx.strokeStyle='#72a3a5';ctx.lineWidth=channel.width*2*scale;ctx.lineCap='butt';ctx.beginPath();
        for(let z=-half;z<=half;z+=2){const x=coord(channel.center+Math.sin(z*channel.frequency)*channel.bend),y=coord(z);if(z===-half)ctx.moveTo(x,y);else ctx.lineTo(x,y);}ctx.stroke();
        if(sim.options.map!=='coast'){ctx.fillStyle='#ac9b75';ctx.fillRect(coord(channel.center-channel.width-3),coord(-7.75),(channel.width+3)*2*scale,15.5*scale);}
      }
      for(const e of sim.entities){
        if(e.hp<=0||e.embarked||!(e.owner===0||e.kind==='shrine'||sim.isVisible(e.x,e.z)||e.kind==='resource'&&sim.isExplored(e.x,e.z)))continue;
        ctx.fillStyle=e.kind==='resource'?{wood:'#315b42',gold:'#e1bf69',stone:'#bac0b4',food:e.water?'#c5dee2':'#ab7560'}[e.type]:e.kind==='shrine'?(e.owner===0?'#91dbc9':e.owner===1?'#df8582':'#e3d3a2'):e.owner>=0?('#'+(sim.players[e.owner].color??(e.owner===0?0xb5e7dc:0xed8b7b)).toString(16).padStart(6,'0')):'#e3d3a2';
        const r=e.kind==='building'?Math.max(2,e.r*scale):e.kind==='unit'?1.6:1.5;ctx.fillRect(coord(e.x)-r,coord(e.z)-r,r*2,r*2);
      }
      if(settings.fog)ctx.drawImage(view.fogCanvas,0,0,size,size);
      const goal=campaignObjective(sim)?.marker;if(goal){const x=coord(goal.x),z=coord(goal.z);ctx.beginPath();ctx.moveTo(x,z-5);ctx.lineTo(x+5,z);ctx.lineTo(x,z+5);ctx.lineTo(x-5,z);ctx.closePath();ctx.fillStyle='#f2ce77';ctx.fill();ctx.strokeStyle='#18251f';ctx.lineWidth=1.5;ctx.stroke();}
      const box=cameraMapBox(view.camera,view.groundHeight(view.target.x,view.target.z),worldSize);
      if(box){
        const x=coord(box.minX),z=coord(box.minZ),width=(box.maxX-box.minX)*scale,height=(box.maxZ-box.minZ)*scale;
        ctx.fillStyle='#f5e8bd12';ctx.fillRect(x,z,width,height);ctx.strokeStyle='#16251f';ctx.lineWidth=3;ctx.strokeRect(x,z,width,height);ctx.strokeStyle='#f5e8bd';ctx.lineWidth=1.5;ctx.strokeRect(x,z,width,height);
      }

      view.minimapCameraBox=box;
      // A center marker stays readable even when an overview covers almost the whole map.
      ctx.beginPath();ctx.arc(coord(view.target.x),coord(view.target.z),2.3,0,Math.PI*2);ctx.fillStyle='#f5e8bd';ctx.fill();ctx.strokeStyle='#16251f';ctx.lineWidth=1;ctx.stroke();
      ctx.strokeStyle='#899b7e';ctx.lineWidth=1;ctx.strokeRect(.5,.5,size-1,size-1);
    }
    const blockedControls='button,a,input,select,textarea,label,[role="button"],#minimap,.bottom-hud,#build-panel,#production-panel,.camera-controls,.objective-panel.interactive-objectives';
    const cursors=new Map();
    
    function edgeVector(x,y,width,height){
      if(x<0||y<0||x>=width||y>=height)return{x:0,y:0};
      const band=Math.min(24,width/4,height/4);
      const strength=distance=>{const t=1-distance/band;return t*t*(3-2*t);};
      let dx=x<band?-strength(x):x>width-band?strength(width-x):0;
      let dy=y<band?-strength(y):y>height-band?strength(height-y):0;
      const length=Math.hypot(dx,dy);if(length>1){dx/=length;dy/=length;}
      return{x:dx,y:dy};

    function arrowCursor(x,y){
      const sx=Math.sign(x),sy=Math.sign(y),key=`${sx}:${sy}`;
      if(!cursors.has(key)){
        const angle=Math.atan2(sx,-sy)*180/Math.PI;
        const svg=`<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="32" height="32" viewBox="0 0 32 32"><g transform="rotate(${angle} 16 16)"><path d="M16 2 6 14h6v14h8V14h6Z" fill="#f1d79b" stroke="#182d25" stroke-width="2" stroke-linejoin="round"/><path d="m16 6-5 6h4v12" fill="none" stroke="#fff5d9" stroke-width="1.4"/></g></svg>`;

      }
      return cursors.get(key);
    }
    
    export class EdgeScroll {
      constructor(){
        this.point=null;this.cursor='';
        const track=event=>{
          if(event.pointerType!=='mouse'){this.reset();return;}
          this.point={x:event.clientX,y:event.clientY,buttons:event.buttons};
        };
        // Track the whole viewport so the header/footer do not swallow an edge.
        document.addEventListener('pointermove',track,{passive:true});
        document.addEventListener('pointerdown',track,{passive:true});
        document.addEventListener('pointerup',track,{passive:true});
        document.documentElement.addEventListener('pointerleave',()=>this.reset());
        window.addEventListener('blur',()=>this.reset());window.addEventListener('resize',()=>this.reset());
        document.addEventListener('visibilitychange',()=>{if(document.hidden)this.reset();});
      }
      setCursor(value){
        if(this.cursor===value)return;this.cursor=value;
        if(value)document.documentElement.style.setProperty('--battlefield-cursor',value);
        else document.documentElement.style.removeProperty('--battlefield-cursor');
      }
      reset(){this.point=null;this.setCursor('');}
      tick(view,dt,{active,enabled,speed=1}){
        if(!active||!enabled||!this.point||!document.hasFocus()||(this.point.buttons&4)){this.setCursor('');return false;}
        const {x,y}=edgeVector(this.point.x,this.point.y,innerWidth,innerHeight);
        if(!x&&!y){this.setCursor('');return false;}
        const element=document.elementFromPoint(this.point.x,this.point.y);
        if(!element||element.closest(blockedControls)){this.setCursor('');return false;}
        this.setCursor(arrowCursor(x,y));
        const distance=dt*view.zoom*.5*Math.max(.25,Math.min(2,Number(speed)||1));
        // pan() maps screen directions through the current camera rotation.
        view.pan(x*distance,y*distance);return true;
      }
    }

    src/main.js:108:function showHelp(){if(playing)paused=true;showModal(`<div class="eyebrow">THE COMMANDER'S HANDBOOK</div><h2>Every empire starts small.</h2><div class="help-grid"><div><h3>Mouse & keyboard</h3><p>Move the mouse to an edge of the game window to scroll the camera. Corners scroll diagonally; the cursor arrow shows the direction. Use fullscreen to scroll at the screen edges. Adjust Mouse edge scrolling and its speed in Settings.</p><p>Click to select. Drag a box to select a group. Shift-click adds units. Double-click selects nearby troops of the same type.</p><p><b>Right-click</b> to move, attack, gather, build, repair, heal, or set a building's rally point. <b>Shift + right-click</b> queues orders.</p><p><b>WASD / arrows:</b> pan · <b>Q/E:</b> rotate · <b>V:</b> camera angle / <b>Wheel:</b> zoom · <b>Middle drag:</b> pan · <b>H:</b> town · <b>M:</b> army · <b>B:</b> build · <b>F:</b> attack move · <b>X:</b> stop · <b>.:</b> idle worker · <b>Esc:</b> pause/cancel</p><p><b>Ctrl + 1–9:</b> store group · <b>1–9:</b> recall group · <b>Space:</b> focus selection</p></div><div><h3>Phone & tablet</h3><p>Play in landscape. Tap your units to select. With a unit selected, tap open ground to move, an enemy to attack, or a resource to gather.</p><p>Drag the battlefield to pan. Use two fingers to pinch-zoom or twist to rotate. The camera buttons also rotate, zoom, and change the viewing angle. The <b>Army</b> button selects every soldier. The <b>Idle</b> button selects idle workers.</p><p>Tap <b>Build</b>, choose a building, then tap open land. Select walls and drag to create a wall line. Gates allow friendly troops through.</p><p>Tap or drag the square minimap to move the camera. Its outlined box and center dot locate your view. Open Production in the top bar to manage queues and select several buildings; the +5 buttons queue a batch. Training and research appear when you select a completed building.</p></div></div><div class="strategy-tip"><b>A good first five minutes</b><p>Keep training villagers. Build houses before reaching the population cap. Place gathering camps near resources. Mix spearmen with archers, advance your age, and bring siege weapons against fortifications. Add healers to preserve expensive troops.</p></div><button class="secondary" data-action="codex">Open the complete field guide ↗</button>`,playing?'help-game':'help',true);}

    import {chromium} from '@playwright/test';
    import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
    import fs from 'node:fs';
    import {UNITS} from '../src/data.js';
    const browser=await chromium.launch({channel:'msedge',headless:true,args:['--enable-webgl','--ignore-gpu-blocklist']});
    const base=process.env.QA_URL||'http://localhost:4173/',errors=[],reports=[];fs.mkdirSync('artifacts',{recursive:true});
    const setup=async page=>{
      page.on('pageerror',e=>errors.push(e.message));await page.addInitScript(()=>localStorage.setItem('crowns-settings',JSON.stringify({music:false,volume:0,quality:'medium',autoQuality:false})));
      await page.goto(base,{waitUntil:'networkidle'});await page.waitForFunction(()=>window.frontier?.view);
      return page.evaluate(()=>{frontier.start({mode:'sandbox',map:'highlands',faction:'alder',difficulty:'normal',seed:512});const s=frontier.sim,a=s.owned(0,'building','barracks')[0],b=s.addBuilding('barracks',0,-15,25,true);s.addBuilding('barracks',1,30,-30,true);s.addBuilding('barracks',0,-15,40);s.owned(0,'unit').forEach(e=>s.stop([e.id]));s.players[0].resources={food:10000,wood:10000,gold:10000,stone:10000};frontier.select([a.id,b.id]);return [a.id,b.id];});
    };
    const queues=(page,ids)=>page.evaluate(ids=>ids.map(id=>frontier.sim.get(id).queue.length),ids);
    try{
      const page=await browser.newPage({viewport:{width:1440,height:900}}),ids=await setup(page);
      await page.locator('#selection-panel [data-train=spearman][data-batch="5"]').click();assert.deepEqual(await queues(page,ids),[3,2]);
      assert.ok(await page.locator('#selection-panel').innerText().then(text=>text.includes('BUILDINGS SELECTED')));assert.equal(await page.locator('#selection-panel .tactics').count(),0);
      await page.locator('#selection-panel [data-train=spearman]:not([data-batch])').click({modifiers:['Shift']});assert.deepEqual(await queues(page,ids),[5,5]);
      await page.keyboard.press('p');await page.locator('#production-panel').waitFor({state:'visible'});assert.equal(await page.locator('#production-panel .production-card').count(),4);
      assert.equal(await page.locator('#production-panel .production-items button').count(),10);assert.equal(await page.locator('#production-count').textContent(),'10');
      const food=await page.evaluate(()=>frontier.sim.players[0].resources.food);await page.locator(`#production-panel [data-building="${ids[0]}"][data-cancel-queue="0"]`).click();assert.deepEqual(await queues(page,ids),[4,5]);
      assert.equal(await page.evaluate(()=>frontier.sim.players[0].resources.food),food+UNITS.spearman.cost.food);

        bpy.ops.object.select_all(action="DESELECT")

                bevel.limit_method = "ANGLE"
                bevel.angle_limit = .8
                bevel.use_clamp_overlap = True

    function pathDistance(x,z,land){
      let distance=Infinity;
      for(const town of land.settlements){
        const end=land.map==='coast'?{x:Math.sign(town.x)*20,z:town.z}:{x:town.x*.2,z:0};
        const dx=end.x-town.x,dz=end.z-town.z,t=Math.max(0,Math.min(1,((x-town.x)*dx+(z-town.z)*dz)/(dx*dx+dz*dz||1)));
        distance=Math.min(distance,Math.hypot(x-town.x-t*dx,z-town.z-t*dz));
      }
      return distance;
    }
    
    export class GroundCover{
      constructor(view){
        this.view=view;const land=view.landscape,rng=seededRandom(land.seed+19),low=view.settings.quality!=='high';
        const capacity=Math.min(low?1800:4800,Math.floor(land.worldSize**2*(low?.04:.075)));
        const winter=land.map==='winter',arid=['desert','canyon'].includes(land.map);
        const material=new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({color:0xffffff,roughness:1,emissive:0x293421,emissiveIntensity:.1});
        this.mesh=new THREE.InstancedMesh(grassTuftGeometry(),material,capacity);this.mesh.count=0;this.mesh.frustumCulled=false;this.mesh.receiveShadow=true;
        this.mesh.name='Solid ground vegetation';this.mesh.instanceMatrix.setUsage(THREE.DynamicDrawUsage);view.terrain.add(this.mesh);
        this.entries=[];this.dummy=new THREE.Object3D();this.color=new THREE.Color();
        const palette=winter?[0xb7c6a7,0xc6c9aa,0x9cae83]:arid?[0xa59562,0xb7ab7c,0x858b55]:[0x829954,0x9aa966,0x71834c];
        for(let i=0;i<capacity;i++){
          const x=(rng()-.5)*(land.worldSize-6),z=(rng()-.5)*(land.worldSize-6),y=land.surfaceHeightAt(x,z);
          if(y<.2||pathDistance(x,z,land)<1.7||winter&&rng()<.5||arid&&rng()<.35)continue;
          this.entries.push({x,y,z,angle:rng()*Math.PI*2,scale:(.65+rng()*.8)*(arid?.7:1),color:palette[i%3],shade:.88+rng()*.18});
        }
        this.update(true,true);
      }
      update(menu=false,force=false){
        const v=this.view,key=[v.target.x,v.target.z,v.zoom,v.angle,v.tilt,menu,v.settings.fog].join(':');
        if(!force&&this.key===key&&v.clock-(this.last||0)<(v.settings.quality==='high'?.3:.5))return;
        this.key=key;this.last=v.clock;
        const sites=new Map(),cell=(x,z)=>Math.floor(x/16)+':'+Math.floor(z/16);
        for(const e of v.sim.entities)if(e.kind==='building'&&e.hp>0){const r=e.r+1;for(let x=Math.floor((e.x-r)/16);x<=Math.floor((e.x+r)/16);x++)for(let z=Math.floor((e.z-r)/16);z<=Math.floor((e.z+r)/16);z++){const key=x+':'+z;if(!sites.has(key))sites.set(key,[]);sites.get(key).push(e);}}
        let count=0;
        for(const e of this.entries){
          if(!nearViewport(v,e.x,e.y,e.z,5)||!menu&&v.settings.fog!==false&&!v.sim.isExplored(e.x,e.z))continue;
          if(sites.get(cell(e.x,e.z))?.some(b=>Math.hypot(b.x-e.x,b.z-e.z)<b.r+1))continue;
          this.dummy.position.set(e.x,e.y+.005,e.z);this.dummy.rotation.set(0,e.angle,v.settings.quality==='high'?Math.sin(v.clock*1.6+e.x*.2)*(.025+(v.weatherState?.intensity||0)*.07):0);this.dummy.scale.setScalar(e.scale);this.dummy.updateMatrix();
          this.mesh.setMatrixAt(count,this.dummy.matrix);this.mesh.setColorAt(count,this.color.setHex(e.color).multiplyScalar(e.shade));count++;
        }
        this.mesh.count=count;this.mesh.instanceMatrix.needsUpdate=true;if(this.mesh.instanceColor)this.mesh.instanceColor.needsUpdate=true;
        v.groundCoverDiagnostics={visible:count,seeded:this.entries.length,triangles:count*this.mesh.geometry.index.count/3,drawCalls:count?1:0};
      }
    }

    param([switch]$SkipStaticBuild)
    $ErrorActionPreference='Stop'
    $taskProject=[IO.Path]::GetFullPath((Join-Path $PSScriptRoot '..'))
    $taskVersion=(Get-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $taskProject 'package.json') -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json).version
    if ($taskVersion -notmatch '^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$') { throw 'Invalid package version.' }
    $taskArtifacts=Join-Path $taskProject 'artifacts'
    $taskStatic=Join-Path $taskArtifacts 'release-static'
    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $taskArtifacts -Force | Out-Null
    
    if (-not $SkipStaticBuild) {
        $taskPreviousLocation=Get-Location
        $taskPreviousStatic=$env:VITE_STATIC_HOST
        $taskPreviousEndpoint=$env:VITE_MULTIPLAYER_URL
        try {
            Set-Location -LiteralPath $taskProject
            $env:VITE_STATIC_HOST='true'
            $env:VITE_MULTIPLAYER_URL=''
            & node node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js build --outDir $taskStatic
            if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Static build failed.' }
        } finally {
            Set-Location -LiteralPath $taskPreviousLocation
            $env:VITE_STATIC_HOST=$taskPreviousStatic
            $env:VITE_MULTIPLAYER_URL=$taskPreviousEndpoint
        }
    }
    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $taskStatic 'index.html'))) { throw 'The static build is missing.' }
    
    Add-Type -AssemblyName System.IO.Compression.FileSystem
    function Write-GameArchive($taskName,$taskBase,$taskFiles) {
        $taskDestination=[IO.Path]::GetFullPath((Join-Path $taskArtifacts $taskName))
        if (-not $taskDestination.StartsWith($taskArtifacts+[IO.Path]::DirectorySeparatorChar,[StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)) { throw 'Archive target is outside the project artifacts folder.' }
        if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $taskDestination) { Remove-Item -LiteralPath $taskDestination }
        $taskArchive=[IO.Compression.ZipFile]::Open($taskDestination,[IO.Compression.ZipArchiveMode]::Create)
        try {
            foreach ($taskFile in $taskFiles) {
                $taskFull=[IO.Path]::GetFullPath($taskFile.FullName)
                if (-not $taskFull.StartsWith($taskBase+[IO.Path]::DirectorySeparatorChar,[StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase)) { throw 'An archive input is outside its allowed folder.' }
                $taskRelative=$taskFull.Substring($taskBase.Length+1).Replace('\','/')
                [IO.Compression.ZipFileExtensions]::CreateEntryFromFile($taskArchive,$taskFull,$taskRelative,[IO.Compression.CompressionLevel]::Optimal) | Out-Null
            }
        } finally { $taskArchive.Dispose() }
        Get-Item -LiteralPath $taskDestination | Select-Object Name,Length
    }
    $taskSourceFiles=@()
    foreach ($taskDirectory in @('src','server','scripts','tests','public')) {
        $taskSourceFiles+=Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath (Join-Path $taskProject $taskDirectory) -Recurse -File
    }
    foreach ($taskFileName in @('package.json','package-lock.json','index.html','vite.config.js','netlify.toml','render.yaml','.gitignore','.nvmrc','README.md','ART_PIPELINE.md','DEPLOYMENT.md','RELEASE_CHECKS.md','ROADMAP.md','CHANGELOG.md')) {
        $taskFilePath=Join-Path $taskProject $taskFileName
        if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $taskFilePath) { $taskSourceFiles+=Get-Item -LiteralPath $taskFilePath }
    }
    Write-GameArchive "crowns-of-the-frontier-$taskVersion-source.zip" $taskProject $taskSourceFiles
    Write-GameArchive "crowns-of-the-frontier-$taskVersion-static.zip" $taskStatic (Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $taskStatic -Recurse -File)

    # Free deployment
    
    Use **Render Free Web Service** for the simplest complete deployment: one URL serves the game and its real-person multiplayer rooms. The included [render.yaml](render.yaml) fills in the build, start, free plan, and health-check settings.
    
    1. Put this project in its own GitHub repository, with `package.json` and `render.yaml` at the root. Do not upload `node_modules`, test artifacts, or local `.env` files.
    2. Sign in to Render, select **New > Blueprint**, and connect that repository.
    3. Confirm that the service plan is **Free**, then deploy. Share the resulting HTTPS `onrender.com` address with players. No separate multiplayer URL or database is needed.
    
    If using **New > Web Service** instead, choose Node, the Free plan, build command `npm ci --include=dev && npm run build`, start command `npm start`, and health-check path `/health`. The server reads Render's `PORT` automatically. Use one instance because rooms are currently kept in memory.
    
    The web-service free tier uses recurring monthly allowances, rather than a fixed trial expiry. It provides 750 instance hours per workspace each month, sleeps after 15 idle minutes, and takes about a minute to wake. Active incoming WebSocket messages count as traffic. Free services can restart, ending live rooms; local single-player saves stay in the player's browser. Bandwidth and build limits also apply. Keep the Free plan and avoid adding a payment method if you want services suspended at chargeable usage limits instead of overage billing. No database is provisioned, so the separate 30-day free database expiry does not apply. Provider terms may change.
    
    This is a free hobby/testing deployment, with limited server CPU. Eight large kingdoms or many simultaneous rooms require hosted performance validation. Free hosting does not establish unlimited capacity or uninterrupted public-game service.
    
    The free deployment defaults to Singapore for Philippine players and one simultaneous multiplayer room to fit the small server. A room still supports up to eight kingdoms. Solo games run on each player's device and do not consume multiplayer rooms. `MAX_ROOMS` can be changed later after measuring server capacity. No account secrets or payment information are stored in the deployment file.
    
    Sources checked 10 October 2026: [free-tier limits](https://render.com/docs/free), [WebSocket support](https://render.com/docs/websocket), [Blueprint configuration](https://render.com/docs/blueprint-spec).
    
    ## Optional Netlify frontend
    
    Netlify can host solo/AI gameplay with the included [netlify.toml](netlify.toml): build `npm run build`, publish `dist`. A static-only build reports that online multiplayer is unavailable while solo modes continue working.
    
    To enable multiplayer from Netlify, set `VITE_MULTIPLAYER_URL=wss://YOUR_RENDER_SERVICE.onrender.com/socket` in the Netlify build environment. On the separate Node service, set `ALLOWED_ORIGINS=https://YOUR_SITE.netlify.app`. Add any custom frontend domain as another comma-separated exact origin, then rebuild/redeploy the frontend. These are public endpoint settings, not credentials. HTTPS sites require secure `wss://` connections.
    
    Netlify's build command and output directory follow its [official Vite guide](https://docs.netlify.com/build/frameworks/framework-setup-guides/vite/). The existing authoritative Node simulation remains a running web service; it is not executed by uploading `dist` to a static host.

    import fs from 'node:fs';
    import {Simulation} from '../src/simulation.js';

    const sim=Simulation.restore(JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(process.env.AUDIT_SAVE||'artifacts/blender-custom-battle-save.json','utf8'))),start=sim.time;
    const before=sim.blockedMovement,records=[],counts={};let captured=false;
    sim.blockedMovement=function(e,dt){
      if((e.stuckTime||0)+dt>=6){
        const order=e.order,target=this.get(order?.target),drop=order?.type==='gather'&&order.returning?this.nearestDrop(e,e.carryType||e.gatherType,!!UNITS[e.type].naval):null;
        const dest=drop||target||order,key=e.type+':'+order?.type;counts[key]=(counts[key]||0)+1;
        if(records.length<50&&dest&&Number.isFinite(dest.x)&&Number.isFinite(dest.z)){
          const status=e.pathStatus,route=this.pathTo(e,dest),freshStatus=e.pathStatus; e.pathStatus=status;
          records.push({time:this.time,id:e.id,owner:e.owner,type:e.type,order:{...order},position:{x:e.x,z:e.z},target:target&&{id:target.id,type:target.type,owner:target.owner,x:target.x,z:target.z,r:target.r},dest:{x:dest.x,z:dest.z},pathStatus:status,path:e.path.slice(0,5),freshStatus,routeLength:route.length,routeEnd:route.at(-1),destinationDistance:Math.hypot(e.x-dest.x,e.z-dest.z),carry:e.carry,carryType:e.carryType});
          if(!captured){fs.writeFileSync('artifacts/navigation-stall-save.json',JSON.stringify(this.serialize()));captured=true;}
        }
      }
      return before.call(this,e,dt);
    };
    while(sim.time-start<90&&!sim.ended)sim.tick(.1);
    const result={start,end:sim.time,ended:sim.ended,counts,records};fs.writeFileSync('artifacts/navigation-audit.json',JSON.stringify(result,null,2));

    const clamp=(sim,n)=>Math.max(-sim.halfWorld+3,Math.min(sim.halfWorld-3,n));
    
    // Resolve formation slots on the unit's own movement surface. This keeps edge
    // slots out of foundations and water without sending land troops across a sea.
    export function formationSlot(sim,unit,point){
      const size=sim.gridSize,half=sim.halfWorld,grid=sim.grid(unit.owner,!!UNITS[unit.type].naval),cell=sim.cell(point.x,point.z);
      if(!grid[cell.z*size+cell.x])return {x:clamp(sim,point.x),z:clamp(sim,point.z)};
      let best=null,score=Infinity;
      for(let r=1;r<=4;r++)for(let z=Math.max(0,cell.z-r);z<=Math.min(size-1,cell.z+r);z++)for(let x=Math.max(0,cell.x-r);x<=Math.min(size-1,cell.x+r);x++){
        if(grid[z*size+x])continue;const wx=x*2-half+1,wz=z*2-half+1,s=Math.hypot(wx-point.x,wz-point.z)+Math.hypot(wx-unit.x,wz-unit.z)*.03;
        if(s<score){score=s;best={x:wx,z:wz};}
      }return best||{x:clamp(sim,point.x),z:clamp(sim,point.z)};
    }

    for(const name of names){const original=sim[name];if(typeof original!=='function')continue;stats[name]={calls:0,milliseconds:0};sim[name]=function(...args){const start=performance.now();try{return original.apply(this,args);}finally{stats[name].calls++;stats[name].milliseconds+=performance.now()-start;}};}

    import {UNITS} from './data.js';
    const clamp=(sim,n)=>Math.max(-sim.halfWorld+3,Math.min(sim.halfWorld-3,n));
    
    // Resolve formation slots on the unit's own movement surface. This keeps edge
    // slots out of foundations and water without sending land troops across a sea.
    export function formationSlot(sim,unit,point){
      const size=sim.gridSize,half=sim.halfWorld,grid=sim.grid(unit.owner,!!UNITS[unit.type].naval),cell=sim.cell(point.x,point.z);
      if(!grid[cell.z*size+cell.x])return {x:clamp(sim,point.x),z:clamp(sim,point.z)};
      let best=null,score=Infinity;
      for(let r=1;r<=4;r++)for(let z=Math.max(0,cell.z-r);z<=Math.min(size-1,cell.z+r);z++)for(let x=Math.max(0,cell.x-r);x<=Math.min(size-1,cell.x+r);x++){
        if(grid[z*size+x])continue;const wx=x*2-half+1,wz=z*2-half+1,s=Math.hypot(wx-point.x,wz-point.z)+Math.hypot(wx-unit.x,wz-unit.z)*.03;
        if(s<score){score=s;best={x:wx,z:wz};}
      }return best||{x:clamp(sim,point.x),z:clamp(sim,point.z)};
    }
    
    export function installTactics(Simulation){
      const p=Simulation.prototype;
      p.patrol=function(ids,x,z,append=false,owner=0){
        if(!Number.isFinite(x)||!Number.isFinite(z))return false;
        const units=ids.map(id=>this.get(id)).filter(e=>e?.owner===owner&&e.kind==='unit'&&!e.embarked&&!['worker','fisher'].includes(UNITS[e.type].role));
        for(const e of units){const target=formationSlot(this,e,{x,z});this.command([e.id],{type:'patrol',...target,originX:e.x,originZ:e.z},append);}
        return units.length>0;
      };
      cancelQueue(buildingId,index,owner=0){const b=this.get(buildingId);if(!b||b.owner!==owner)return;const[q]=b.queue.splice(index,1);if(q){for(const[r,n]of Object.entries(q.cost))this.players[owner].resources[r]+=n;if(q.kind==='age')this.players[owner].agePending=false;}}
      demolish(buildingId,owner=0){const b=this.get(buildingId);if(!b||b.owner!==owner||b.kind!=='building')return false;
        if(b.type==='towncenter'&&this.owned(owner,'building','towncenter').length===1)return this.fail('Your last town center must stand.',owner);
